Stable control layout: menu/sound icons far-left, 'i' info icon next to them, bet -/+ flank the central SPIN button, AUTOPLAY sits below/right of SPIN. The info booklet is a strictly linear 7-page sequence navigable with left/right triangle icons and closable with a green or white 'X', consistent across every page.

Jar identity (Green/Yellow/Pink) is double-coded by both color AND a fixed left-to-right screen position; the 3 buy-bonus offers also carry distinct text labels ('STIKY WILD'/'1X5 WILD'/'2X2 WILD') as a non-color backup. Low-value suit tokens are distinguished by shape (spade/diamond/club/heart) as well as color.
Toggle switches (Settings/Autoplay) use knob position (left=off, right=on) as well as track color; the selected bet tile uses both a distinct yellow fill and dark (vs white) text.

No audio-only information observed; Sound and Music are separate decorative toggles in Settings. All game state (win amounts, spins remaining, multiplier, jar counts) is conveyed via on-screen text/numerals.
Balance/Win/Bet, the bonus-round multiplier and jar counters are all printed as large bright-yellow or white numerals on dark backgrounds, high contrast throughout.

Large circular touch targets throughout; the SPIN button is the largest and most central control. Autoplay (with configurable stop conditions) and Buy Bonus both reduce the number of required manual actions.

Stable control positions across screens: BUY BONUS fixed top-left, wordmark fixed top-right, the 5-button vertical control column fixed on the right edge, BALANCE/WIN/BET always in the same left-center-right order along the bottom bar. The Rules panel is one continuous linear scroll (paytable, then rules, then paylines, then RTP table), not paginated.

The multiplier ladder's active step is marked by explicit 'x<number>' text plus its position at the bottom of the stack; mute state uses an 'x' glyph on the speaker icon; Push Bet on/off is shown by toggle-handle position as well as colour; Free Spins state is reinforced by a full background/lighting change and text counters, not colour alone.
The low-tier purple and blue candy balls are similar in hue and are differentiated mainly by the blue ball's small star marking, not colour - worth close attention for symbol identification by shape.

No audio-only information was observed; all game state (wins, free spins remaining, multiplier value, feature triggers) is conveyed through on-screen text and imagery; sound toggles are purely decorative.
Spin is a large circular target; Autoplay presets run up to 1000 spins, and Quick Play (press-anywhere-to-skip animations) both reduce the number of clicks needed for repeated play.

Control positions are stable: sound/menu top-right of the canvas; wordmark, bonus-buy, autoplay and bet-select icons stacked down the right edge; large Spin button bottom-right; Balance/Total Bet fixed to the bottom corners. Info panels share one bottom navigation row, each a single continuous scroll with no hidden tabs.

Nav arrows are triangle-shaped, close is an X, confirm is a checkmark, toggle state shown by switch position, every multiplier and win amount is a printed number, and Free Spins state is also signalled by a background theme change plus 'FREE SPINS LEFT' text. Residual risk: red heart symbol vs magenta/pink star symbol relies partly on hue, but shape (heart vs star) remains a safe secondary cue.

No information is conveyed by audio alone; AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX are purely decorative toggles in System Settings. All game state (win amounts, free spins remaining, multiplier values, buy-free-spins cost) is shown as on-screen text/numerals.

Key values (win amounts, spin counts, multiplier values, bet/buy cost) are consistently shown as large high-contrast printed numerals on dark plaques or panels (e.g. win-screen total, free-spins-left counter, multiplier reel candies), not conveyed via colour or icon alone.

Large round touch targets for SPIN, menu, sound and info. SPACE and ENTER keys start/stop a spin without the mouse; holding SPACE engages Turbo Spin. Autoplay (adjustable spin count, up to at least 100) minimises repeated clicks.

Control positions are stable across screens: menu (hamburger) and sound stacked far bottom-left, info 'i' button just right of them, bet +/- flank the large central SPIN button, AUTOPLAY sits directly below SPIN. The rules/paytable booklet is a strictly linear 7-page sequence navigated with left/right arrows and closed with a central X, with an explicit 'Page N/7' counter on every page.

Green hexagon gem vs plain green square, and cyan diamond-square vs blue-white swirled oval, are distinguished by shape/facets/texture, not color alone; feature states use text banners (BONUS ACTIVE, FREE SPINS LEFT n) not color cues
BOMB multiplier values and Multiplier Reel values are printed as plain numbers on each tile, legible independent of the rainbow-striped tile colors

No audio-only information; AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX are purely decorative toggles; all game state (wins, spins left, multiplier growth, bonus purchase, RTP/volatility/limits) is conveyed via on-screen text and numbers
Settings/rules panels use a near-black semi-transparent overlay with white heading and white body text for high contrast; CREDIT/BET labels are yellow text on dark background

Large round click targets, central SPIN button largest; SPACE and ENTER keys also start/stop a spin (no click required); Autoplay with configurable spin count and SKIP SCREENS option reduces required interactions

Stable control layout: hamburger-menu+sound bottom-left, info 'i' button beside them, bet -/+ flank the central SPIN button, AUTOPLAY under SPIN; paytable/rules booklet is a strictly linear 7-page sequence shown as 'Page N/7'

4 high symbols differ by shape: Red Star (4-lobe crimson), Orange Donut (amber ring with central hole), Blue Square Jelly (cyan square), Green Star (5-lobe lime). Lobe count and outline distinguish Red Star vs Green Star without relying on color.

4 low symbols differ by shape: Green Jelly Gumdrop (lime teardrop with seed dots), Watermelon Slice (red-green triangle — only triangle in set), Purple Gumball (solid grape sphere), Banana (yellow curved elongated). Shape alone sufficient to distinguish all four.

SCATTER has 'Scatter' text in purple italic on hot pink wrapper. WILD has gold 'W' letter on purple square with gold border. 4 modifier corner types have distinct silhouettes: square frame (Direct Money Award), sphere+bow (Win Multiplier), cannon (Add Wilds), rocket (Big Wild).

All win amounts displayed as dollar text on screen. Feature mode shown as text on left panel (FREE SPINS LEFT / GOLDEN SPINS LEFT). Golden Spins guaranteed modifier type revealed as icon plus text on intro card. Total win shown as dollar text on round summary screen.

HOLD SPACE keyboard shortcut activates turbo spin. Autoplay configurable up to 100 spins. SKIP SCREENS option auto-skips feature intro and end screens. Bonus buy buttons (Free Spins $200, Golden Spins $500) always accessible from on-screen left panel.

Bottom bar labels CREDIT, BET, WIN, FREE SPINS LEFT as text. Win events show '[N]X [symbol] PAYS $[amount]' annotation on grid. Direct Money Award corner displays dollar value as text. Total win screen shows dollar amount and spin count as labeled text.

WILD tile identified by a gold crown icon and 'WILD' text, not color alone; jars/meters carry text labels (WILD/FREE SPINS/JACK POT, MINI/MINOR/MAJOR/MAXI/GRAND) alongside their candy colors; jackpot progress uses filled-vs-empty pip icons; the buy/cancel dialog uses checkmark-vs-X icon shapes in addition to green/red.

No audio-only information observed; all game state (win amounts, free spins remaining, jackpot names/amounts, modifier names, RTP/bet/volatility figures) is conveyed as on-screen text; Ambient Music and Sound FX are togglable and decorative.

Free Spins feature state is signalled by a dramatic background/lighting shift (dark purple/magenta with white light rays) versus the pastel base-game scene, not by color alone; win/credit/bet amounts are shown in large high-contrast white/yellow text.

Large round click/touch targets; the central SPIN button is the largest single control; SPACE/ENTER also start/stop the spin; Autoplay with an adjustable spin count and a Skip Screens toggle reduces the number of required interactions for extended play.

Stable control layout across all game states: menu/sound/info bottom-left, bet +/- flanking the central spin button, autoplay adjacent to spin; the info booklet is a fixed linear 9-page sequence with identical arrow/X navigation chrome and a 'Page n/9' indicator on every page.

Jelly-candy symbols that share a payout tier are told apart mainly by their jelly color, not by outline: Star=gold/amber, Green square jelly=teal-turquoise green; Purple shell=magenta/purple, Green crescent=lime-green; Letter A=crimson-red, Letter K=amber/gold, Letter Q=magenta/pink, Letter J=lime-green, Number 10=orange.

Wild (red-and-white striped peppermint) also carries the printed word 'WILD!' baked into the art; the Scatter/Bonus badge has a teal ring and the printed word 'BONUS', so both remain identifiable without relying on color.

No feature requires sound: wins, the Free-Spins trigger (CONGRATS pop-up) and the Free Spins N/10 counter are all shown as on-screen text/numbers; Music and Sound FX can be muted independently via Settings.

Reel background is dark purple/near-black behind glossy bright symbols for strong contrast. Base game uses a pale blue-sky pastel candy-land scene; Free Spins switches to a deep navy night sky filled with stars, giving a clearly different backdrop per mode.

Core actions are single clicks on large, well-separated circular buttons (Spin, Autoplay, Info, Settings) plus a clickable bet-amount dropdown list; Spacebar can be used instead of clicking the Spin button.

Symbol identity is distinguishable by shape/silhouette (letters, gem/star, bear, heart, lollipop, pumpkin) independent of color, and every symbol's payout is printed in adjacent plain text, not conveyed by color alone. Checkbox/toggle states in Settings and Autoplay use a checkmark glyph (present/absent), not color. The free-spins state is conveyed redundantly by a large text ring reading 'FREE SPINS' plus a spins-remaining counter, not by the background color shift alone.

No information is conveyed by audio alone. Settings exposes independent Music and Sound FX toggles, and all game-state information (wins, spins remaining, bet, balance, feature trigger, RTP) is presented as on-screen text/graphics.

Spacebar can trigger spin as an alternative to clicking (enabled by default in Settings). Autoplay offers fixed round counts (10 up to 1000) or unlimited, reducing the number of required manual actions. Bet is adjustable via small step arrows or via a single click into the full preset-value ladder.

Control layout is stable across screens: info(i)+settings(gear) bottom-left, balance/bet readouts center-left, autoplay(A)+spin bottom-right. Paytable and rules are both reached via the same 3-icon left rail inside the info panel (money-bag=paytable, clock=round-history [non-functional in this demo build], question-mark=rules) and are linear scrollable documents rather than paginated click-through screens.

Win amounts, spin counters, feature names ('Free Spins', 'Sticky Wild') and the active payline label ('Line N pays') are always printed as text, not conveyed by colour alone. Paytable line diagrams use highlighted-vs-empty cell fill (magenta fill vs grey) rather than distinguishing colours between different lines. Settings/Autoplay toggle state is shown by a check-mark glyph, not colour.

Regular symbols are distinguished mainly by shape/printed glyph, not colour: royal letters A (red), K (gold/orange), Q (magenta/purple), J (green) and 10 (orange) each carry a distinct printed letter/numeral; candy symbols (red candy, orange gummy bear, gold star, orange jelly, purple shell, green crescent) each have a distinct silhouette.
No information is conveyed by audio only; Music and Sound FX are decorative toggles in Settings. All win, feature-trigger and spin-counter information is presented as on-screen text/numerals.

Win amounts are shown as large gold numerals with a radiating glow against the reel background; the paytable/rules panel uses white/light-grey body text on a near-black background for high contrast versus the pink in-game screens.

Bet adjustment uses small up/down triangle arrows next to the Total bet field, plus a full scrollable dropdown ladder (0.20-100.00) as an alternative to repeated stepping. Spacebar can substitute for clicking Spin (toggle in Settings). Autoplay offers five configurable auto-stop conditions (any win, bonus won, single win exceeds, balance increases/decreases by) to reduce required manual actions.

Bottom-bar control positions are stable across all observed screens: Information (i) and Settings (gear) sit together on the left of the bet display, Autoplay (A) and Spin sit together on the right. The paytable/rules booklet is a single long scrolling document per tab (Payments/History/Help), not a paginated click-through -- both scroll position and tab selection are needed to describe location.

The 7 paying symbols differ by both color and shape (star/heart/flower/gummy-cluster/triangle-drop/oval/jellybean), so cluster identification does not depend on color; the BONUS scatter is further distinguished by its own printed wordmark and swirl pattern.

The multiplier underlay's pale-pink/blue tint overlay is the one color-only cue in the game, but it is always paired with a legible printed 'X<n>' numeral, so the multiplier value remains readable without color perception.
The volatility badge combines the word 'LOW' with a distinct wave-shaped icon rather than relying on the usual color-coded bolt scale.

BUY FEATURE (orange/rainbow) and SPECIAL BETS (purple/pink) buttons are distinguished by printed text labels and different background patterns in addition to color; the three price tiers inside each dialog are also ranked by a printed star-icon count (1/2/3 stars), not by color alone.

Settings and autoplay toggle switches show their on/off state via both knob position and track color, plus a white checkmark glyph on checked checkboxes, so state is readable without color perception.

No information is conveyed by audio only; AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX are purely decorative toggles. All game state (win amounts, free spins remaining, multiplier value, bet, credit) is presented as on-screen text/numerals.

All primary actions use large circular or rounded-rectangle touch targets; the central SPIN button is the single largest target on screen. SPACE and ENTER are keyboard alternates to clicking SPIN, and holding SPACE engages turbo spin; AUTOPLAY with a configurable spin count further reduces required interactions.

Control layout is stable across screens: menu/info/sound icon cluster always bottom-left, bet -/+ always flank the central circular SPIN button bottom-right, AUTOPLAY sits just under SPIN. The 8-page info booklet is a strictly linear sequence with 3 fixed navigation icons plus an explicit 'Page N/8' readout.

Most functional info duplicated by shape/text/position rather than color alone: paytable nav arrows are triangle-shaped, toggle switches show state by handle position as well as track color, win/spin-count values are printed as high-contrast numerals on ribbons, WILD multiplier shown as explicit 'xN' text badge. Residual color-dependent cues: the four high-value candy symbols differ by shape (ball/dome/cube/teardrop) and the four royals by letter glyph (A/K/Q/J), each also carrying a distinct color (purple/red/green/blue candies; pink A, orange-gold K, purple Q, green-blue J letters).

No information is conveyed by audio alone; AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX are separately toggleable and decorative. All game state (wins, free spins count, multiplier value, purchase cost) is conveyed via on-screen text/numerals.

Win amounts and free-spins counts are shown as large high-contrast gold numerals on red ribbon banners, legible independent of color vision; the WILD's multiplier is shown as an explicit large 'xN' text badge stamped on the symbol rather than only a color cue.

The five Grouped-Pays symbols are shape-coded as well as color-coded (heart, hexagon, 5-point star, cube/diamond, rounded triangle), so confusing colors does not change identification; Wild and Scatter are further distinguished by being spelled-out text-logo wordmarks rather than pictured objects. The five Boost progress badges use icon color to show which symbol is being counted, with no separate text label on the badge itself, so color-blind players must also learn the badge-to-symbol shape mapping.

No information is conveyed by sound alone: Sound-Ambient and Sound-Effects are independently toggleable in Settings, and every game-state change (Feature Triggered, win amounts, Free Games played count, Boost thresholds reached) is shown as on-screen text or graphics as well as sound.

The space bar spins and stops the reels per the Help screen, giving a full keyboard-only path to play; SPIN and the info button hold fixed positions on every screen. GRAND/MAJOR/MINOR tier panels in right sidebar are distinguished by text label AND color: GRAND (red background, red text), MAJOR (dark purple background, magenta text), MINOR (dark green background, green text). Text labels are primary identifiers — no color-only encoding.

Individual candies mainly distinguish their regular and golden colourway by hue/gloss on an otherwise identical silhouette (e.g. purple/lavender vs metallic-gold donut); colour-blind players may find this specific distinction less reliable than shape identification of the candy itself.

Jackpot bars MINI (dark green), MINOR (dark blue), MAJOR (magenta) and GRAND (dark red) are named in text, not only by colour. Bar order left to right: MINI, MAJOR, GRAND, MINOR.

In the respin grid four zones (blue, purple, green, red tiles with faint dark ideograms) are told apart only by tint; multiplier badges share the zone colours and carry printed numbers, but matching a badge to its zone relies on colour.
Settings toggles show state by knob position (left off, right on) as well as colour (grey versus green). Autoplay checkboxes show checked state with a white tick on green.
Royals A, K, Q, J, 10 are red, purple, gold, blue and green letters with gems; the letters themselves identify them. Volatility is written as text HIGH VOLATILITY with a wave icon.
Feature starts show text banners (FULFILLMENT BONUS, QUADRUPLE BONUS) and results show text with amounts (BONUS TOTAL, CONGRATULATIONS, SUPER WIN). Settings have toggles AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX.

Payouts, jackpot values, bets and balance are printed as text in light digits on dark panels. Base game is a bright misty valley; the feature switches to a deep blue night scene (Fulfillment) or a golden sunrise (Quad). Info panels are near-black with white text; the reel field is dark maroon with thin gold dividers.

Wild is a red tile with a large black brush ideogram and no Latin text; Cai Shen sits on a red card with gold border. Win banners: BONUS TOTAL on dark red with gold text, CONGRATULATIONS on a red card with gold frame, SUPER WIN on a bright green banner.

SPACE and ENTER start and stop the spin; holding SPACE gives turbo spin. Autoplay with SKIP SCREENS reduces taps, and feature banners say PRESS ANYWHERE TO CONTINUE. Spin speed button cycles normal, quick, turbo.
Buy dialogs need a deliberate tap on the green check that appears after about 1.5 s; tapping the card body cancels. Each respin in CHEST RESPIN needs a manual tap on SPIN unless autoplay is used.
The game is a single canvas; no screen-reader labels were observable. Chest names, jackpot tiers, bets, balance and results exist only as drawn text.

A failed lane is not shown by red color alone: the lane pill turns solid red, a dark red blood-splatter graphic appears on the road beneath it, and both the CASHOUT and GO! buttons grey out and become flat/disabled at the same time.

A successfully crossed lane is a solid filled pill versus an outlined/empty pill for uncrossed lanes; the next attemptable lane is marked by a glowing ring outline in addition to being colored blue, so state is readable by shape, not color alone.

The selected risk level (EASY/MEDIUM/HARD/DARE DEVIL) is marked by a bright orange outline/highlight ring around one of four dial icons, and the level name is also printed as text ('RISK: EASY'), so selection does not rely on color alone.

Settings toggle switches (Battery Saver, Ambient Music, Sound FX) show state by knob position (left=off, right=on) as well as track color (grey=off, green=on); autoplay checkboxes (Reset Bet / Increase Bet, Turbo Spin, Quick Spin) show a white checkmark glyph inside the box in addition to green fill.

All key round outcomes are conveyed visually as well as audibly: a successful crossing shows the chicken moving and the lane pill turning solid orange with an updated CURRENT WIN text; a failed crossing shows the lane pill turning red plus a blood-splatter graphic and both action buttons greying out; a cash-out changes the bottom text from CURRENT WIN to WIN and updates the CREDIT total. No essential game-state information is conveyed by sound alone.

Every lane shows a printed numeric multiplier label underneath it (e.g. '1x', '1.09x', '24x') in addition to the pill's fill color, so the payout value can be read as text rather than inferred from color or position alone.
The current win amount is shown as large centered gold/white text at the bottom of the screen, changing from 'CURRENT WIN $X.XX' during a round to 'WIN $X.XX' after a successful cash-out.

Round progression needs only two fixed-position decision buttons per lane (GO! to continue, CASHOUT to collect), always in the same screen location. SPACE and ENTER keys are a keyboard alternative to mouse clicks for starting a round and advancing to the next lane.

Autoplay supports configurable NUMBER OF BETS, NUMBER OF STEPS, STOP ON LOSS and STOP ON PROFIT, and a SET CUSTOM PATH option to pre-select lanes, allowing extended play with minimal repeated manual input.

Suggested reading order: game title, current risk level and lane-ladder state (which lane the chicken occupies, its multiplier, whether the next lane is available), CASHOUT button state (enabled/disabled plus current win amount if any), GO!/START! button, bet amount and +/- controls, CREDIT balance, then menu/settings/sound/info icons and AUTOPLAY.

A winning match is never conveyed by color alone: marked simultaneously by a gold glowing border around only the 3 matched cards, identical icon artwork repeated in exactly those 3 positions, and an explicit 'YOU WIN! $<amount>' text toast plus the numeric 'LAST WIN' readout.

The 5 base tiers (single banana / banana pair / bucket / banana bunch / large bunch) are distinguished by silhouette and shape and by an explicit printed dollar figure under each icon, not by hue — all share the same yellow/orange/brown palette family.

The 3 jackpot tiers (MINI/MAJOR/MEGA) additionally carry an explicit gold text banner naming the tier baked into the icon art, legible even without distinguishing the tiers by card-background glow intensity.

The PLAY/GO button changes its text label (triangle glyph vs 'GO') and the status line above it changes text content between states, giving a redundant textual cue instead of relying on a color/icon swap alone.

Toggle switches in the burger menu (Sound/Music/Space-to-spin) use both position (left=off, right=on) and a stronger fill color (grey vs green) — position redundancy covers red-green color-vision differences.

The three chicken-family high symbols (red rooster / pink bird / white chicken) are partly distinguished by card-frame color (red / purple / green) but also differ in bird artwork, head shape and paytable position, so color alone is not the only cue; frame color in isolation would not be reliable for a color-blind user comparing two similar birds at a glance. HELD vs HOLD reel states are distinguished by WORD TEXT on an identically colored blue-and-gold banner, not by color. Toggle switches (settings) are distinguished by handle position (left=off/right=on), not only by green-vs-grey track color.

No audio-only information was found — AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX are purely decorative toggles. All game state (win amounts, line numbers, HELD/HOLD status, bonus prize values, autospins remaining) is conveyed via on-screen text/graphics, not sound alone.

CREDIT, BET, WIN amounts and the 'Page N/6' rules position indicator are shown as large high-contrast gold/white text on a dark wood background. Winning symbols on the reels are additionally outlined with a bright highlight box as a redundant non-text cue alongside the 'LINE N PAYS $X' text.

The Spin and Hold decision window (choosing which reels to hold before the respin) is fixed at 10 seconds, not extendable, and has no visible countdown/timer graphic anywhere on screen (verified by inspecting the hold-decision frame). A player needing more time to click/tap a reel has no way to pause the window or see how much time remains before the auto-respin locks in the suggested holds — a genuine interaction-timing barrier.

Control layout is stable across screens: a 3-icon stack (menu/sound/info) bottom-left, CREDIT/BET labels center-left, bet -/+ flanking the central SPIN button, AUTOPLAY below SPIN. Rules/paytable content is a strictly linear 6-page sequence with previous/next/close controls and an explicit 'Page N/6' textual position indicator on every page.
The four jackpot tiers differ by BOTH color AND a printed tier name (MINI/MINOR/MAJOR/GRAND) in every occurrence, so color-blind users can rely on the text alone.
Chicken Coin vs Super Chicken Coin use TWO non-color cues in addition to color: comb shape (normal jagged vs red heart-shaped) and ring color (plain gold vs red outer ring).
Buy Bonus tier volatility uses a flame-count icon (shape/count based) rather than color alone, though the tier panels also use color/glow intensity (purple vs red/orange glow) as a secondary cue.

Music and Sound are independently toggleable from a small settings popup; all game state (win amounts, jackpot values, spins remaining, feature triggers) is conveyed via on-screen text and numbers, no audio-only information observed.
The Bonus Game's spin-remaining indicator uses lit (green) vs unlit (dark grey) dot state below the grid, not hue alone; unfilled grid cells show a tiled 'iNOUT' watermark rather than being blank.

The spin button is the single largest interactive target. An optional '«Space» to spin & go' toggle (burger menu) lets the Space bar trigger a spin. Autoplay reduces required clicks but offers no configurable stop conditions (no loss-limit/win-limit/spin-count selector was found).

Control positions are stable across all base-game states (gear/settings bottom-left, hamburger menu top-right, BUY BONUS fixed left of the reels, bet/spin/autoplay controls bottom-right). The paytable/rules booklet is a single continuous scroll of 6 pages rather than a paged carousel.

The active difficulty button and the CASH OUT vs GO!/PLAY buttons are distinguished by fill color (yellow = active/primary, dark red = inactive/secondary) but always also carry distinct text (Easy/Medium/Hard/Hardcore; PLAY/GO!/CASH OUT <amount>), so color is never the only cue.
A lost round is signalled by the chicken sprite disappearing and feather particles appearing, not by color alone; the CASH OUT and GO! buttons are additionally dimmed/desaturated.

No gameplay-critical information is conveyed by sound alone. Sound/Music toggles are independent of the Spacebar-to-spin and Welcome-Screen toggles, and every button action has an on-screen text or icon equivalent.
Settings toggles (Spacebar to spin, Welcome Screen) use a yellow-filled-track with the knob on the right for ON; knob left/right position is a redundant non-color cue.
A keyboard alternative exists for the core PLAY action via the 'Spacebar to spin' toggle in Game Settings (default ON), reducing reliance on precise mouse clicks for the primary repeated action.

No game-state info relies on color alone: symbols are disambiguated by silhouette (fruit vs card-suit vs nut vs mushroom vs chest); toggles use knob position; confirm/cancel use checkmark/X; nav arrows use triangle direction; volatility pairs a bolt icon with a text label.

Cyan spade vs crimson heart, and violet blueberry vs magenta mushroom, rely most on hue, but each keeps a unique silhouette (card-suit vs sphere vs cap-and-stem) that stays distinguishable in grayscale.

All feature triggers, win amounts and round outcomes appear as on-screen text/banners (CONGRATULATIONS banners, WIN labels, FREE SPINS LEFT counters), not conveyed by audio alone; SOUND FX and AMBIENT MUSIC can be independently toggled off.
CREDIT/BET/WIN labels are gold text on a dark translucent bar, high contrast; all rule and payout text is rendered as high-contrast on-screen text, not embedded only in low-contrast art.

SPACE/ENTER keys start and stop the spin as an alternative to mouse clicks; Autoplay (up to 100 spins in the captured menu) and Turbo/Quick Spin reduce required interactions; the bet menu's BET MAX button reaches the ceiling without repeated +/- presses.

All monetary values, feature names and rules appear as on-screen text in the GAME RULES booklet, viable for OCR/screen-reading; grid symbols are icon-only with no text labels, so live-play symbol identification would need alt-text support.
CASH OUT (gold/amber gradient) and GO! (bright green gradient) sit side by side during every live round; the distinction is duplicated by different button text, not colour alone.

The next/active multiplier ball is opaque white with bold black text; remaining future balls are pale and translucent with faint outline text -- a brightness-based distinction that does not rely on red-green or blue-yellow discrimination.

A lost round produces no dedicated loss screen, banner, colour flash, or described sound cue -- the field silently resets to idle and only a small balance decrease in the header indicates the round ended in a loss.

The selected difficulty tab (EASY/MEDIUM/HARD/MAD) is marked by a subtle lighter-grey pill-shaped background while its label text is rendered DIMMER grey than the three unselected tabs, which show bold white text -- selection is not signalled by brighter text as commonly expected.

The current cash-out value is shown as text in two places at once during a live round -- a red-text tag beneath the chicken and the numeric label on the gold CASH OUT button -- so it does not depend on a single small readout.
Every action (choose difficulty, adjust bet with +/- steppers, START, GO!, CASH OUT) is a single discrete click on a generously sized button; no drag, hold, or timed/reflex input is required.

The entire interface is rendered on a canvas with no DOM controls or ARIA text found by the scene probe, so assistive screen-reader technology cannot natively read the balance, ladder values, or button labels.

The current/secured multiplier badge (white pill, bold red text, red coin-pouch icon) versus future/unclaimed badges (dark navy pill, white text, no icon) is distinguished by three simultaneous cues - fill colour, text colour and icon presence - not colour alone, which is a colourblind-safe pattern.

The orange CASH OUT button next to the green GO button uses a red-green-adjacent hue pair that could be hard to tell apart for red-green colourblind users; both buttons are also distinguished by different printed text and different horizontal position, giving a working non-colour fallback.

No sound cue announces a loss (or a win beyond the visible text banner); round outcome relies entirely on visual signals, so a player who cannot see the screen and only hears audio gets no cue at all when a round ends.

Active vs inactive difficulty tabs are distinguished mainly by brightness of two similar blue hues (bright mid-blue active vs darker desaturated blue inactive) plus text weight; contrast between the two states is moderate and no icon or check mark reinforces which tab is selected.

Bet amount +/- buttons signal their disabled state (at the $0.1 floor or $100 ceiling) only by fading to a paler, lower-contrast version of themselves; there is no lock icon, strikethrough or text change to reinforce it.

All core actions (START, GO, CASH OUT, bet +/-, difficulty tabs) are single, well-separated large click targets; no drag, double-tap or timed-reflex input is required, and Cash Out can be pressed at leisure with no countdown observed, which is favourable for motor-impaired players.

A win shows a readable text banner ('YOU WIN! $X.XX'), but a loss has no text, banner, icon-with-label or announced state at all: the only signals are the balance silently decreasing, the ladder desaturating to grey, small driftwood debris appearing, and the die freezing on its final face. Without the balance exposed as a live region, a screen-reader user gets no equivalent of a loss.

The dice roll result is shown only as a picture (idle rotating cube vs. a settled single face with 1 to 6 pips), with no accompanying text such as 'You rolled a 5' — blind or screen-reader users cannot obtain the roll result from the current UI.

The two action buttons differ by colour only in the base state: CASH OUT is amber/yellow, GO is bright green, and they sit side by side at the bottom right. They are distinguishable by their text labels and by position (CASH OUT is always the left of the pair), so colour is not the only channel.

The win banner is a green rounded panel with a yellow 'WIN!' pill and the amount in white; the same information is carried by the word WIN and by the balance counter in the header, not by colour alone.

Multiplier values are printed in large light-grey text on dark-grey manhole tiles set against a mid-grey road, which is a low-contrast combination. The multiplier already reached by the chicken is shown separately in white on a blue plate directly under the character, at higher contrast.

The round advances one lane per click of GO, with no time limit on the decision, so the game does not require fast or repeated input. A setting called '«Space» to spin & go' in the menu maps the same action to the keyboard for players who prefer not to use a pointer.

The interface is rendered as ordinary DOM text rather than only on a canvas, so button labels, the balance, the bet field and the rules modals are exposed as readable text. The road, the chicken and the multiplier tiles themselves are graphical and carry no text alternative.
Progress is carried by the multiplier printed on each manhole and by the chicken's position on the road, never by colour alone. The difficulty and the bet are shown as text in the bottom bar.

A flat cartoon road seen from directly above in bright daylight: grey asphalt with white lane dashes, a white chicken on the left, dark manhole discs carrying pale multiplier text, and colourful trucks crossing. The action button is a large green circle.
One click per step and one to collect, with no timing window and no holding. There is no autoplay, so a long run has to be clicked out by hand.
The game is drawn on a canvas, so the road, the manholes and the multipliers are not exposed as text; only the surrounding menu is real markup.

A crossed lane differs from an active one by SHAPE, not only colour - its multiplier bubble is replaced by a gold coin marker. The cash-out and step buttons carry distinct text as well as distinct colours, and a collision is shown by a large flame silhouette plus the cash-out figure dropping to a literal 0.
The one place that leans on colour alone is the set of toggles in the menu (sound, music, space to go), whose on and off states differ by tint rather than by a mark.
Each lane prints its multiplier inside its bubble and the pending payout is printed on the cash-out button, so the state of a round can be read from a still screen.
The round is turn-based rather than timed: it waits for a step or a cash-out. The 'space to go' toggle allows advancing with a key instead of a precise tap.
The control bar is real DOM with named elements, but the road, the chicken and the bubbles are drawn on canvas, so progress is not exposed as text.

In base-game play a cleared lane differs from an uncleared one by shape and icon as well as colour, so progress does not depend on hue. During the free-spins sequence the distinction leans more on colour alone - a green versus a purple oval of the same shape - and the chicken's position on the road is the reliable fallback cue.
Sound is a toggle in the burger menu, and every outcome is printed on screen, so no result is carried by audio alone.
Every lane prints its multiplier on the manhole itself, and the running total is shown in a dedicated banner, so the state of a round can be read from a still screen.
The base game is turn-based rather than timed: the round waits for a step or a cash-out. The purchased bonus plays itself and needs no input at all.
The control bar is real DOM with named elements, but the road, the chicken and the manholes are drawn on canvas, so the round's progress is not exposed as text.
Lane coins are told apart by the printed multiplier number, not by colour: upcoming coins are bronze brown with a number, passed coins are golden yellow with a dollar sign.
The round button is bright green but also carries an arrow icon in idle state and the text GO during a round; CASHOUT is a golden yellow button with a text label and the amount.

Win and loss are told apart by the WIN! text on a green panel, the balance change and the pose of the chicken knocked flat with X marks, not by colour alone. The difficulty level is always named in text (EASY, MEDIUM, HARD, HARDCORE).
Menu toggles differ by knob position (left = off, right = on) as well as by colour (green = on, grey = off).
Sound and Music can be switched off in the burger menu. As far as the frames show, no information is carried by sound alone; audio was not captured, so this is not confirmed.

A car parked over a coin hides that coin's multiplier, so the next multiplier can be invisible on some frames. Bar text is white or light grey on a very dark charcoal bar; modal panels are near-black with white headings.

The chicken can be stepped with the Space key when the menu toggle is on (on by default on the captured frame); otherwise the round button GO must be pressed. CASHOUT is a single large button. Bet and difficulty can be changed only between rounds.
All controls carry plain English text labels (BALANCE, BET, DIFFICULTY, CASHOUT, GO); the scene itself is a canvas. The outcome of a step is shown only by animation and the balance change.

The three plate/marker states are each carried by a different shape and pictogram, not colour alone: upcoming = blue/azure bauble printed with the multiplier number; cleared = solid gold/orange bauble with a white dollar-sign glyph; lost = solid red bauble with a white fin pictogram; Easy's final (30th) plate additionally uses a unique turquoise egg shape instead of a round bauble.
The active difficulty in the selector row is shown with a filled/lighter pill background plus bold white text versus dim grey text for the other three -- not colour hue alone.

Sound and Music are independent toggles in the burger menu; no gameplay-critical information (the dorsal-fin danger warning, the plate-state markers) is conveyed by audio alone -- all of it is visual.
Multiplier and dollar values are rendered as large, high-contrast white bold numerals on solid-colour bauble backgrounds; modal panel text is white/light-grey on a near-black background throughout.

Core interaction is two large buttons (CASH OUT / GO) plus a difficulty row and a bet stepper -- no fine-motor drag or timed-precision input is required; a 'Space to spin & go' keyboard toggle exists as an alternative to clicking GO.
A crossed lane is marked by an ADDED object - a stack of tyres appears beside it - rather than by a colour change, so progress is legible without distinguishing hues.
No lane carries a danger indicator before the strike, so nothing is lost by a player who cannot read a colour cue: there is none to read.
Sound is a toggle in the burger menu and every outcome is printed on screen, so nothing is carried by audio alone.
Each lane prints its multiplier on a lit board at a fixed height, and the pending payout replaces the start button's label, so the round's state can be read from a still screen.
The round is turn-based rather than timed - it waits for a step or a cash-out.

Win and loss are not told by colour alone: a loss shows the knocked-down chicken, a grey CASHOUT button with a dash and an x0 row in the bet history; a win shows the yellow WIN! label with the amount in text.
The active CASHOUT button is yellow with black text and a number, the inactive one is grey with a dash, so the state is also readable from the printed number.
The round button is emerald green and changes from a white triangle (Play) to the white word GO during a round, so the state is carried by shape and text as well as colour.
The next multiplier tile is told from later ones only by brightness (bright against dimmed), but the number inside every tile stays readable in both states.
The bet history marks each row with a green shield icon; reading the numbers needs no red and green pairing.
Sound and Music toggles are in the burger menu; no on-screen cue is described as depending on sound alone, and the sound content itself was not observable from frames.
Captions BALANCE, BET and DIFFICULTY are small light-grey text on a near-black bottom panel; multiplier labels are large and bold with dark outlines.
A round needs single clicks only (Play, GO, CASHOUT). The Space key replaces the mouse for Play and GO when the menu toggle is on. There is no timed input and cash-out is not time-limited.
GO! (green) and CASH OUT (yellow/orange) buttons are distinguished by their text labels and, on CASH OUT, by a live dollar amount printed below the label, not by color alone.

A passed-safely step marker (gold coin embossed with a white egg icon) differs from a still-open step (grey metallic disc with a diamond-hatch texture and a printed multiplier) in both color and texture/icon, not by color alone.
A loss is shown by the chicken's pose (eyes replaced with grey X marks, ruffled feathers) and a black-and-yellow diagonal hazard stripe, not by a color change alone.
The win banner combines a green fill with a trophy-and-egg icon and the word WIN plus the dollar amount, not color alone.

No dialogue or spoken instructions are used; every round outcome (win, loss, ladder progress) is conveyed via on-screen text and iconography, so the game is fully playable with sound off. Sound and Music are independently toggleable sliders in Settings.
All monetary values and multipliers are printed as high-contrast plain white or black bold numerals directly on their tokens and buttons, never conveyed by color or icon alone.

The selected difficulty tab is a raised, protruding segment whose label text is DIMMED grey, while unselected tabs sit flush with bold WHITE text — the selected tab actually has LOWER text contrast than the unselected ones, a counterintuitive reversal worth noting for low-vision players; selection is still identifiable by the protruding shape.

Round outcome is shown clearly and redundantly: a manual cash-out shows a green 'WIN! $<amount>' banner with a trophy icon, and a loss shows the chicken's dizzy KO pose with X-marked eyes and a hazard skid stripe — the result is always legible on screen, not left ambiguous.

Core interaction is a small number of discrete clicks per round (choose difficulty, adjust bet with +/-, press START, then repeated GO!/CASH OUT clicks); no drag, hold, or precise-timing gesture is required anywhere in the observed flow.

Multiplier values are always printed as numbers on the road markers regardless of their bronze/gold colour, so ladder steps are readable without colour perception. The current-position tag is both a distinct blue shape and located directly under the hen. The final/Grand-Prize tier is shape-distinct (gold disc with an egg icon), not just colour-distinct. CASH OUT vs GO! buttons carry explicit text labels in addition to amber/green colouring. Difficulty-tab selection is shown by brightness/boldness and column position, not hue alone.

No screen captured demonstrates audio-only information; Sound and Music are independent toggles in Settings, both defaulting to on, consistent with audio being decorative/ambient rather than carrying unique gameplay information. This was not directly verified, since no screen isolates an audio-only cue (e.g. a carriage-approach warning sound) from a visual counterpart.

Only two distinct in-round actions are required (step forward / cash out), both large rectangular buttons occupying roughly a third of the screen width each. Bet adjustment uses simple repeatable +/- buttons rather than a drag slider. No autoplay exists, so every step requires a discrete manual press, which could be a burden on long ladders (up to 24 steps on Easy) since there is no way to advance multiple steps at once or set an auto-cashout target.

Stable, consistent control layout across all captured screens: balance top-left, help/sound/settings icon row top-right, difficulty tabs bottom-left, bet-amount adjuster bottom-center, primary action button(s) bottom-right. The Rules booklet is a single scrollable document with a persistent left-hand list of six named jump-targets, mapping well to a heading/landmark structure.
Card ranks are told apart by printed letter or number (10, J, Q, K, A), not only by colour: green 10, blue J, purple Q, orange K, red A.
Wild multipliers differ by the printed number 2X or 3X, not only by shading; the Scatter carries the word SCATTER.

Red fire hydrant, red A and red fire truck share a red hue but differ strongly in shape. Vehicles are told apart by silhouette and signage: light bar on the police car, roof sign on the taxi, ice-cream cone on the van, ladder and hoses on the fire truck.
Free Spins state is signalled by the text FREE SPINS LEFT with a number as well as by the golden-orange reel frame.
Music and Sound toggles exist in the settings popup; win and Free Spins states are shown visually, no sound-only cue was seen.

Wins are announced as text in the bottom bar: WIN with the amount and LINE n PAYS with the amount. Banners are text, but the prompt PRESS ANYWAY TO CONTINUE needs a click. Heavy graffiti texture on symbols and frames may reduce legibility.
Reel frame is hazard-striped yellow-orange and dark navy; panels are dark translucent charcoal with white text; the spin button is bright green with white circular arrows.
Spin by the button or the spacebar; turbo by holding the spin button; autoplay presets 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 50, 75, 100, 500, 750, 1000 and infinity. Banners need a click or tap to continue.
Free Spins counter, win amounts and line wins are shown as on-screen text; no screen-reader labels were verified in the captured frames.
The current/safe column is marked by both a bright green disc color and the chicken's on-screen position on that lily pad, so position duplicates the color cue
Win vs loss is shown by distinct illustrations (coins-and-chicken vs crocodile-and-remains) plus explicit 'YOU WIN!' / 'WIN FUN 0' text, not by color alone
Settings toggle switches show ON/OFF state via the knob's left/right position as well as gold fill color
Sound and Music have independent toggles in Settings; every round outcome (win amount, multiplier, cash-out amount, loss) is shown as on-screen text and imagery, not conveyed by audio alone

All primary controls (PLAY, CASH OUT, GO!, difficulty tabs, bet -/+, 1/2, 2x, MIN, MAX) are large rounded buttons with generous hit areas; a 'Spacebar to spin' toggle (default ON) lets players start rounds without precise pointer clicks

Multiplier chips are blue by default (a darker blue/purple on Hardcore volatility) and turn gold/amber after a Multiplier Boost is collected; every chip, including the golden egg, prints its value in bold white text with a black outline regardless of chip colour, so the multiplier is readable independent of hue.

The Cashout field's active/inactive state is marked by BOTH a colour change (grey to gold) AND a gold border appearing/disappearing (shape-based), not colour alone; it is dim with no border and no value before any step is taken, and gold-outlined with the win amount once a Cashout is available.
Autoplay checkbox state (e.g. 'Steps to cashout') is shown by BOTH fill colour (dark = unchecked, gold/yellow = checked) AND a white checkmark glyph appearing/disappearing, not colour alone.
Settings sliders (Sound FX, Music) convey level by a gold fill versus dark track PLUS the position of a white circular handle, readable without relying on hue discrimination.

The total-bet stepper marks its limits by REMOVING the arrow glyph, not by dimming it: at the 100.00 FUN ceiling the up arrow is absent and at the 0.10 FUN floor the down arrow is absent, so the boundary is readable without judging brightness.
Sound FX and Music are independently adjustable/mutable sliders in Settings; all round outcomes (win amount, loss) are conveyed with on-screen text and numbers as well as animation, not audio alone.

Multiplier values are printed in bold white text with a black outline on every chip colour (blue default, purple/darker-blue on Hardcore, gold when boosted, and the golden egg), keeping high contrast and legibility regardless of chip colour or acuity.

Only two controls are needed to complete a round - Play (advance one step) and Cashout (bank the current win) - both large, isolated HUD targets; Autoplay's 'Steps to cashout' stop condition can fully automate play for users who find repeated per-step clicking difficult.

The HUD is a small, fixed set of labelled fields (Balance, Total bet, Volatility, Cashout, Play) always in the same bottom-of-screen position, plus a stable 3-icon row (turbo, autoplay, cosmetic skin) and a stable top-right menu row (sound, settings, info, history, close); the Cashout field is the single most decision-relevant number each step and is co-located with its own label, distinct from decorative in-lane chip art.

Most state cues are text-and-icon based (checkmarks, filled/unfilled toggle boxes, explicit Low/Medium/Very High volatility text labels, numeric 'Free spins: N/5' counters). Residual color-dependent cue: the BET WAYS diagram uses a green check mark vs. a red X for valid/invalid way shapes, though the check/cross glyph shapes remain distinguishable without color. Card symbols A (pink/magenta), K (orange), Q (teal/cyan), J (green), 10 (orange/tan), 9 (turquoise) are differentiated mainly by color plus distinct hand-lettered glyph shapes as a fallback.

No information is conveyed by audio alone. Settings exposes independent Volume/Music/Sound FX toggles, and all game-state information (wins, free-spins count, multipliers collected, bet, balance) is duplicated in on-screen text.

Bet adjustment uses small up/down triangle steppers requiring many repeated clicks to span the 0.20-50.00 FUN range, rather than a direct-entry field or slider. Spacebar-to-spin (on by default) and Autoplay with configurable stop conditions reduce the number of discrete clicks needed to play extensively.

Bottom-bar control positions are stable across base-game states: Information(i) and Settings(gear) far-left, Balance/Total-bet center-left, Autoplay(A) and Spin far-right. Eight chicken targets differ by four independent cues: label plate colour (grey, green, light sky blue, deep blue, purple, pink, orange, gold), the printed multiplier number on the plate, bird size (clearly larger from x3 upward, largest at x24 and x48) and plumage (x1.1 is pale cream). The number is always printed, so colour is never the only signal. Autoplay target cards repeat the same plate colours and numbers.

Weak spot: x1.1, x1.2 and x1.5 are small birds of similar size and differ mainly by number and plate colour. The light sky blue plate (x1.5) and the deep blue plate (x3) are close in hue and differ by lightness and bird size.

Toggles (Sound, Music, Space) show state by knob position as well as green versus grey fill. Selected autoplay presets and target cards have a green outline (presets also green text). During autoplay the locked BET field is shown by greyed digits and arrows and by a white X replacing the autoplay icon.
No sound-only cues were identified; the round outcome is shown visually (explosion, feathers, coins, popup). Sound and music content was not assessed.

Small multiplier plates on x1.1, x1.2 and x1.5 birds are hard to read at 1280x800; birds fly continuously and overlap, a large bird can hide a small one. Win amount appears as a yellow number in a small translucent plate and in the LAST WIN field (yellow on near-black); a grown target is marked by an orange glow.

Targets move constantly and a manual click needs lead ahead of the bird. The SPIN button picks a random target itself and autoplay needs no aiming, which lowers the aiming demand. Hold-to-turbo needs press-and-hold; the spacebar fires SPIN as an alternative (toggle 'Space' to spin and go, ON by default).
Game is canvas-rendered; wins are announced only visually (popup number, LAST WIN, rolling balance). No text alternative was identified.

Active difficulty is also carried by the zombie's costume silhouette, not colour alone: bare head (Easy), tan/grey pot-shaped helmet (Medium), orange-and-white football helmet with face cage (Hard), full green army fatigues with combat helmet (Hardcore); the difficulty name is also printed as text.

A passed tombstone changes creature silhouette (green humanoid zombie becomes a yellow/orange smiling sunflower with a jack-o'-lantern face) in addition to colour, and its position is always immediately behind the chicken -- three independent, redundant channels for the 'cleared' state.

During a live round, the locked BET and DIFFICULTY fields use greyed-out (desaturated) styling plus removal of the stepper affordance (a shape/behaviour cue), not colour alone; the bet-history win/loss rows are distinguished by text content (a dash vs. a dollar amount) and by the multiplier value (x0 vs. a real multiplier), not by row colour.
The WIN! badge uses a high-contrast yellow/gold pill with bold black text, and the win amount is printed in large bold white text with a dollar-coin icon.
The PLAY/GO action can be bound to the Spacebar via a 'Space to spin & go' toggle in the settings menu, as an alternative to a precise mouse click on the round button.
Jackpot tiers GRANDE/MAJOR/MINI use both color (lime-green/cyan-blue/orange tiles) AND distinct text labels — readable without color perception.
WILD symbol displays the word 'WILD' as text overlay in neon-green on a flame-burst tile — identifiable by text label, not color alone.
Royal symbols (A/K/Q/J) differ in letter form AND color: A=lime-green zigzag, K=cyan-blue faceted, Q=purple circular medallion, J=coral-red lightning texture.
Free Spins mode: background shifts from warm crimson to deep blue/navy night sky — hue difference (red vs blue) detectable under deuteranopia and protanopia.
Money Respin mode: grid cells shift from neutral to dark green with gold-dotted borders on occupied cells — shape/border pattern change, not only color.

Win amounts, which line paid, respins remaining, MONEY values and feature progress toward the 10,000x cap are always shown as on-screen text/numbers, so the game is fully playable with sound off.

During the Nudge Feature, the large animated win-counter overlay is centered directly over the middle row of the grid and physically covers those symbols for the whole reveal animation, so the exact winning combination on intermediate nudges cannot be read from the game's own presentation, only the aggregate running number.

Large, well-separated round/gift-shaped touch targets for all primary actions (Spin, Bet Max, Autoplay, bet +/- steppers). The SPACE bar is a keyboard alternative to clicking Spin/Stop, and Autoplay with optional stop conditions reduces the number of repeated actions needed to play many rounds.

Bottom-bar readouts (BALANCE, BET, BET LEVEL, COIN) are machine-readable text pills, not image-only. The Help screen is a genuine linear HTML document exposable to a screen reader as ordinary text, unlike the canvas-drawn game field itself, which is not exposable this way.
High symbols are told apart by portrait shape (old god, warrior, veiled woman, smiling man, young man), not by card colour alone; payout tiers are printed as numbers.
Switches in SYSTEM SETTINGS show state by knob side (left off, right on) as well as track colour (grey off, green on).

Red CANCEL and green YES buttons in the buy confirmation carry text labels.
Every outcome has a text or visual counterpart: line-win strip, WIN counter, FREE SPINS LEFT counter, COMPLETED label and banners; win amounts are always shown as text.
Autoplay up to the slider value (100 shown) with Turbo Spin, Quick Spin and Skip Screens options; spin by SPACE or ENTER, hold SPACE for turbo spin; no timed inputs seen.

Each of the 9 piggy tiers is triple-encoded, not colour-only: an exact multiplier number printed on every piggy at all times (x96 down to x1.2), a strongly differing relative size of the piggy icon (largest for x96, smallest for x1.2), and in the paytable/rules dialogs an exact printed percentage plus a proportional-length progress bar next to it.

A normal win on tiers x1.2 through x12 shows only a small floating '+$amount' speech-bubble near the tapped piggy, with a handful of coin sprites; the large full-screen 'Mega Win' coin-rain banner with big bold text and a dimmed background is reserved for the top three tiers (x24/x48/x96) only. A low-vision player watching for the big banner alone will miss most wins.

The target is a piggy drifting across the sky; a tap must land on the opaque body pixels, not the transparent wing corners or the sprite's bounding box, so hitting a specific piggy is a genuine moving-target precision task -- even automated capture tooling found direct piggy clicks unreliable. The large (~150px) fixed-position PLAY button in the bottom-right corner is the reliable alternative, favourable for limited-precision pointing, and only one bet is ever in flight at a time so rapid repeated taps cannot queue or double-bet.

Hovering/holding a piggy prints a tooltip 'Win Chance: N% / Hits: M' -- the exact burst probability for that tier and a per-instance tap counter -- information that is exposed only this way and is not otherwise printed on the field. Info-booklet navigation uses green triangle/cross icons distinguished by shape (left triangle = previous page, X = close, right triangle = next page), not colour alone.

Bonus buy dialog: five options coded by unique spatial position (top/left/center/right/bottom), unique color tint per panel (dark/olive/brown/teal/purple), and unique name text — any single dimension sufficient for differentiation without color

All critical game state communicated via on-screen text: GOOD LUCK trigger overlay on trigger spin, CONGRATULATIONS intro screen with numeric respin count, WIN $X.XX in bottom HUD, animated multiplier flyout values during collection sequence, TOTAL WINS running readout throughout feature; separate AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX toggles available in settings overlay

Base game grid columns left to right: PAYER (reel 1, amber panel labeled PAYER vertically, value-assigning special, empty cells show brown cross-hatch texture); four main paying reels (reels 2-5, regular symbols, MONEY coins, SCATTER); COLLECTOR (reel 6, teal steel vault labeled COLLECTOR vertically, pays collected sum)

Sound is a single on/off toggle in the settings popover; no round event is announced by audio alone - the countdown, the multiplier and the crash are all shown on screen.
Bet-limit refusals appear as a small red caption under the bet field ('The rate exceeds the limit of 200'), rendered noticeably smaller than the bet value itself and with no icon.

Manual cash-out is time-critical: the action button must be pressed during a flight that can end in under two seconds. The 'Auto stop' field removes the timing requirement entirely by committing the exit coefficient before the round starts.
Round-history chips are colour-coded by multiplier band, but the number is printed inside every chip, so no information is colour-only.
Sound is decorative and switchable in the settings menu; the round outcome is visible without audio.
Balance, bet amounts, the auto cash-out value and the rules booklet are DOM text and scale with browser zoom; only the flight animation is canvas.

Bet panels are DOM controls with visible labels, and the panel button text states the round state (Place bet / Cancel / Cash out).

Rounds-history chips are colour-coded by multiplier tier (blue below x2.00, green x2.00-9.99, gold above x10.00), but every chip also prints the exact multiplier as text, so the tier is never colour-only.
The 'You Win!' banner is confirmed by the words 'You Win!' plus a goal-net icon and the printed cash amount, not by the green banner colour alone.

No information is conveyed by sound alone: Sound and Music are separate labelled toggle/slider controls in Settings, and every round outcome (win amount, multiplier, balance) is also shown as on-screen text.

The two betting panels are visually identical and distinguished only by left/right screen position; each panel's own Bet Amount, Auto Cash Out value and button state must be read individually since nothing else separates them.

BALANCE/WIN/BET and panel text are real DOM text (not canvas-drawn) and read as exact machine text, a good baseline for screen-reader exposure if the DOM nodes carry accessible names/aria-live regions (not verifiable from screenshots alone).

Bet-panel action buttons pair color with a printed label: green Place Bet, red Cancel or Stop Autoplay, so the button's state is never color-only.

History-ribbon chips color-code round size with an outline (blue for typical results, green from roughly x2 up, orange or magenta on very high values), but the multiplier number is always printed inside the chip, so a color-blind player loses only the at-a-glance severity cue, not the number itself.

All state changes observed (bet accepted, round-start SMASH!, milestone crossings, round-end BOOM!, round result) are shown as on-screen text and graphics, none audio-only. Sound and Music are independently toggleable sliders in Settings, each with its own mute/unmute icon pair.

The live multiplier is always shown as large, high-contrast white-on-blue numeral text (bold red-on-blue with a black outline at the moment of a crash), never color-only, so the growing value is readable without depending on color perception.

Lit-lane state cue is BOTH a color change (teal to bright yellow) AND a position cue (the batsman sprite visibly stands under the current lane) - redundant, so it remains usable without color perception.

The five paying gems are red, blue, purple/violet, teal/turquoise and pink, each on a differently shaped/colored plaque; SCATTER is pale blue-white with a distinctive pearl-ring border unlike the solid-color paying gems; WILD is a gold plaque with green 'WILD' text. One color-only distinction exists (the red '12' in 'IN 12 FREE SPINS' on the win screen) but the surrounding sentence still conveys the same information without relying on color.

No information is conveyed by audio alone; SOUND FX and AMBIENT MUSIC are purely decorative on/off toggles in settings. All game state (multiplier, wins, free spins remaining, ways count, bet/credit) is conveyed through on-screen text and numerals.

Win/credit/bet/multiplier and ways-count values are printed as large bold gold numerals on dark or icy high-contrast backgrounds throughout the base game, free spins and win screens; UI buttons are large round dark circles with bold white line-art glyphs.

Large round click targets throughout; the central SPIN button is the largest single target. SPACE and ENTER keys start/stop the spin as keyboard alternatives to clicking, and holding SPACE engages turbo spin. Autoplay (up to a slider-selected count, observed up to 100) reduces the number of required manual actions.

Control layout is stable across all screens: menu+sound stacked bottom-far-left, info 'i' button just to their right, bet -/+ flanking the central SPIN button, autoplay directly below spin, CREDIT/BET text left-of-center. The rules/paytable booklet is a strictly linear 7-page sequence navigated with left/right arrows and closed via a center X or a top-right X.

Primary risk: all 7 paying symbols are crystals/a nugget distinguished mostly by hue. Usable non-colour cue: high-value symbols are multi-shard CLUSTERS (or the uniquely shaped gold nugget blob), low-value symbols are always a SINGLE solitary shard -- shard count/shape signals value tier independent of colour.

Known weak point: the low-value 'small red-orange single crystal' and the high-value 'red-orange crystal cluster' share the same red-orange hue family; they can only be reliably told apart by counting shards (one shard = low value, a cluster of several = high value), not by colour.

The CLUSTER PAYS validity diagram in the paytable pairs a green checkmark (valid orthogonal adjacency) with a red X (invalid diagonal-only adjacency) -- shape-differentiated, not colour-only. Settings/Autoplay checkbox state is shown by presence/absence of a white checkmark glyph, not colour alone.

No information is conveyed by audio alone; Music and Sound FX are separately toggleable in Settings, and all game-state information (win amounts, free-spins counter, multiplier values, bonus price) is presented as on-screen text/numbers.

Bet adjustment uses small up/down triangle steppers rather than a single +/- pair. Autoplay preset-count buttons (10/25/50/100/250/500/750/1000/unlimited) reduce the number of manual spin clicks needed. Spacebar can be enabled in Settings as an alternate spin trigger.

Bottom-bar control layout is stable across all captured screens: info/settings icons far-left, balance centre-left, bet stepper centre, autoplay and spin buttons right. Paytable and Rules are each a single continuously-scrolling document (not paged with next/prev buttons), opened via the 'i' information button and closed with a top-right 'X'.

Green and gold/orange crystals share almost the same notched-shard silhouette and differ mainly by hue, a risk for red-green color blindness; pink (downward triangle), purple (elongated notched hexagon) and blue (rounded pentagon) have distinct shapes and are easier to tell apart without relying on color.

Winning-combinations table rows are marked by a dot-fill pattern (filled / paired-ring / empty) plus a printed multiplier number, not by color alone, so the achieved combination stays readable without color perception.
No audio-only information observed; Sound and Music are separate toggleable sliders in Settings, and all outcomes (round win, bonus result, balance) are conveyed through on-screen text and numbers.

Bet amount can be set with min/max buttons, incremental +/- buttons, or a typed Amount field, reducing the precision needed for repeated adjustments; autoplay (5-100 rounds) further reduces the number of manual actions required.

Stable screen layout every round: balance top-left, paytable top-left-middle, logo top-center, bonus-spinner indicator top-right, five crystal-result slots mid-screen, bet controls bottom bar. No audio-only information observed; SOUND FX and AMBIENT MUSIC are decorative toggles. All game state (win amounts, free spins left, Total Multiplier, feature triggers) is conveyed through on-screen text/numerals, not sound cues alone.

All primary controls are large circular touch targets; SPIN is the largest button on the base-game screen. The lava-sphere SCATTER's orange-red glow could be confused with the ham or orange by color alone for a red-green color-blind user, but its cracked-sphere silhouette with a flame base makes it unambiguous by shape.

The Color Tumble feature's exploding clusters are defined purely by each reel cell's own BACKGROUND color (observed: green, purple/violet, and a gold/olive tint during Free Spins) matching across 5+ adjacent cells - there is no text label or pattern distinguishing cell background colors, so a colorblind player cannot anticipate which cells will cluster before the game confirms it. Paytable payout values are color-independent in effect: the rough pink crystal and rough green crystal pay identically (5/4/3-of-a-kind), as do the rough purple crystal and rough gold crystal nugget - distinguishing these pairs by color is not required to know the payout tier.

Non-game controls avoid color-only coding: the Ante Bet ON/OFF toggle is marked by both handle position and an arrow-vs-checkmark icon plus the literal word 'ON'/'OFF'; paytable-booklet navigation uses triangle/cross shaped icons, not color alone; the disabled Buy Free Spins plaque under Ante Bet is shown via reduced brightness/desaturation reinforced by rule text, not hue alone.

No information is conveyed by audio alone; SOUND FX and AMBIENT MUSIC are independently toggleable and purely decorative. All game state (wins, spins left, current multiplier, symbols collected toward the meter, feature triggers) is shown as on-screen text and numerals.

All primary controls are large circular touch targets. SPACE and ENTER keys start/stop a spin (keyboard-operable, no mouse required). The Volatility toggle's two states are partly signalled by hue (blue vs gold capsule icon) but backed by a text-weight cue (bold-active vs grey/washed-out inactive) that does not depend on color perception. Free Spins vs Super Free Spins backgrounds differ mainly by a lavender-vs-cream tint, but both always carry an explicit text badge ('BONUS ACTIVE' + price paid, 'Free spins: N/10' counter) independent of color.

No audio-only information observed on any captured frame; win amounts, feature triggers, spins-remaining counters and round totals are all on-screen text/numbers. Music and Sound FX are independently toggleable in Settings; Quick Spin availability is noted as license-dependent.

Stable control layout: info(i)/settings(gear) icons far bottom-left, bet display/steppers center-bottom, autoplay(A)/spin far bottom-right in the base game. The Volatility control is the single most important element to expose to assistive technology: it silently changes six distinct RTP values and locks to a single mode (shown as only ONE word in the badge, with no visible second option) during bonus rounds. Jackpot tier boxes and bonus-pick tiles print their tier name as text, not just a color; toggle switches change thumb position as well as fill color; win and feature amounts are plain numerals; the three booklet-navigation icons are distinguished by triangle-left/cross/triangle-right shapes, not hue. The 15 payline diagrams rely partly on a distinct accent color per line, but each line also carries its own printed number, which remains legible without color discrimination.

No audio-only information was observed; AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX are independently toggleable and purely decorative. All game state (wins, free spins remaining, jackpot amounts, bonus results) is conveyed through on-screen text and graphics.

Large round click targets, SPIN being the largest and most central. SPACE and ENTER keys start/stop spins; holding SPACE engages turbo spin. AUTOPLAY (adjustable spin count plus a SKIP SCREENS option) reduces the number of required interactions for extended play.

Control positions are stable on every base-game/feature screen: menu and sound icons at far bottom-left, 'i' info button next to them, bet +/- flanking the large central SPIN button, AUTOPLAY below/right of SPIN. All three symbols are distinguishable by shape alone independent of color: Diamond = faceted multi-facet geometric gem; Cherry = two round fruit spheres with leaf and forked stem cluster; 7 = single bold numeral digit. AMBIENT and SOUND FX audio toggles are independently controllable in the Settings panel (gear icon). Deaf and hard-of-hearing users have full information access with audio disabled.

Three reveal methods available: (1) SCRATCH! button reveals all 9 cells simultaneously with a single click — primary quick-play method; (2) click individual cells one at a time to reveal each independently; (3) AUTOPLAY sequentially auto-scratches all queued tickets hands-free. STOP button (single click) halts AUTOPLAY at any point. Purchase flow requires one radio button selection and one BUY NOW click. BUY MORE TICKETS is a single button when the ticket queue is empty.

Win amount displayed as text in the bottom bar (labels TOTAL WIN and WIN with dollar amounts, e.g. $2.00). Each revealed cell shows a text prize value beneath the symbol ($100,000, $10,000, FREE PLAY, etc.). Purchase options are labeled with quantity and total price in text.
Symbol identity relies on shape/letter/icon as well as colour: red vs blue diamond symbols differ in outline shape too, and A/K/Q/J differ by letter shape, not only by colour.

Scatter-star tiers (blue/red/gold) are colour-differentiated, but each has a unique printed multiplier next to it in the top bar and paytable, so the payout is always readable as text even if the colour cannot be distinguished.

No information is conveyed by audio alone; sound is limited to three independent toggles (All Sounds/Sound Effects/Music) and wins/state are always shown as on-screen text and numbers as well.

Winning symbols are marked by both a bright magenta connecting line with glowing white end-dots and dimming of all non-participating symbols, plus the per-line win amount shown in large gold 3-D digits — dual non-colour, high-contrast cues.

The large circular Spin button is the primary target; the keyboard space bar is a full alternative for spinning and for skipping intro/win animations (Quick Play), and Autoplay (up to 1000 spins) further reduces repeated input.

Layout is stable across states: logo/scatter-bar top-left/top-center, reel grid centered, speaker+menu icons fixed top-right, autoplay/bet-select/spin icons fixed on the right edge, balance/total-bet fixed at the bottom corners. Royal letters differ by letterform even though colored differently; scatter tiers are labeled with explicit text (3 Blue/Red/Gold Scatters award xN); selected list items use a white-fill/black-text swap rather than a color change; the winning payline is marked by both a highlighted number badge and a printed win amount, not color alone.

No audio-only information observed on any captured screen; all game state (balance, bet, win amount, scatter payouts, RTP) is conveyed as on-screen text. Sound toggles (All Sounds/Sound Effects/Music) are purely decorative with no gameplay-critical audio cues.

Large circular SPIN button is the biggest interactive target; autoplay offers 8 preset spin counts (up to 1000) to reduce manual actions; bet and autoplay selection use tall list rows rather than fine sliders.

Scatter tiers are named in words (Blue/Red/Gold Scatters) alongside star color; payline identity relies on printed numerals 1-5, not color; win highlighting combines a bright line overlay with a floating gold number; toggle/selection state uses icon-glyph change or solid-fill contrast, not color alone; the four royal letters A/K/Q/J are identified primarily by their own printed letterform.

No audio-only information observed; all game state (wins, bet, balance, RTP, rules) is conveyed as on-screen text. The Enable Sounds prompt can be answered YES or NO with no consequence to comprehension.

Primary controls (Spin, Autoplay, Bet Select) are large circular touch targets; Spin is also keyboard-operable via the space bar, and autoplay round counts from 10 up to 1000 reduce the number of required interactions for extended play.

Large primary PLAY/STOP button; SPACE key also triggers a spin ('PRESS SPACE TO SPIN' hint in settings); autoplay (default observed 10 spins) reduces the number of clicks needed for repeated play

Every plain die differs by BOTH pip colour AND pip count/pattern (1 through 6 pips), so all 8 regular symbols remain distinguishable without relying on pip colour alone.

Special symbols (Wild, Scatter 1, Scatter 2) are distinguished by explicit icon shape (die-with-WILD-text, faceted blue crystal, round purple/magenta gem) and by accompanying text labels naming each symbol in the paytable, not colour alone.

Reskin selector labels the three colour schemes with explicit text ('RED'/'WHITE'/'BLACK'), not colour-only.

No audio-only information was observed on any captured frame; all game state (balance, bet, wins, feature triggers, gamble outcomes) is conveyed through on-screen text and numerals. Sound is purely decorative and can be muted (Music/Sound FX toggles in Settings).

UI controls are white icon glyphs on dark circles/pills (shape-based, high contrast); bet stepper uses distinct up/down triangle shapes rather than colour; checkbox state in Settings is shown with a visible check-mark glyph, not colour alone.

Under (teal-green) and Over (purple) sides are distinguished by more than color: the Roll buttons are labelled 'Under <N>'/'Over <N>' in text, and the two 'Bet Details' cards keep a fixed top(Under)/bottom(Over) order with numeric Win Chance/Payout/Multiplier values, so a side is identifiable without perceiving color. Header controls (back, balance, sound, settings), the two Bet Details cards, and the two Roll buttons keep the same fixed screen positions at all times; all key numbers (Win Chance, Payout, Multiplier, Balance, bet limits, RTP figures, version numbers) render as plain on-screen text rather than as images, which favors text-based access -- verified visually from screenshots only, not with an actual screen reader.
The four card-suit low symbols (spade/heart/club/diamond) are distinguished primarily by shape, color is a secondary cue only — safe for all forms of color blindness.

Paytable values are printed numbers and symbols differ by silhouette and object type (burger, bucket, tray, cup, glass, wing), not by hue alone.
Winning symbols sit on hot-pink tiles with thin connector lines; in respin features inactive symbols turn dark grey silhouettes, so state is carried by brightness as well as tile color.

No captions for sound cues are visible; features and wins are announced visually by banners (One more Scatter, Total Win, big win number). Sound can be toggled in the player menu.

Paytable and Rules panels: white titles and light-grey body text on dark slate grey, payout numbers in pink; the bonus stage turns hot pink and magenta with a yellow-gold outline, mystery respin screens cyan-blue.
Spin by tap or the Space key on PC, hold Space for continuous spins, tap during a spin to stop the reels; Auto Spin of 10, 30, 50, 80 or 1000 spins; no timed inputs seen.

Paytable and Rules panels are real DOM text and readable by a screen reader; the reels, ways banner, unlock counter, bonus-spin icons and Total Win are drawn on a canvas with no visible text alternative.
