Card symbols A/K/Q/J/10/9 are color-coded by candy-cane stripe hue but are always paired with a distinct printed letter/number glyph, so identity is never color-dependent for this tier.

No audio-only information was observed; sound (ambient music, sound FX) is togglable and decorative, and all game state - spins remaining, win amounts, feature triggers, multipliers, RTP/volatility/bet-range figures - is conveyed through on-screen text and numerals.

CREDIT/BET/WIN readouts are large high-contrast yellow-on-dark or gold-on-dark text; winning symbols and active WILDs during Free Spins get an added glow outline as a shape cue in addition to any color highlight.

The Free-Games tier is exposed both as a sentence ('Triggers 10 Free Games' / 'Triggers 25 Free Games') and as a plain icon count (2 vs 3) in the top-right preview strip. Jackpot tiers are labelled by name ('Minor Jackpot' / 'Grand Jackpot') in the ticker above the reels. On a winning free-games spin the centre banner number can still be mid-animation; the authoritative settled figure is the static 'WIN ‡X.XX' text in the bottom status bar.

Each high-value character symbol has both a distinct neon border colour (gold=top symbol, magenta/pink, green, blue) AND a distinct portrait/art, so colour is redundant, not the sole identifier; cocktail (low-value) symbols are distinguished by glass shape and garnish rather than colour.
Volatility-mode toggles print an explicit ON/OFF word next to each ribbon rather than relying on colour alone.

Free Spins vs Super Free Spins is differentiated by disco-ball icon colour (green vs purple), but this is always paired with the fixed purchase context (which BUY button was pressed) and distinct printed multiplier ranges (x2/x3/x5/x10 vs x2/x5/x10/x15/x25), so colour is not the only cue.

No audio-only information was observed; all game state (win amounts, free-spins counters, multiplier values, RTP, bet limits) is conveyed as on-screen text/numerals. Sound (music, SFX, volume) is togglable and decorative.
Payout numbers and rule text in the Payments and Help panels are high-contrast white/light-grey text on a near-black background throughout.

Large rounded touch targets throughout (Spin, Autoplay, Bonus Buy, mode toggles). Spacebar is a full keyboard alternative to clicking Spin. Autoplay with configurable stop-conditions (on any win / bonus won / single win exceeds / balance increases or decreases by) reduces the number of required manual actions.

All color-coded states are also conveyed by text/shape: won bet rows show a numeric multiplier + payout figure (not just a green tint); the outcome-history ribbon's blue-vs-purple chip split duplicates a magnitude already printed as text; the crashed-vs-live multiplier readout differs in both color (dark maroon/red vs white) AND accompanying state text ('Waiting for the next round' appears only after a crash).

Sound and Music toggles exist in the side menu and were OFF by default in the captured session; all outcome information (win/loss, multiplier, payout) is presented as on-screen text/numerals, not audio-only cues.

Key state changes (round result, win amount, bet-limit error) are shown as large, high-contrast bold numerals or banners against the near-black background; the bet-limit rejection toast is a large red banner with white text at the top of the game area.

All interactive controls (buttons, toggles, text inputs) are conventional rectangular/pill click targets of typical web-UI size (roughly 80-180px wide by ~35-45px tall at 1280x800); the only timing-critical action is manual cash-out during the ascent, and it has an auto-cashout alternative (armed target multiplier) for players who cannot react in time.
Bet-stepper disabled state is shown by brightness (dim grey vs. solid white), not hue, and is confirmed by the value stopping at the printed 0.20/50.00 bet limits.
Settings toggle on/off state is shown by BOTH fill color (dark grey = off, yellow/gold = on) AND a black checkmark glyph inside the pill, not color alone.

Win-tier escalation is dual-coded: MEGA WIN uses a cyan glow, SUPER MEGA WIN uses a red/crimson glow, but the tiers are also distinguished by the printed word ('MEGA' vs 'SUPER MEGA') and a larger printed win amount, not by glow color alone.

Chance x2 active state is shown by icon shape change (BUY cart icon becomes a cart-with-X icon) and the round action icon shape change (double-arrow becomes a star), not color alone. The purple 'BONUS ACTIVE' badge and the purple 'BUY FREE SPINS' button share a similar hue but are distinguished by position, size and accompanying text (noted as low residual risk).

No information is conveyed by sound only; Sound FX and Music are separate toggle/slider controls in Settings, and all game-state information (wins, free-spins count, multiplier values, bonus status) is duplicated as on-screen text and numbers.

Bet adjustment uses small up/down triangular stepper arrows rather than a drag slider (discrete, motor-friendly steps). Spacebar-to-spin is enabled by default, reducing the need for precise pointer clicks. Autoplay with configurable stop conditions further reduces required repeated input.

Control layout is stable across states: info/settings icons bottom-left, Balance and Total-bet stepper center-left, status/message text center, autoplay and spin controls bottom-right, BUY/bonus-status badge top-left. Paytable (9 pages) and rules (14 pages) are each a single long vertically-scrolling document reached via the 'i' and '?' icons.

The active-row cue is redundant to color: a bright green outline marks the active row, but the row is also always the physically lowest among the currently unlocked rows, so position confirms state if green cannot be distinguished. Multiplier-ladder values are always printed as white numerals ('x2' up to 'x100'), never color-only, and each digit chip is identified by its printed numeral rather than its accent-color glow ring.

No information observed in the captured frames is conveyed by audio alone: win amounts, remaining autoplay spins, RTP, Total Bet, Push-Up state and multiplier-meter values are all rendered as on-screen text or numerals. The Settings panel exposes independent mute toggles for All Sounds, Sound Effects and Music.

High-contrast neon glow styling throughout: thick glowing outlines on every symbol tile, a bright green full-width outline band on the active row against the dark navy grid, and bold white numerals for win amounts, the Total Bet figure and every multiplier-ladder value against dark backing bars.

Large circular touch targets for Spin, Autoplay and Bet Select. Bet and Push-Up tier are both chosen from a scrollable preset list rather than a fine +/- stepper requiring many taps. Autoplay presets run from 10 up to 1000 spins, reducing the number of interactions needed for extended play; the keyboard space bar also spins or skips animations.

State changes are expressed as text, not just animation: a 'PUSH-UP' pill badge appears while the modifier is armed and disappears once the round ends; the win-meter bar and a bottom 'WIN: <amount> fun' banner print every payout in plain numerals. The three side panels (Settings, Know The Game, Autoplays) share one consistent right-slide-in layout with a top-right 'X' close and the same bottom icon nav bar, aiding predictable navigation.

Every numbered vinyl chip shows its digit as printed white text in addition to its neon ring colour (red/orange/green/blue/grey/pink-magenta), so a chip's value never depends on colour perception alone; only the internal green triad (4,5,6) and blue triad (1,2,3) differ mainly by ring brightness, where the printed digit remains the reliable fallback.

The row currently eligible to score is marked by a brighter glowing border AND inward-pointing chevron arrows, not colour alone; the Meter Lock event is announced by both a padlock icon and the explicit text 'METER LOCK', not colour alone.

No game information is conveyed by audio alone. Settings exposes 'All Sounds', 'Sound Effects' and 'Music' toggles, implying sound is decorative; wins, meter level, Meter Lock, Push-Up status and bet are all shown as on-screen text or iconography.

Win amounts are duplicated in three places at once for a resolved round: an overlay on the winning chips, the top equalizer-style readout and a large bottom banner, all in large gold/white numerals, so no single small readout is the only source of the win figure.

The circular SPIN button and the panel confirm ('OK') button are large rounded targets; the space bar both starts a spin and skips/quick-plays an in-progress animation, and Autoplay (up to 1000 spins) reduces the number of individual clicks required to keep playing.

Control positions are stable across every captured screen: hamburger menu and sound-mute top-right, Balance bottom-left, Total Bet bottom-right, Push-Up/Bet-Select and the round's SPIN button in a fixed bottom-right cluster; the paytable/rules/info/settings panels share one 4-icon bottom nav bar (grid/?/gear/shield) and each opens as a linear scrollable document with a top-right close 'X'.

Royal letters A/K/Q are distinguished by shape as well as color; toggle switches by handle position; checkboxes by checkmark glyph; MONEY-symbol values and win amounts are printed as text/digits. One residual color-only cue: the VOLATILITY badge shows 4 gold-lit vs 1 grey-unlit lightning bolt with no accompanying numeral.

No audio-only information observed; SOUND and VIBRATION are decorative on/off toggles in Settings, and all game state (win amounts, spins-remaining counter, bet/credit) is conveyed through on-screen text.
Payout numbers, WIN amounts and MONEY-symbol values are rendered as large, high-contrast white/yellow/gold text on dark backgrounds, legible without relying on color.

The central SPIN button is the largest click target and can be held down for turbo spin; Autoplay (adjustable spin count, up to 100 shown) reduces clicks needed for extended play; bet +/- and autospin controls use large round buttons rather than small fields.

The info booklet is one continuous scrollable sheet (no fixed page breaks) with heading landmarks: GAME RULES, FREE SPINS, MAX WIN, VOLATILITY, HOW TO PLAY, MENU, BATTERY SAVER, INFORMATION SCREEN, BET MENU, AUTOPLAY. Bottom bar order left to right: Information, Autoplay menu, Spin-speed cycle, Bet/coins menu, System-settings hamburger; a mute icon floats outside the bar at the lower-left.

Buy Bonus banner is dark maroon/brown; Chance x2 banner is dark forest-green -- could be hard to tell apart for red-green color blindness, but both are also always distinguished by fixed position (left/right) and their different printed labels ('BUY BONUS' vs 'CHANCE x2').

Feature active/disabled state is shown by brightness change (dim grey = disabled, saturated orange = active) plus explicit 'ACTIVE' text and an icon-shape change (spin button switches from circular arrows to a star when Chance x2 is on), not by hue alone.

The three win-celebration tiers are distinguished by unique badge iconography -- Big Win: dark red/maroon shield crossed by bronze swords; Mega Win: green shield with two gold dragon-head motifs; Super Mega Win: bright gold/red coin crossed by silver-and-bronze swords -- plus printed tier name text, not color alone.

No information is conveyed by audio alone; Music and Sound FX toggles are independent and purely decorative. All game-state information (wins, spins remaining, multiplier values, feature active/disabled status) is shown as on-screen text/graphics.
All paytable and rules payout numbers are printed in orange-gold high-contrast text on a dark charcoal panel background.
Bet stepper arrows and autospin round-count buttons turn flat dull grey when disabled versus bright white/highlighted when enabled -- a brightness cue on large legible controls.

Primary actions (Spin, Buy Bonus, Chance x2, Cancel/Buy in the purchase dialog) are large, clearly separated targets. Spacebar can substitute for clicking Spin (on by default). Autoplay offers 5 configurable stop conditions, reducing manual actions needed for extended play.

Paytable and rules panels are each a single continuous scrollable document (mouse-wheel/scrollbar driven), not paged with next/previous buttons -- expose as one long scrollable region per panel. Control layout is stable across screens: info/settings bottom-far-left, Balance/Total bet+stepper center-left, Autoplay/Spin bottom-right.

Jackpot tier names (Mini/Major/Mega), free-spins/Hold-and-Win state changes, and all payout numbers are always accompanied by text labels, not conveyed by color alone. The Hold & Win grid uses a shape change (metal grate texture vs a round gold coin) to distinguish empty from filled cells, independent of color. Paytable line diagrams are labeled with a line number in addition to gold/grey cell highlighting. Residual risk: jackpot-bar label colors (green/cyan/pink for Mini/Major/Mega) rely partly on color, but each is also spelled out in text.

No audio-only information was observed; all game state (wins, respins remaining, free spins remaining, jackpot values, bonus purchase prices) is conveyed through on-screen text and numerals. Sound (music/SFX) is adjustable and togglable independently in Settings.

Large circular touch targets for Spin and Autoplay; Spacebar is a keyboard alternative to clicking Spin (on by default in Settings). Autoplay with fixed round-count presets (10 up to 1000, or unlimited) reduces the number of required manual actions.

Control positions are stable across all screens: info/settings icons bottom-left, Balance/Total-bet fields center-left, win readouts center, Autoplay/Spin buttons bottom-right, Buy-bonus button fixed at the character artwork's base on the left. The info booklet (paytable + rules) is a long linear scroll sequence within 2 selectable sections (paytable, rules) plus one non-functional section (history) in this build.

All four corner tiles are visually identical (dark tile, white question-mark) before a pick, so there is no colour cue predicting which one hides dynamite. The dynamite icon itself appears grey/desaturated on the Bomb Count control and bright red only inside the Bonus Game reveal reel; the actual round outcome is always confirmed by the printed Bank/balance figures, not by tile colour.

The primary Start Game / Cash Out lever changes its glow from grey (idle) to green (active) to signal state, but the printed word underneath it always duplicates the state in text, so the control remains usable without colour perception.

All observed game feedback (round result, bonus trigger, multiplier changes) is duplicated as on-screen numeric/text changes (Bank figure, win-panel sum, balance); a separate Sound slider and Music slider in Settings allow muting audio entirely without losing any information.

The Bet Amount field uses a green-tinted seven-segment LCD-style readout with visible unlit 'ghost' segments behind the lit digits (a skeuomorphic calculator effect), which may be lower-contrast than the plain bold digits used for Balance and Bank elsewhere on screen.

On the cash-out win panel the 'odd N.NNx' multiplier label is printed in small white/green text at the top-right, noticeably smaller than the large magenta cashed-out sum beside it; a user relying specifically on the multiplier value may need to zoom in to read it.

The whole game is operable with a small number of large, well-separated targets: one primary lever (Start Game/Cash Out), four corner tiles, and simple +/- steppers for bet amount and bomb count, each with one-click min/max shortcuts to the extremes. No drag gestures, hold-to-activate controls, or time-pressured input were observed.

Game state (Bank, current and next step multiplier, bet amount, balance, RTP, bet limits, bonus multiplier values, rules-booklet section headings) is rendered as real on-screen text rather than baked into images. The one exception is the four corner tiles, which are icon-only ('?' glyph, and whatever icon a revealed tile shows) with no accompanying text label in the captured build, so tile identity/state needs alternative-text support.
The three multiplier wheels are colored green, purple and red, but each is also identified by its numbers: green x2 to x10, purple x10 to x30, red x30 to x100, plus the LEVEL UP text sector.

Power Clamps are red jaws on bright green coiled cables hanging over the top of a symbol; the cable shape separates them from the symbols. Battery indicator: three green segments plus a yellow lightning-bolt segment at the right, told apart by position.
Royal letters differ by letter shape (A, K, Q) as well as color (dark red, dark purple, olive green).
Winning tiles glow orange-yellow with flame sparks; the strip under the reels repeats the outcome in words as Win or Total Win.
Wins are shown visually: glowing winning tiles, Win and Total Win text in the strip, a MEGA WIN banner. Sound content was not captured, so whether any outcome is conveyed by sound alone is unknown.
Inactive Start Auto Spin button is dim brick-red with low-contrast text. Balance and bet readouts are pale cyan-blue digits on dark panels; Max Bet and Confirm are orange on a dark ground.
A scrolling text ticker under the reels shows rule text in moving fragments, so a single frame never shows a whole sentence.

Space key starts a spin, holding it continues spinning, pressing it during a spin skips the animation. Tapping the Spin button or game area stops the reels. Autoplay offers 10, 30, 50, 80 or 1000 spins. Control buttons are about 80 px round; the menu hamburger at the right edge is the smallest target.
Balance, bet and win are text readouts in three panels along the lower part of the screen. The game is a canvas build; the Paytable and Rules panels are real DOM text, the reels are not.

The four low-value cannister symbols are mainly distinguished by colour (purple, orange, green, teal/cyan) and the three high-value portrait cards by colour-bordered frame (purple, red, green); each also has a distinct illustration as a secondary cue, but green vs teal cannisters risk confusion for a colour-blind user relying on hue alone.
Paytable's valid/invalid cluster-shape examples (Cluster Pays section) use both colour (green vs red) AND a distinct glyph (checkmark vs cross) side by side, not colour alone.

Mid-round win-tier popups are colour-coded (red = MEGA WIN, magenta/pink = SUPER MEGA WIN, green = BIG WIN) but the tier name is always spelled out as text alongside the colour, so it is legible without colour discrimination.

Special symbol colours described in words: Scatter is a gold sheriff-star medallion on a dark-red disc; Wild is a gold/yellow badge with white 'WILD' text; Booster is a glowing cyan/blue energy orb; Destroyer is a metallic blue-grey robotic skull with glowing red eyes and a red-orange glow.

No audio-only information was observed; Music and Sound FX are independently toggleable in Settings, and all game state (wins, spins left, multipliers, feature status) is conveyed via on-screen text and numerals.
Checkbox states in Settings (Quick spin / Spacebar to spin / Music / Sound FX) are shown by a checkmark glyph inside a white-outlined square, not by colour alone.
Spacebar can trigger a spin (toggle in Settings, default ON), reducing reliance on precise mouse clicks. Autoplay supports round counts up to 1000 or unlimited, reducing repetitive clicking.

Bottom-bar controls keep stable relative positions across all base-game screens: Info+Settings far-left, Balance/Total-bet centre, Autoplay+Spin far-right. Buy Bonus and Wild Spin are both anchored to the same left-side arcade prop with their own always-visible price readout, independent of any menu.

Wins are shown as numbers and a WIN strip, not by color alone. Selected values in Bet Options and Auto Spin are marked by yellow text plus a highlighted band or fill. Symbols differ by shape; the Wild tile (red-and-gold tile with a groom) is labelled with the printed word WILD.
Palette is deep red, gold and warm orange with pink medallions and jade green accents; menu panels are dark slate grey with yellow text.
All state changes have text banners: rotating tip banner, BIG WIN, Remaining Free Spin counter, WIN BOTH TOP & BOTTOM x8.
Line win value is drawn over symbols in a decorative font, which is hard to read. Menu text is yellow on dark slate grey.
Spin by tap or Space key (hold Space for continuous spins; tap during a spin to stop). Auto Spin offers 10, 30, 50, 80 or 1000 spins. Turbo toggle shortens reel spin time.
Balance, bet and win on the main screen are canvas drawings; the Paytable and Rules panels are real DOM text.

The entire bet decision is colour (red/black/green), but each of the three bet buttons is disambiguated by fixed screen position (left/middle/right) and a unique multiplier label (x2/x14/x2), so a colour-blind player can act on position and multiplier text alone without telling red from black. The winning tile itself is disambiguated by its printed digit: 0 is always green, and 1-14 alternate red/black in a fixed, learnable order visible directly on the strip -- but the strip surface otherwise relies on colour alone, with no extra pattern/glyph marking red vs black beyond the digit. Separately, the rules dialog's header line uses a small emoji legend that prints a WHITE circle for what is visually the black tile colour in the live game -- a minor colour-naming inconsistency between the rules text and the actual tile colour.

No spoken narration is present. Sound and Music are separate toggle sliders in Settings, so effects and music can each be muted independently. All game-critical information (bet amount, chosen colour, multiplier, balance, round result) is rendered as on-screen text, so the game is fully usable muted.

Tile digits are large bold white numerals on flat, high-contrast coral-red/charcoal-black/teal-green backgrounds, and the bet buttons print large multiplier text (x2/x14/x2) rather than relying on small icons. There is no dedicated win-screen overlay to notice; the round outcome must instead be read from the on-screen Balance figure and the My bets table (Time/Bet Amount/Multiplier/Payout), both plain text rather than animated graphics.

All interactive controls (three colour buttons, bet amount min/-/+/max, Place bet, Cancel, settings icons) are large discrete click targets rather than drag or precision gestures, and no rapid or continuously-held input is required. A placed bet can be cancelled any time before the strip starts spinning, giving a forgiving window to correct a misclick.

The three colour-bet buttons carry both a colour word and an explicit multiplier ('x2', 'x14', 'x2') and could be exposed with accessible names such as 'Bet Black, pays 2 times stake'. The critical gap is the round outcome itself: the strip's stop position is communicated purely by tile colour plus the printed digit, and the fixed odd/even-to-colour mapping (which digits are red vs black) is never stated anywhere in the on-screen text, so a screen-reader user has no textual rule to derive the winning colour from the digit alone.

Character symbols are distinguished by portrait subject (king, politician, playwright, lady, witch) and frame color (dark red, blue-grey, dark silver, pinkish-gold, dark violet) — shape and portrait face provide primary identification.

Royal symbols use letter shape as primary identifier: A (dark red), K (cobalt blue with crown above), Q (purple-magenta with gem accents), J (emerald green). Letter shape alone uniquely identifies each.
WILD is a folded newspaper with 'WILD' text printed in gold — text label distinguishes it from all portrait/letter symbols regardless of color.
BONUS symbol is shaped like a real tube train carriage front with 'BONUS' text in golden-orange — unique silhouette and text label, not dependent on green color alone.

COLLECT and GAMBLE buttons in Feature Gamble have distinct shapes and clear text labels. Winning payline is highlighted in green but 'LINE N PAYS $X' text is always displayed, confirming which line won without relying on color.
BONUS trigger highlight: acid-green glow around BONUS symbol cells, but each cell also shows the tube train carriage image. Payouts are always numeric dollar text, no color-only encoding.

AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX are independently toggleable in Settings. BATTERY SAVER reduces animations. Feature Gamble outcomes (collect vs gamble success/failure) are accompanied by visual text overlays — no audio-only feedback.

Reels use dark charcoal tunnel background with warm gold/brass frame. Character portraits use warm earthy tones on dark backgrounds with ornate gilded frames. Contrast between symbol frame and reel cell (mahogany brown) is moderate — high-contrast mode not available.

Feature Gamble hierarchy uses a side panel listing station names in text (Pentonville, King's Cross, Canary Wharf, Buckingham Palace, End of the Line). Active selection indicated by bright green-teal glow plus text highlighting.

Keyboard controls: SPACE and ENTER start/stop the spin. Turbo spin available (hold SPACE). Autoplay supports up to 100 auto-spins with SKIP SCREENS option to bypass intro/end screens. Bet adjustable via on-screen +/- or bet menu.

All interactive controls are icon-based (hamburger menu, speaker, 'i' info, spin circle, +/- ovals, AUTOPLAY rectangle). Underlying button roles are standard Pragmatic Play canvas layout — no native ARIA labels exposed in canvas context.

Win amount, current bet, and credit balance are all shown as text overlays on the bottom bar (e.g. WIN $1.00, BET $2.00, CREDIT $99,999.00). Feature names during bonus use text titles (station names).

Held reels during the re-spin feature are marked by a yellow outline frame plus desaturation of all non-held content (double non-color cue). Winning payline shows a printed number over it, not color alone. Toggle switches show handle position besides track color. Payline indicator ovals carry a printed number besides their fill color.
No information is conveyed by sound alone; the Sound-Ambient and Sound-Effects toggles are optional. Jackpot amounts, bet/win and feature state are always shown as on-screen text.

Primary actions (PLAY / STOP during re-spins) are large circular centered targets; the space bar also starts and stops a spin. BET MAX raises only BET LEVEL, not COIN — reaching the true maximum bet requires adjusting COIN separately.

Control layout is stable between the base game and the re-spin feature: only background art and a 'Re-spins Remaining' counter change, no button relocates. The Help screen and the paytable booklet are both linear scrollable documents with an explicit close control.

Four dragons each have distinct frame color (gold/purple backing, crimson/red, dark green, amber/tan) AND distinct face style (adult friendly = purple, adult fierce = red-orange, mature ridged = green-magenta, juvenile rounded = teal-green). Red-green deficient viewers: amber/tan frame of the teal-green dragon is a reliable non-color structural cue.

RESPIN PHASE crystal types identified by both color (green, red, blue, purple) AND panel position: green crystal = top-left FREE SPINS panel, red crystal = bottom-left WILDS panel, blue crystal = top-right WIN MULTIPLIER panel, purple crystal = bottom-right MYSTERY SYMBOLS panel. Panel position alone uniquely identifies each crystal type without color.

WILD symbol: dark red background may appear brownish in protanopia; identified by bold gold 'WILD' text label and ornate gold frame regardless of background hue. Reel restriction (reels 2-4 only) is a structural positional cue. Settings toggles: ON = right position with bright appearance; OFF = left position with dark/grey appearance — dual position and brightness cue.

All game outcomes, wins, and feature activations communicated via visual text overlays: 'BONUS ACTIVE', 'GOOD LUCK!', 'RESPINS LEFT N', 'WIN $X.XX', 'FREE SPINS COMPLETED'. Win amounts shown as numeric text. AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX are independently toggleable in system settings.

SPACE and ENTER start/stop spin; HOLD SPACE activates turbo spin. AUTOPLAY supports up to 100 auto-spins with SKIP SCREENS option to bypass feature intro/outro animations, reducing required interactions. Buy Free Spins (100x total bet) provides direct FS access without needing the natural BONUS corner trigger.

All symbols identified by name (dragon type or card rank A/K/Q/J/10) or text label (WILD, BONUS). Win amounts displayed as '$X.XX'. RESPIN PHASE accumulator panels show numeric counts as on-screen text (e.g. 'WIN MULTIPLIER 2x', 'MYSTERY SYMBOLS 30', 'FREE SPINS 3', 'WILDS 2'). '1600 WAYS TO WIN' shown as text below reel grid.

Four card royals (A/K/Q/J) each combine a distinct colour AND a distinct letterform, staying distinguishable by letter shape alone; win-highlight uses a gold glow/outline box (shape), not colour fill only; feature names (GOLD RESPIN, FREE SPINS, SUPER MEGA WIN, BIG WIN) are spelled out as large text alongside their gradient colours; checkbox toggles use a checkmark glyph, not colour alone.

No information observed to be conveyed by audio alone; Settings expose independent Music and Sound FX toggles; all wins, spin counters, respin counters and feature triggers are shown as on-screen text/graphics.

Coin symbols print their FUN denomination in bold directly on the coin face (e.g. 0.05, 1.00, 7.00, 16.00 FUN); the Gold Respin respin counter is printed as plain numerals in the bottom status bar, on the right side next to the spin/refresh icon.

Spin and Buy Bonus are large circular targets; Spacebar can trigger a spin instead of clicking (on by default, toggle in Settings); Autoplay offers configurable stop conditions (any win, bonus win, win exceeds amount, balance increases/decreases) to reduce required manual actions.

Stable, predictable control layout: info/settings icons bottom-left, bet stepper and balance centre-left, autoplay/spin at far right, Buy Bonus fixed mid-left of the play area; paytable (25 pages) and rules (13 pages) are two separate linear scrollable documents with clearly headed sections (About the Game, How to play, Features, Spin Results, Settings, Return to Player, RNG, Additional information).
Card symbols differ by letter/numeral shape as well as color: A is orange/gold, K is red, Q is green, J is teal/cyan, 10 is pink/magenta.
WILD is a golden dragon head with a red mane on a dark/green frame, identified by its distinct dragon-head shape and 'WILD' pay-table text, not color alone.
Money-orb values in free spins are shown as printed dollar text on a dark plaque beneath the symbol (e.g. '$20.00'), not conveyed by color alone.

Settings/autoplay toggle states use switch-handle left/right position and a checkmark glyph in addition to green=on/dark=off track color; bonus-buy confirm/cancel buttons use checkmark vs X glyph shape in addition to green vs red.

All game state (spins left, win amounts, feature triggers, retrigger levels, buy cost, RTP/volatility/bet limits) is presented as on-screen text and icons; AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX are independently toggleable decorative audio, not carriers of unique gameplay information.

Win amounts and feature counters use large high-contrast lettering (e.g. gold numerals on a green plaque for 'SUPER WIN', large printed 'FREE SPINS LEFT n' counts) legible without fine color discrimination.

The 5 pre-round free-spins modifier icons are all rendered in the same neutral grey/silver tone with no differentiating highlight observed, making it hard to tell visually which modifiers (if any) are active for a given round without reading each icon's pictogram individually.

All primary controls are large round touch targets; SPACE and ENTER start/stop the spin, and holding SPACE triggers turbo spin. Autoplay offers a configurable spin count and a SKIP SCREENS option to reduce required interactions.

Control positions are stable across all base-game screens: hamburger-menu and sound icons at bottom-left, separate 'i' info icon beside them, CREDIT/BET readouts center-left, SPIN centered-right with -/+ bet buttons flanking it, AUTOPLAY below SPIN. Info booklet is a fixed linear 8-page sequence with a 'Page n/8' readout on every page.

The three baby dragons are told apart by creature shape and face as well as tile colour (orange-red with open mouth, blue with orange wing fin, green with bulging eyes), but their tiles are red, blue and olive green, so shape is the safer cue.
The four suit tiles (spade, club, heart, diamond) are all dark grey stone with only a small colour accent in the gem (yellow-gold, light blue, pink, green). Rely on the icon shape, not colour.
The Dragon Eye is recognised by its vertical black pupil on a red scaled tile. Winning clusters get a bright gold glow plus a printed amount on the cluster.
Feature banners are told apart by printed name (Earth Dragon, Water Dragon, Fire Dragon) as well as colour: green, light blue and orange letters. The GET STARTED button is identified by its text.

On the Auto Spin sheet the selected pill (10, 30, 50, 80, 1000) differs from the others only by a lighter green fill and green number against grey; contrast is low and the state is not marked by shape.
Every feature is announced by a text banner (Earth Dragon !, Water Dragon !, Fire Dragon !, WIN, TOTAL WIN, Mega Win), so sound is not required. Sound can be switched off from the menu.
UI panels are dark slate grey with light grey text; balance and bet numbers are pale green. The Wild is a golden W drawn slightly larger than a tile over the centre cell.
The collection bar fill changes by stage: dark when empty, blue toward the 30 target, red toward 55, orange with a gold dragon ornament toward 80; the plaque text size stays the same.

Spin by tap or the Space key (hold for repeated spins, press during a spin to skip animation). Auto Spin offers 10, 30, 50, 80 or 1000 rounds, Turbo shortens animation, and the bet picker has Max Bet and Confirm buttons. No timed input is needed.
Paytable and rules panels are real DOM text. The reel grid is a canvas without text alternatives; outcomes are shown only visually, with amounts printed over winning clusters and in the WIN field.

Symbol identity is carried by shape and illustration, not color alone: four low symbols are four distinct gem shapes (spade, heart, club, diamond) on near-identical grey tiles; the four high symbols are different creatures or an eye.
The gem colors of the low symbols (orange spade, red heart, blue club, green diamond) are redundant with their shapes.
The four collection-bar stages are told apart by the printed count and denominator (x/10, x/30, x/50, x/70) as well as by bar color (green, blue, red, olive-yellow to gold).
Winning clusters are marked by a glowing outline and a printed cash number on one tile while non-winning tiles dim, not by color alone.
Wild is a golden dragon egg in a glowing cyan-blue tile with scattered gold coins, and carries the word WILD in red-orange letters on a dark red-brown banner.
No audio-only information observed: feature starts are shown by text banners, bar color change, particle effects and background art changes. A Sound toggle exists.

Dark purple-blue cave background with warm orange, gold and red accents; text on the info plaque is gold (WIN) or pale grey-blue (scrolling hint); menu panels use white text on dark charcoal-navy with pale orange-peach active items and buttons.
Cascades use bright glows, shards and fire rings; Turbo mode (struck-through lightning bolt means off) shortens animations.
Spin by tap or Space key; holding Space continues spins; Auto Spin offers 10, 30, 50, 80 or 1000 spins; the dragon features are automatic and need no input.
Each symbol is a distinct illustration; the cash amount of each winning cluster is printed on a tile and mirrored in the WIN pill. Hint banners and collection-bar counters are text.
During a cascade the banner above the grid shows the win of the current cascade while the bottom centre pill shows the accumulated round total; they must not be added together.

Symbol identity is never colour-only: each premium/mid symbol has a unique background card colour AND a unique pictorial subject (ingot vs toad vs carp vs pot vs scroll vs coin-knot); the five card-rank symbols are further distinguished by their printed letter/digit glyph.

WILD (small gold yin-yang medallion with 'WILD' text) and SUPER WILD (large gold dragon-lion head) are both gold-toned but distinguished by shape/size and text label, not colour; SCATTER is distinguished from SUPER WILD by its red 'SCATTER' text label and flame iconography.

Volatility rating is shown as an explicit sentence of text ('High volatility games pay out less often on average but the chance to hit big wins...') in addition to a 5-bolt icon badge, so it is not colour/icon-only.
Settings and Autoplay toggle switches show ON/OFF state via handle position (left=off, right=on) and, for Autoplay's checkboxes, a white checkmark glyph, in addition to green/grey colour.
Ambient music and sound effects have independent on/off toggles in System Settings; no game-critical information (win amounts, feature triggers, rules text) is conveyed audio-only.

All numeric information (bet, credit, win, RTP, paylines, free spins count) is shown as readable on-screen text; symbol payouts are always presented as text tables, never conveyed only by relative icon size.

Turbo spin is available both as a held-key shortcut (HOLD SPACE) and as a separate Autoplay-menu checkbox; Autoplay supports a configurable spin count (default 100 observed) plus a Skip Screens option to reduce required interactions.

Functional state is duplicated in text/shape: OFF/selected states are printed as words, payout tiers are row-labelled numbers, wild/coin multipliers are printed as 'xN' text, and section headers combine a red accent bar with bold text rather than color alone. Residual risk: some similarly-shaped paying symbols (purple hexagonal pot vs pink lotus pot; teal bell pot vs blue-violet jar) rely partly on hue at small size, though their tier numbers and fixed paytable position remain non-color anchors.

No audio-only information was observed; all round outcomes, feature triggers, counts and multipliers render as on-screen text/numbers. Sound settings (All Sounds / Sound Effects / Music) can each be muted independently.

Primary actions use large circular hit-targets (SPIN, right-rail icons); Base Bet and Push Bet selection require opening a dedicated panel and clicking a row/tile rather than fine dragging; Autoplay removes the need for repeated spin clicks. Push Bet cannot be turned off mid-round or mid-autoplay -- autoplay must be stopped first.

Paytable/rules/info booklets are strictly linear scroll sequences with a fixed header (PAYTABLE / GAME INFO / KNOW THE GAME) and a consistent bottom nav bar (grid, question-mark, gear, shield icons) for switching between them; Balance and Total Bet are always anchored bottom-left/bottom-right of the game screen in a stable position.

The 5 payline tags flanking the reels are each a different color (yellow/red/blue/green/magenta) but every tag also carries a unique digit 1-5, so line identity is readable without color discrimination.

Money-symbol values are always shown as printed dollar text on each cell's plaque, never conveyed by the coin/gem icon color alone; Big Money Wheel prize segments likewise carry printed multiplier text ('40X', '10X', '100X') alongside their segment color.
Settings toggle switches (Battery Saver, Ambient Music, Sound FX, Intro Screen) show on/off via BOTH color (grey vs green track) and the physical left/right position of the white handle.

The Hold and Spin 15-segment progress meter distinguishes filled vs empty cells by a busy multicolor pinwheel pattern versus a flat single-tone gold disc (pattern/brightness cue, not hue alone) — flagged as a residual low risk since it is the least text-redundant indicator in the game.

No audio-only information observed; Ambient Music and Sound FX are separately toggleable and purely decorative. Bet, credit, win amounts, respins remaining (hearts), feature triggers and wheel results are all conveyed through on-screen text and icons, not sound alone.

Win/congratulations screens use very large, high-contrast bold gold 3D digits and lettering on a dark red parchment background; balance/bet/win readouts in the bottom bar use bright blue/yellow text on a dark bar.

Large round click targets for SPIN, menu, sound and info; SPACE and ENTER keys also start/stop the spin. AUTOPLAY (adjustable spin count plus a SKIP SCREENS option) reduces required clicks for extended play, and both Hold and Spin and the Big Money Wheel Bonus auto-advance between reveals, needing only a single 'press anywhere to continue' tap at trigger/result screens.

Stable control layout across all screens: hamburger menu + sound stacked bottom-left, a separate 'i' info button beside them, bet -/+ flanking the central SPIN button bottom-right, AUTOPLAY beneath SPIN. The info booklet is a strictly linear 6-page sequence with an explicit 'Page N/6' readout on every page, navigated by previous/close/next controls.

All 7 paying symbols have distinct shapes and embedded letter/number labels (A, K, Q, J, 10, coin shape with square hole, lantern with tassels). WILD and SCATTER have English text labels embedded in the artwork. Color is supplementary — no symbol relies on color alone for identification.

Mini slot 8-symbols are differentiated by color (red/blue/green). Multiplier payouts are also displayed as numeric text labels (50x/15x/5x for Dragon Spins; 2500x/250x/25x for Hot Pots). Hot Pots header shows numeric labels X2500/X250/X25/X5 — readable without color.
BUY BONUS (red cancel / green confirm) buttons also carry distinct X and checkmark icons. UI buttons have full text labels: BUY BONUS, ANTE BET, AUTOPLAY, START AUTOPLAY.
All bonus triggers, win outcomes, and game rules conveyed as on-screen text. Settings menu has explicit SOUND FX and AMBIENT MUSIC toggles. No audio-only information identified.

Credit and bet values displayed in large cyan text at bottom bar. Win amounts shown in large bold text with glow effect (BIG WIN screen). Bonus multipliers shown in large labeled numerics above reels (X2500/X250/X25/X5).

Keyboard shortcuts available: SPACE (hold for turbo spin), ENTER (start/stop spin). Autoplay supports adjustable spin count (up to 100) with SKIP SCREENS option to reduce interactions during bonus sequences.

All win amounts, bet values, credit balance, and bonus multipliers are displayed as numeric text on screen. Bonus triggers and rules described in paytable text (7 pages). No audio-only information identified.

Red Dragon (red-orange), Green Dragon (olive-green), and Blue Dragon (ice-blue) are distinguishable by unique shape and facial features — horn type, eye color, head tendrils — in addition to color. Shape identification alone is sufficient for any colorblind type.
Royal letters A, K, Q, J are identifiable by letter shape alone regardless of their distinct gem colors (emerald-green, sapphire-blue, crimson-red, magenta). No color perception required.

WILD is uniquely shield/crest-shaped with text 'DRAGON KINGDOM' — identifiable by shape and text without color. SCATTER is a unique arch/gate shape with 'FREE SPINS' text. Both distinguishable without color perception.
Settings toggles indicate state by both color (green=ON, gray=OFF) and horizontal position (left=OFF, right=ON). State is readable without color perception.
All game events fully indicated visually: retrigger banner text, HUD counters (FREE SPINS LEFT, MULTIPLIER, WIN amount), and overlay panels. No audio required for gameplay decisions.

No autoplay function present. Every spin requires an explicit SPIN button click. Bet adjustment requires separate +/- button interactions. No keyboard shortcut information documented in captured rules.
Game renders entirely on a canvas element with no accessible DOM text. All payout tables and rules are in the 6-page in-game info panel, accessible visually. No screen-reader API support detected.

Most controls are shape/text-based, not color-coded: icon glyphs (menu lines, speaker, +/-, info 'i'), toggle-switch handle position (left=off/right=on), explicit numeral/text values (level counter, egg multipliers, win amounts, autospins count), and nav-arrow shape (left/right triangle vs X).

Progressive Feature active/inactive state is shown by presence/absence of numeral overlays on the dragon eggs, not by color shift alone; the egg whose multiplier is applied to a win carries an animated glow/highlight in addition to color.

Symbol colors named for reference: WILD = golden dragon eye on teal ring; blue dragon = icy cyan-blue head with white horns; red dragon = crimson-red/maroon head with pink throat; fire 7 = orange-red lava numeral; purple spade = magenta-purple gem; red heart = pink-red gem; green club = emerald-green gem; blue diamond = pale ice-blue gem.

No audio-only information observed; SOUND FX and AMBIENT MUSIC are purely decorative toggles. All game state — balance, bet, win amounts, feature level/counter and multipliers, and instructional hints — is conveyed visually/textually on screen.
Balance/bet labels (CREDIT/BET) are yellow on a dark background; win amounts and progressive-feature numerals are gold on dark teal/maroon panels — all rendered as large high-contrast text.

Large round click targets, with the central SPIN button the largest interactive element. SPACE and ENTER also start/stop a spin (keyboard-operable); holding SPACE engages turbo spin. Autoplay with adjustable spin count reduces required clicks for extended play.

Control positions are stable across all screens: menu+sound stacked far-left, info 'i' button to their right, bet +/- flank the central SPIN button, AUTOPLAY sits directly below SPIN. The rules booklet is a linear 6-page sequence navigated by left-triangle/right-triangle with a single 'X' to close, each page marked 'Page n/6'.

Wins are shown by a glowing yellow outline on winning symbols with the other tiles dimmed, and also by a text banner under the board ('1 WAY = $0.8', '2 WAYS = $5.6') and 'LAST WIN: <amount>$' in the message strip, so the result does not rely on colour alone.
Jackpot plaques are always visible on the left and carry the tier name in words (GRAND red plaque, MAJOR purple, MINOR blue, MINI green) plus the amount and a character portrait.

The three pots differ by colour (green, red, blue) and by fixed position: green on the left, red in the centre raised and largest, blue on the right. Gold Coin rims are red, green or blue, so the matching pot is identified by position.

Green Dragon Coin is green with an embossed dragon and no number, while Prize Coins are gold with numerals, so the collector differs by emblem as well as colour. Risk of red-green confusion exists for the red and green pots and coins; position mitigates it.

Pay symbols differ by shape and by tile frame colour (light blue koi, purple coin bundle, red lantern, teal lotus, dark green dragon); low symbols are letters and numbers: A red, K purple, Q pink, J green, 10 blue, 9 light cyan.

Splash pages are told apart by heading text ('Jackpot Bonus' and 'Hold & Win'), not only by dot colour; the active dot is bright green against a dark green one. Jackpot Bonus coins differ by portrait (girl, lady, red-robed figure, emperor); closed coins are dull brown with a dragon face.
Settings contain only Music and Sound switches. Whether any sound cue exists for wins was not tested.
The Hold & Win respin counter is shown as numbered cells 1, 2, 3 rather than by colour only.
Buy Bonus prices are printed in a large decorative font that OCR does not read; a human reads them fine.

Spin, autoplay and bet changes are single clicks. Turbo needs a long press on the spin button labelled 'HOLD FOR TURBO'. Autoplay starts with one click, has no round-count setting and is stopped with the same button turned into an X. Win banners require tap to continue.
Not determined: no screen-reader support or ARIA structure was examined. The game is canvas-rendered and the DOM channel only listed control elements.

The three Dragon Pots meters are colour-coded (blue/green/gold) but also labelled with text (WILD/MULTI/BONUS), fixed vertical position (top/middle/bottom), and matching dragon colour — colour is never the only cue.
Buy Feature (purple plaque) vs Special Bets (red plaque) buttons differ by colour, explicit text label, and screen position (upper vs lower), not colour alone.
The paytable win-path diagram uses a green check mark and a red X, additionally distinguished by shape (check vs cross).

The 5 royal card symbols (A/K/Q/J/10) are printed in different colours (red/purple/green/blue-cyan/gold-orange) but are primarily identified by their letter/number glyph, colour is only a secondary cue.
The premium option in the Buy Feature and Special Bets modals (Super Free Spins / Super Spin) is marked by a gold border plus explicit larger price and descriptive text, not colour alone.

No audio-only information observed; SOUND FX and AMBIENT are separate toggles, and all game state (spins left, active multiplier, win amounts, feature trigger/result) is conveyed through on-screen text, confirming sound is decorative/supplementary.
Win amounts, spins-left counts and multiplier values are always shown as large, legible, high-contrast white/gold text on dark stone plaques, not conveyed by colour or icon alone.
Volatility is shown both as 5-of-5 lightning-bolt icons and spelled out as the word 'VOLATILITY' with accompanying explanatory text.

Large round click targets for spin, bet +/- steppers, and menu/sound/info icons; SPACE and ENTER keys are keyboard alternatives to clicking SPIN. Autoplay and the SKIP SCREENS option reduce the number of required interactions for repeated play and for skipping feature intro/outro screens.

Base-game control layout is stable: hamburger menu and sound icons stacked far-left, a separate 'i' info button beside them, CREDIT/BET labels center-left, bet -/+ flanking the central SPIN button, AUTOPLAY below/right of spin. The 8-page info/rules booklet is a strictly linear sequence walked with back and forward arrow buttons, closed via a centre or top-right 'X', with the current page always announced as 'Page N/8'.
Wild is identified by shape and text, not color alone: a gold crown with a blue gem and a red ribbon printed with the word 'WILD'.
Scatter is identified by shape and text: an orange dragon egg wrapped in flames with a gold 'SCATTER' nameplate.

Free Spins state is signalled by both a background/palette shift (blue indoor palace hall vs. outdoor grey stone arch and green forest) and explicit text ('Free spins: n/total', 'BONUS ACTIVE'), not color alone.
Settings and Autoplay toggles use checkmark glyphs inside checkboxes and filled/outlined button states, not color alone; the bet stepper uses up/down triangle glyphs rather than color coding.

Residual risk: the BUY BONUS button is red and the CHANCE x2 button is purple with no shape differentiation beyond their printed labels and toggle affordance -- a user relying purely on button color rather than reading the label could confuse the two.
No audio-only information observed on any captured screen; Music and Sound FX are independent toggles in Settings and appear decorative, as win/feature state is always also shown as text and imagery.
Ways-count banner and the Free Spins multiplier are shown as large gold high-contrast numerals against a light or dark solid background, legible at low vision.

Large circular touch targets for Spin, info, settings and autoplay. Spacebar can trigger Spin (Settings > 'Spacebar to spin', on by default). Autoplay offers up to unlimited rounds and an optional Quick Spin toggle (off by default), reducing required manual actions.

Control layout is stable across screens: info (i) and settings (gear) grouped bottom-left, Balance/Total bet centered, autoplay (A) and Spin grouped bottom-right, Buy Bonus/Chance x2 as a fixed left-side vertical pair during the base game. The paytable and rules booklets are each a single linear 9-page scroll reachable via the 'i' button.

Waterfall colors map to modifier names but are never color-only: pink/rose = BALANCE, yellow/gold = PROSPERITY, blue = VITALITY, and the modifier name is always printed as text on-screen and again on the bonus-choice dialog. Jackpot bar segments (green=MINI, blue=MINOR, magenta=MAJOR, red=GRAND) are likewise always paired with the printed label.

Toggle switches, checkboxes, cancel/confirm buttons and paytable navigation arrows encode state by shape/glyph/position (checkmark vs X, triangle direction, knob left/right) in addition to color, so no control depends on hue alone.
No audio-only information observed; AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX are decorative toggles. All game state (wins, spins/respins remaining, bonus totals, bet/credit) is conveyed through on-screen text.
Win amounts and balances are large high-contrast white or yellow-orange text on dark plaques/panels; body text throughout the 8-page rules booklet is white on a black/dark translucent panel.

All primary buttons (spin, bet +/-, buy-bonus confirm/cancel, bonus-choice cards) are large circular/rectangular click targets; SPACE/ENTER start or stop a spin as keyboard alternatives; autoplay (configurable spin count) and SKIP SCREENS reduce required interactions during feature rounds.

Control layout is stable across screens: menu+sound stacked bottom-far-left, a separate 'i' info button to their right, bet -/+ flanking the central spin button, autoplay directly below spin; the rules booklet is a fixed linear 8-page sequence.

Most state is conveyed by icon shape, switch position or explicit text (the 'X Free Spins Remaining' counter, 'FEATURE TRIGGERED'/'YOU HAVE WON' banners, printed BET/WIN labels and paytable numbers) rather than colour alone. One residual risk: the payline highlight on a win uses a gold box outline plus a coloured line-number badge (pink/magenta observed); the badge colour is decorative, but the printed number inside it is the accessible cue.

No information observed is conveyed by sound alone: feature state (trigger, spins remaining, win amount) is always shown as on-screen text/banners in addition to any sound cue. Settings expose separate 'Sound - Ambient' and 'Sound - Effects' toggles (both on by default) plus a footer mute icon.

The jackpot ticker prints its amount in orange digits on a black readout window, a high-contrast pairing. Bottom-bar controls are white icon glyphs on gold/green/bronze circles, and BET/WIN/COIN values are printed as light text on the dark status strip beneath the reels, not conveyed by colour alone.

SPIN and AUTO PLAY are large round targets; BET LEVEL and COIN steppers are small round +/- buttons requiring precise clicks. Autoplay offers preset spin counts (10/20/30/50/100/500) and configurable stop conditions (balance decrease, single win threshold, free-games triggered), reducing the number of manual interactions needed.

Bottom bar has a stable left-to-right order: info '(i)', BET display with BET LEVEL steppers, BET MAX, SPIN, AUTO PLAY, COIN steppers, BALANCE; the status strip below always echoes BET and, after a win, WIN as text, not only as a graphic. The 10-page paytable booklet and 15-page Help screen are both continuous scrolling documents rather than paginated, so content is encountered in a fixed linear order.

Most state cues are reinforced by icon shape, printed text/numerals or position rather than color alone: control glyphs (lightning bolt, minus, plus, play-triangle, claw-arrows, hamburger lines), the WAYS banner text, the printed SCATTER and WILD labels, multiplier-tile numerals, and the REMAINING FREE SPIN counter. Residual risk: the four low-value symbols are suit-colored icons on similarly dark card backgrounds (a green diamond, a dark navy-blue club, a purple heart, a dark reddish-brown spade) — they stay distinguishable mainly by suit shape, a safe non-color cue, but contrast against the card background is low for some color-vision-deficiency profiles.

No audio-only information was observed; a Sound toggle exists in the More Settings menu for decorative music/SFX only. All game state (wins, remaining free spins, accumulated multipliers, current ways count) is conveyed through on-screen text and numerals, not sound.

Key state changes use large, high-contrast text on dark backgrounds: the free-spins count intro ('19' in large gold numerals), the win banners ('TOTAL WIN 23.91' in glowing orange), and multiplier-tile values in large chipped white/grey lettering. In the Bet Options scroll-pickers the selected row is marked by BOTH a lighter background band AND bolder/brighter text (position + weight cue, not size/color alone), which also aids low-vision users distinguishing the active value.

Large circular tap targets for all primary controls, with SPIN the largest. A keyboard alternative exists but is explicitly PC-only: Space starts a spin, press-and-hold repeats spins until released, pressing Space during a spin skips the animation, and Space activates the sole available button when only one is on screen. Auto Spin (10/30/50/80/1000 presets) reduces the number of required taps for extended play; Turbo Spin shortens each spin's duration.

Bottom control bar is consistent across base-game states: TURBO far-left, bet minus/plus flanking the large central SPIN button, AUTO to its right, hamburger menu at the far right edge; balance/bet/WIN readouts sit in a row just above the controls. The Paytable and Rules booklets are real DOM text (document.body.innerText), paginated with a fixed header and a close 'X', not OCR-only canvas text — a strong positive for screen-reader compatibility.

Jackpot panels use red (GRAND), green (MAJOR), blue-indigo (MINOR), purple (MINI) backgrounds — each also labeled by name text AND dollar amount AND corner position; no tier requires color alone to identify.

WILD (dark medallion, green WILD text), SCATTER (tiger face on red pedestal), WHEEL (green dragon medallion), WHEEL UPGRADE (gold dragon medallion) — all four have distinct subjects and shapes beyond color difference.
Royals: A blue-purple (大 character) / K red / Q pink-magenta / J green / 10 orange-red / 9 yellow-gold — each identified by distinct letter or numeral shape; color is supplementary only.
Buy buttons: BUY FREE SPINS red and BUY WHEEL BONUS green — differentiated by text label and price in addition to color; color identification not required.
SPACE and ENTER keyboard controls to start and stop spin. Autoplay available with configurable spin count. Skip Screens option auto-skips feature intro and end screens.

Win amounts, jackpot values, feature names, and Free Spins counter (FREE SPINS LEFT N) all rendered as on-screen text. Feature intro overlays use full text labels (CONGRATULATION / YOU HAVE WON / N FREE SPINS / PRESS ANYWHERE TO CONTINUE).

Top and bottom strips are not told apart by colour alone: they differ by position, by symbol family (round tiger head versus antlered dragon head) and by the paytable halves (left half tiger, right half dragon). Blue neon marks the tiger side and hot magenta pink marks the dragon side.

Medallion tiers are golden yellow (top), silver grey (middle) and salmon pink (paw and claw). Paws and claws differ from heads by silhouette, but the gold and silver heads of one family share a head shape, so the metal tone is the only difference between them; the rank stays readable from the paytable rows.
A strip being active or switched off is shown by icon shape (crossed circle when active, play triangle when off), a greyed paytable half and covering text, not only by dimming.
Wins are shown by printed amounts (TOTAL WIN ribbon and the WIN cell), a bright coloured frame around the winning strip (cyan on top, magenta at the bottom) and a lit paytable row.
No sound-only information was observed: wins, the Minimum Bet toast and ribbon messages are printed. A Sound toggle exists in the menu.

Dark night purple and indigo background with luminous neon blue and magenta accents; panels are charcoal grey-blue with white titles, grey labels and yellow highlights; balance, bet and win digits are golden yellow. Strip selection buttons at the left edge are small (about 80 px).

Spin by tapping the spin button or the game area, or with the Space key on PC (hold Space to repeat spins). Autoplay offers 10, 30, 50, 80 or 1000 spins; turbo toggle available, off by default. A first tap on a strip button during a win animation can be ignored.
The game is a Cocos canvas; only the paytable and rules text is real page text. Cabinet controls are canvas nodes.
All 5 high-value symbols identified by distinct object shape: miner portrait, crystal gem, ore cart, lantern cage, pickaxe — shape alone differentiates them without relying on color
Royals identified by letter/numeral glyph: A=purple-magenta, K=orange-amber, Q=red disc, J=ice-blue, 10=neon-lime — letter or number is the primary identifier; color is secondary
WILD symbol carries gold WILD text label; BONUS symbol carries gold BONUS text label — both are text-identified regardless of color perception

Settings and ANTE BET toggles use dual coding: thumb position (left=OFF, right=ON) in addition to grey=OFF / green=ON color; winning cells have golden-yellow glow border AND large WIN text/amount at bottom center

All audio optional: SOUND toggle in bottom bar; SETTINGS has AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX toggles. Feature triggers and win amounts shown via prominent on-screen text overlays (CONGRATULATIONS! YOU HAVE WON N FREE SPINS; WIN $X.XX); no game-critical information is audio-only

Winning cells highlighted by bright golden-yellow glow border; WIN amount in large orange-yellow text at bottom center; win classification text (e.g. HUGE!) rendered in very large 3D block letters filling the upper screen

Single large SPIN button in bottom-right area; SPACE and ENTER keyboard shortcuts start and stop the spin; AUTOPLAY supports up to 100 auto-spins with SKIP SCREENS option to bypass intro and end-round animations

Canvas-rendered game with no accessible DOM elements; all interface text (BET, CREDIT, WIN amount, feature announcements) is rendered as canvas graphics and requires an assistive overlay for screen reader access

Day/Night duality: warm orange (SUN/left side) vs cool blue (MOON/right side). Screen position (left vs right) and symbol shape (solar orb with rays vs crescent moon) provide non-color differentiation.
Gamble wheel: win sector is green (large, upper portion) and lose sector is red (smaller, bottom). Sector size is a secondary non-color cue, but is marginal for deuteranopia/protanopia users.
Settings toggles: ON state is green (right position), OFF state is grey (left position). Toggle position (left/right) is the primary non-color cue.
Bonus buy confirm/cancel: green checkmark button (confirm) vs red X button (cancel). Icon shape (checkmark vs X) fully differentiates without color.
SCATTER (circular golden coin medallion) vs WILD (large golden Egyptian god mask) differ substantially in shape. WILD text label and SCATTER text label appear in paytable.
All game rules and feature triggers displayed as on-screen text overlays. Win amounts shown numerically. No audio-only information identified from visual review.
SPACE and ENTER keyboard shortcuts start and stop the spin. All bet adjustments and feature buttons accessible via mouse click. No swipe or multi-touch controls required on desktop.

Key UI values (bet, credit, win amount, free spins left) are rendered as text on screen. Symbol identities during gameplay rely on visual recognition only; no text labels accompany symbols on the reel grid during play.
Collect symbols and the trail signs carry text labels (COLLECT, LOCK & COLLECT, WIN STEPPER, CASH MATCH, SUPER COLLECT), so green, blue, orange, purple and red identity is not colour-only.
Cashpot plaques carry the words MEGA, MAJOR, MINOR, MINI and their amounts, so red, purple, blue and green are redundant.
Royal letters A (red-orange), K (green), Q (purple) and J (magenta) differ by letter shape as well as colour.
Locked rows in Road Trip are marked by a ROAD CLOSED stop sign and a striped barrier, not by colour alone.
Mutt Cutts upgrades (red, purple, blue, green) are explained in the rules by colour name only; on screen the effect is also shown by the animation of the cash amounts affected.
Rules text is white on a dark panel, headings and numbers are yellow; readable at 1280x800.

Spin by the large round button or by the spacebar (per rules, depending on operator); a turbo button speeds up spins; autoplay offers 10, 25, 50, 75, 100 by single click; the stake window needs one click per change, no sliders.
Win amounts print as numbers in the PAID bar and on the I.O.U. paper; the rules are full text in the panel. No evidence about audio cues was recorded (sound muted in capture).

The two Mystery Duel 'VS' tiles are distinguished on the static paytable ONLY by outline color: green outline leads to the 'Wild or Dead' duel, red outline leads to the 'Multiplier Showdown' duel. Before the duel animation resolves and prints 'WILD'/'DEAD' or the two competing multiplier numbers, a color-blind player has no non-color cue to tell the two apart.
Low-value royal symbols are colored (A=red, K=gold/yellow, Q=green, J=purple/magenta) but remain identifiable by their letter glyph, not by color alone.
Settings toggle switches (Quick spin, Spacebar to spin) show state via fill color (yellow=on / dark=off) AND a checkmark glyph that only appears when on, so state is not conveyed by color alone.

No information is conveyed by audio only. Sound FX and Music are separate adjustable/mutable sliders in Settings, and all outcomes (wins, free-spins count, Buy Bonus price, duel results) are also shown as on-screen text.

Win amounts and the accompanying '<n>x BET' multiplier are printed as large, high-contrast white/yellow numerals on full-screen win splashes (BIG WIN on dark green, MEGA WIN on dark blue, TOTAL WIN on red/orange), not relying on subtle color distinctions to convey the amount.

Bet size is adjusted with small up/down triangle steppers rather than large +/- buttons (a possible small-target concern). Spacebar-to-spin is available and ON by default, and Autoplay offers a wide range of preset round counts (10 up to 1000, infinity, or a custom field) to reduce the need for repeated manual clicking.

The bottom control bar keeps a stable layout in every base-game state: info(i)/settings(gear) far left, balance and bet readouts center-left, contextual hint text center, Autoplay(A)/Spin far right. The Buy Bonus entry point (green cart icon) is always fixed top-left below the wordmark. Paytable and rules are both single, linear, vertically-scrolling panels reached via the 'i'/'?' icons, not paginated with buttons.

The red, blue and green gem symbols share a near-identical faceted kite/hexagon silhouette and are distinguished mainly by hue -- a residual risk for red-green color blindness. Mitigated because winning lines always repeat a single symbol type, so users can pattern-match the repeated icon instead of naming the exact color.
Pink/magenta heart gem and yellow/gold gem have unique silhouettes (heart shape; rounded nugget shape) and are safely distinguishable from the other gems by shape alone, not just color.
WILD/WILDWILD cells are marked with a bright gold rectangular border (shape/position cue) in addition to color, distinguishing them from plain stone cells and from the printed word 'WILD'/'WILDWILD'.
Winning cells are outlined with a gold glow (shape/position cue), not color alone; the win pay strip repeats the exact winning icon so the win is identifiable by icon-matching.
In the BUY FREE SPINS confirmation dialog, cancel vs confirm are differentiated by glyph (red circle with white X vs green circle with white checkmark), not color alone.
The ways-to-win diagram in the paytable uses a green checkmark vs a red X, a color-only cue pair, but each is also uniquely shaped (check mark vs cross), mitigating the risk.

No audio-only information observed; AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX are decorative toggles. All game state (wins, spins left, multiplier rules, feature activation) is conveyed through on-screen text and iconography.

Win amounts and free-spins counters are printed as large, high-contrast text (yellow/gold or white on a dark plaque), legible without color discrimination. Free-spins state is also signalled by a full background palette shift (teal/green cave to blue/purple ice cave), not color alone.

Large round click targets; the central SPIN button is the largest. SPACE and ENTER keys also start/stop a spin (keyboard-operable). AUTOPLAY and BUY FREE SPINS reduce the number of clicks required for repeated play.

Stable control positions across all base-game screens: hamburger-menu and sound icons far-left, 'i' info button beside them, bet -/+ around the central SPIN button, AUTOPLAY below SPIN, BUY FREE SPINS plaque fixed at upper-left. Wild (black cat) and Scatter (rainbow butterfly) carry unique illustrated identity plus printed 'WILD'/'SCATTER' text labels, not dependent on color
Royal symbols A, K, Q, J, 10 are distinguished primarily by the printed letter/number glyph (red A, blue K, orange/gold Q, green J, purple/magenta 10) - color is a secondary cue only
Settings toggle switches (Battery Saver, Ambient Music, Sound FX) show both switch position (left=off/right=on) and fill color (grey=off/green=on), redundant for color-vision-deficient users
All bonus-critical information (Free Spins trigger, insect pick reveals, spins-left/multiplier counters, win totals) is duplicated in on-screen text; no feature is audio-only
All HUD text (credit, bet, win, free spins left, multiplier) rendered in high-contrast white/orange/gold lettering on a dark semi-transparent bottom bar
Turbo Spin can be triggered by holding the SPACE key as an alternative to precise mouse clicks; Autoplay 'SKIP SCREENS' option auto-skips feature intro/end screens to reduce required clicks
Same-value dwarves (red/blue/gold hat-and-robe, all paying 5=12x/4=3.2x/3=0.8x) are distinguished by the held item's shape: beer glass, gold pot, or teacup, not color alone.
Settings menu toggles show on/off via handle position (left=off, right=on) in addition to grey/green track color.
Autoplay checkboxes show a checked state via a white checkmark glyph, not fill color alone.
The 25 payline icons in the paytable are individually numbered 1-25 rather than relying on their distinct colors.
Paytable navigation controls (previous/close/next) are differentiated by triangle/X shape, not color.

No audio-only information observed; Ambient Music and Sound FX are separately toggleable and purely decorative. All game state (win amounts, free spins remaining, win-tier callouts) is conveyed via on-screen text and numerals.
Large round click targets for the menu, sound, info, spin, and bet +/- buttons.
SPACE key confirmed to trigger turbo spin; Autoplay lets a player set up to 100 spins with a single button press, with a Skip Screens option reducing intro/end-screen interrupts.

Stable control layout across all screens: menu+sound stacked bottom-left, info button beside them, CREDIT/BET left-of-center, SPIN centered with bet +/- flanking it, Autoplay directly beneath Spin. The info booklet is a linear 6-page sequence with a persistent 'Page n/6' indicator.
SCATTER METER tier badges use color (green/blue/orange-bronze/silver/gold) but each badge also shows the text label BRONZE/SILVER/GOLD and a dollar amount — non-color reinforcement present
BUY FEATURE confirm/cancel buttons differ in both color (red vs green) AND icon shape (X vs checkmark) — accessible to all colorblind types
Royal symbols A/K/Q/J/10/9 use distinct colors (golden-orange/red-orange/bright green/teal/purple/violet) but each is also identified by its letter or numeral glyph

All payout amounts, scatter awards, win amounts, and game rules shown as on-screen text. AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX can be independently toggled off in System Settings
WIN amount and BUY FEATURE price in large bold gold text on dark background; CREDIT/BET in large cyan text; moderate-to-good contrast. EXTRA CHANCE OF BONUS toggle label is small — zoom recommended
Reel symbols approximately 145x115px at 1280x800 desktop; paytable icons smaller (~80x80px). Rules text is medium-size white on dark overlay — readable
SPACE/ENTER start/stop spin; hold SPACE for TURBO SPIN (hold-based — may be difficult for some users). QUICK SPIN mode provides middle option. Autoplay up to 100 spins with SKIP SCREENS option

No information is conveyed by audio alone; Settings exposes independent Music and Sound FX toggles, and all game-state changes (wins, feature triggers, counters, RTP, rules) are shown as on-screen text/graphics.

Two hanging-sign BUY buttons plus the main spin button are large click targets; Spacebar can trigger spin (on by default); autoplay offers preset round counts up to 1000 or unlimited to reduce repeated clicks; Buy Bonus removes the need to spin repeatedly to reach a feature.

Control layout is stable across screens: info/settings bottom-left, bet field with stepper arrows center-left, win/line readouts center, autoplay and spin bottom-right. Paytable and rules are linear, drag-scroll single-column panels (no click-through pagination) reached via a 3-icon side rail (Payments/History-link/Help).

Most functional cues are shape- or text-based rather than color-only: toggle switches show handle position, checkboxes show a check glyph, nav arrows are distinguished by triangle direction vs. an X. No audio-only information was observed; ambient music and sound effects are independent on/off toggles in system settings (both default off). Game state (win amounts, free spins remaining, multipliers, active bet mode) is always conveyed as on-screen text/numerals in addition to any sound effect.

Win amounts, multiplier badges and the free-spins-left counter are printed as large white numerals with a black outline directly on screen, legible without color discrimination. CREDIT/BET readouts are high-contrast orange/yellow text on a dark bar, and the max-win/title text on the promo screen is large high-contrast text.

Large circular click targets for spin/menu/sound/info. SPACE and ENTER can start/stop spins from the keyboard (holding SPACE engages Turbo Spin), reducing the need for precise clicks. Autoplay, with an adjustable spin count and a skip-screens option, reduces the number of required interactions for repeated play.

Control positions are stable across the whole session: menu+sound stacked bottom-far-left, a separate info button just to their right, bet -/+ flanking the central spin button, autoplay directly beneath spin.
