All game outcomes shown as text. Win amount and payline detail displayed visually in bottom bar. No audio-only state signals. Sound effects and ambient music are individually toggleable (SOUND FX and AMBIENT MUSIC toggles in SYSTEM SETTINGS, plus speaker icon in main bar). Game fully playable with sound off.

Largest interactive element is the SPIN button (round circle, center-right of bottom bar). SPACE and ENTER keyboard shortcuts start and stop the spin. AUTOPLAY reduces required click frequency (up to 100 auto-spins). Bet adjustment via two round buttons flanking SPIN. All targets are round buttons with generous touch area.

5x3 reel grid, 15 cells. Fixed bottom bar layout (left to right): settings button, info button, sound button, CREDIT/BET display, HOLD SPACE hint, SPIN button, bet minus/plus, AUTOPLAY button. Win shown as 'WIN $X.XX' center bottom bar with sub-label 'LINE N PAYS $X.XX'. 5-page game rules booklet navigated by left/right triangle buttons; each page has a header (GAME RULES / HOW TO PLAY / SETTINGS MENU / AUTOPLAY).

Cherry (deep red, two round globes on Y-stem) vs Strawberry (bright red, single heart-shaped body with seed surface and leafy cap): shapes fully distinguish both red-colored fruits without relying on color. Plum (purple-blue with orange pit) vs other round fruits: half-cut face and color combination is unique.

Watermelon: green exterior may appear olive/yellow-brown to red-green colorblind users; red flesh interior similarly muted. Shape (round fruit body plus angled wedge slice) is unique among all symbols and sufficient for identification. Seven (pink/magenta) is the only numeral — shape fully distinct from all fruit symbols.

Multiplier Wheel sectors are color-coded (confirmed: red=100x, orange=5x, green=25x; remaining sectors include pink/magenta and purple tones). Bold yellow multiplier text is printed on each sector — color is not required to read the wheel result. All multiplier values are text-readable.

AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX can be toggled off independently in System Settings. All game state is shown as on-screen text: WIN $X.XX in bottom bar, CREDIT and BET labels, AUTO SPINS LEFT counter. MULTIPLIER WHEEL trigger is visually indicated by wheel glowing on-screen. No information is audio-only.

Symbols are very large (approximately 220x290 px each at 1280x800 desktop viewport) and fill nearly the full reel cell. WIN amount displayed in large bold gold text in the center bottom bar. Paytable uses white text on near-black background with high contrast. Spin button is approximately 80px diameter.

SPACE or ENTER key starts and stops the spin (confirmed in rules). HOLD SPACE activates Turbo Spin. Autoplay available with configurable spin count via slider; TURBO SPIN, QUICK SPIN and SKIP SCREENS options reduce required interactions. All play controls are in the bottom bar with large spin button.

CREDIT and BET labels are explicit text elements. WIN $X.XX shown as text in bottom bar. All 5 pages of GAME RULES are text-panel content. HOW TO PLAY page describes all UI controls in text. Reel spin outcomes are not announced by text beyond the win amount display.

The six paying symbols differ by shape (person, pot, blade, three coin stacks of decreasing height). The coin stacks are close in shape and differ by metal tone (yellow-gold, grey-blue, copper-brown) and by engraved mark, so rely on the marks and paytable order.
Prize Wheel symbol sectors are blue 1x, green 2x, red 5x, and yellow with purple BONUS; every sector also prints its value as text.

Big wheel tiles are blue-grey 2x, olive-green 4x, red-orange 10x, bright yellow DOUBLE in purple letters; used tiles are dark brown-black with a skull face. Each tile prints its value as text, and used tiles carry a skull as well as a dark colour.
The selected Auto Spin value (10, 30, 50, 80, 1000) is shown only by pill shading and digit colour (filled dark-teal pill with mint digits); no checkmark or text marks it.
A Sound control in the menu row toggles sound ON or OFF; wins and the bonus are also shown as text banners and on-screen amounts. Sound content cannot be judged from still frames.

Wins are announced by text (Total Win banner and the WIN amount in the centre HUD pill), not only by glow; winning symbols get a gold frame while others are dimmed, and the winning line number appears as a golden digit on the reel edge.

HUD numbers are bright mint-turquoise on dark brown pills; panels use white text on dark charcoal-blue with mint-turquoise highlights and a filled mint confirm button. The selected Bet Options row is the middle row with larger white digits.

Space key starts a spin, holding Space keeps spinning, pressing Space during a spin skips the reel animation (PC version). Turbo Spin button and Auto Spin (10, 30, 50, 80, 1000) are available; tapping the game area during a spin stops the reels.
Paytable and Rules panels are real DOM text; the game itself is drawn on a canvas. The only start action on the splash is a button with the readable text GET STARTED.
Line-count badge (orange) and multiplier badge (blue) are both paired with explicit printed numerals ('5 LINES'/'27 LINES', 'x1'/'x2'), so colour is not load-bearing.
The winning payline is drawn as a bright green trace AND named in text (e.g. 'Line 5 pays'), so it can be identified without relying on colour.
Base-game (green) vs bonus-game (orange) payline diagrams in the paytable booklet are additionally distinguished by 'Base Game'/'Bonus Game' text headings and individual 'Line N' labels.
Risk Game cards use standard red/black pip colouring, but each card also shows a printed rank index (e.g. '8', '7', '10') readable without colour perception.
No information is conveyed only through audio; Music and Sound FX toggles are purely decorative — win banners, balance changes and feature states are all also shown as on-screen text/graphics.
Win banners ('BIG WIN'/'MEGA WIN'/'TOTAL WIN') are large high-contrast cream ribbons with dark red bold text outlined in gold over a dark maroon plaque, plus the numeric amount printed beneath.

Bet is adjusted with a simple two-button (+/-) stepper to a hard floor of 0.10 FUN and ceiling of 50.00 FUN; Spin is one large round target; Spacebar can substitute for clicking Spin (on by default); Quick Spin is disabled in this build/license.

Control layout is stable across states (info/settings bottom-left, balance/bet centre, spin/autospin bottom-right); post-win Collect/Gamble icons appear in that same bottom-right slot only after a win resolves. The paytable/rules panel is a continuous 16-page scroll with no 'Page N/M' indicator, so scroll position needs to be announced explicitly.

Feature type is stated explicitly in text ('FREE SPINS' vs 'SUPER FREE SPI[NS]') in addition to a green vs dark red/maroon background tint; Settings toggle switches use handle position (left=off, right=on) plus grey/green color; card-rank symbols (A red/orange, K green, Q purple/magenta) are distinguished by the printed letter glyph, not only color.

Multiplier and Free-Spins-Left counters are printed as plain numbers, not conveyed by color; volatility (5 of 5 lightning bolts) is conveyed by icon COUNT, not color; info-booklet nav controls use shape (left/right triangle, X) rather than color alone.

No audio-only information observed; AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX are separately toggleable and appear decorative; all game state (wins, spins left, multiplier, feature triggers) is conveyed visually via on-screen text.
Win amounts, spin counts and multiplier values are shown as large high-contrast gold/white text on dark backgrounds throughout (win screens, free-spins side panels, preview).

Large round click targets; the central SPIN button is the largest element; SPACE/ENTER also spin (keyboard-operable); autoplay (selectable spin count, default 100) and a 'skip screens' toggle reduce the number of clicks needed per session.

Control layout is stable across all screens: menu+sound stacked far-left, info 'i' button beside them, bet +/- around the central spin button, autoplay below spin, BUY FREE SPINS panel fixed left of the reels; the info booklet is a linear 7-page sequence with an explicit 'Page N/7' indicator on every page.
CASHOUT is dark grey when inactive and bright yellow with black text when active, and only the active button carries the amount in text (for example $10.90).
The green round button shows a white triangle when idle and the white word GO during a round, so the state is told by symbol and not only by colour.
The four Buy Bonus cards (deep blue, purple, olive gold, dark red) are duplicated by the tier name, the printed cap number, the free game count and the number of lit lightning icons from one to four.
Win size is told by the banner text WIN or MEGA WIN and by figures, not only by colour.
Selected autoplay presets get a green outline and green digit, and the slider value is also printed as a number at the right.
No on-screen cue depends on sound alone; the Sound and Music toggles were both off in the captured session.
Ladder numbers are small white italic digits with a dark-blue outline over a busy foliage background; the current step is also shown by the golden hard-hat marker and by the CASHOUT amount in text.

Round actions need one click each (play, GO, CASHOUT); the Space key can drive the round when the menu toggle is on. Free games and autoplay need no input; autoplay runs 10 to 200 rounds with a preset cash-out step.
Rules and menu text live in an HTML layer, but the ladder, the centre multiplier label and the win banners are drawn pictures; the CASHOUT amount is real button text.

Active multiplier shell is shown by glow, brighter fill and size change AND by the number printed on the shell; base game shells are pale blue with the active one glowing hot pink-red and gold digits, free spins shells are golden with the active one glowing orange-red
Letters A (red), K (violet), Q (teal green), J (bright blue) are told apart by letter shape; colour is redundant. Animals and objects differ by silhouette
Winning cells in free spins are marked by an orange glowing frame in addition to the amount on the ribbon
No mandatory audio cue: wins, free spins entry and the BIG WIN banner are shown visually with text; a Sound toggle is in the menu
Portrait play field with large round controls at the bottom; paytable payout numbers are gold-yellow with symbol counts in white on dark grey panels, headings gold-yellow on dark charcoal-navy
Disabled controls (minus at minimum bet, plus, Auto and minus during a spin) are only dimmed, with no text label
Free spins transition shows a bright full-screen flash and a pearl-bubble swirl; ribbon tip texts scroll continuously
Auto Spin with 10, 30, 50, 80 or 1000 spins, Turbo Spin toggle, holding Space repeats spins, tap on the field stops the reels; controls are large round targets
Paytable and Rules panels are real DOM text and readable by a screen reader; reels and multiplier shells are canvas graphics with no observed text alternative

WILD multiplier value and SCATTER identity are always given as printed text/portrait art, not colour alone; paytable navigation arrows are shape-differentiated (triangle/cross/triangle); toggle switches use handle position (left=off/right=on) in addition to on/off colour.

Buy-feature buttons carry a full text label and price, not colour alone. Residual risk: the purple BUY FREE SPINS/BUY SUPER FREE SPINS buttons, the purple ante panel and the magenta SCATTER card share a similar purple/magenta hue family, but each carries distinguishing text or art so identification does not depend on colour alone.

No audio-only information was observed; Ambient Music and Sound FX are purely decorative toggles in Settings. All game state (win amounts, spins remaining, wild multipliers, feature triggers) is conveyed through on-screen text and numerals.
Free-spins-awarded count and round win totals are shown as large gold digits on a dark red ribbon plaque ('CONGRATULATIONS / YOU HAVE WON') — high-contrast, legible without colour discrimination.

Large round click targets, with the central SPIN button the largest single target; SPACE/ENTER also start/stop spins and holding SPACE triggers turbo, giving a keyboard-only path; Autoplay with a configurable spin count plus a Skip Screens option reduces clicks needed for extended play.

Control positions are stable on every screen: menu/sound/info icons bottom-left; bet -/+ around the central SPIN button; AUTOPLAY below/right of SPIN; BUY FREE SPINS / BUY SUPER FREE SPINS / ANTE panel stacked top-left in base game; the rules booklet is a fixed 7-page linear sequence with identical previous/close/next + 'Page n/7' navigation on every page.
Card ranks are told apart by letter shape (A, K, Q), not only by colour: purple A, blue K, teal Q on cream tiles.
Gold symbols have a golden-yellow tile with sparkle; Wild is a purple tile with the word WILD; Scatter is a crown on a red-orange tile with the word SCATTER.
Multipliers, win amounts, balance and bet are printed as digits; the selected row in Bet Options is shown by a darker pill and larger whiter digits.
Win amounts, multiplier digits, free-spin counter and total win are shown as text; no required information is sound-only in the captured frames.
Menus are dark slate grey panels with white titles, grey body text and tan values; the start button is a red button labelled GET STARTED.
One large Spin button; Space starts a spin on PC and hold Space keeps spinning; Auto Spin offers 10, 30, 50, 80, 1000; Turbo Spin toggle; Max Bet button sets size and level to maximum.
Game is drawn on a canvas; the player menu items (Sound, Paytable, Rules, History, Quit) have text labels, and wins, balance and bet are printed as digits.

Low-value royals differentiated by letter/numeral shape as well as color: A red/orange, K cyan/turquoise, Q magenta/pink, J green, 10 purple/violet, 9 magenta/pink with teal accents. WILD (blue/white crystal shard) and FREYA SUPER SYMBOL (gold winged crown on dark red) differ by distinct icon art/shape, not only card color.

Toggle state shown by knob position (left = off, right = on) in addition to green-when-on fill. Spin button changes glyph shape (double-arrow idle vs square-with-red-outline active) rather than relying on color alone. Ways-to-win diagram pairs a checkmark/X glyph with green/red coloring.

No information is conveyed by audio alone: wins, multiplier, free-spins-left and feature triggers are always also shown as on-screen text/numerals; AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX are independently togglable.

Volatility indicator uses 5 lightning-bolt icons whose fill contrast could be less distinct for some viewers; mitigated by the accompanying explicit 'High volatility' text label (the bolt count itself conflicts with the text and should not be read as 'very high').

The end-of-round total is a rolling count-up animation: two captured frames of the same 'CONGRATULATIONS' overlay showed different transient CREDIT values ($99,814.00, then $99,942.00) before settling at $99,954.60 on the following win screen — readers should rely on the final settled value, not an intermediate animation frame.

SPACE and ENTER provide keyboard alternatives to clicking SPIN; holding SPACE engages turbo spin; Autoplay (configurable spin count, SKIP SCREENS option) reduces the number of discrete actions needed for repetitive play. All primary controls are large circular/rounded targets.

The collect-vs-replay choice, when randomly offered at 50x-80x total bet Free Spins wins, requires the player to make a decision on a temporary on-screen prompt; its exact timing/visual design was not captured (did not appear during the recorded round), so any time-limit on the decision window is not confirmed from screenshots.

Info/rules booklet is a strictly linear 8-page sequence navigable with only two glyphs (left/right triangle) plus a distinct close (X); bottom-left (menu/sound/info) and bottom-right (bet-/spin/bet+/autoplay) control clusters hold stable positions across every screen, suitable for simple sequential navigation instructions.
The expanded reel-3 WILD is orange/gold flaming letters literally spelling 'WILD' on a black tile - identified by shape and text, not color alone.

Toggle switches (settings, autoplay checkboxes) show state by BOTH knob position and track color: dark-grey track/left position = off, green track/right position (or white checkmark on green fill) = on.

The four Free Spins tiers are distinguished by distinct background artwork (starry sky / city-at-night / daytime skyline / night skyline with search-lights) and explicit printed spin-count and multiplier numbers, not by color alone.
One residual color-only cue: disabled bet '+'/'-' buttons at the min/max bet limits are signalled mainly by reduced brightness/contrast rather than an alternate icon or text state.

No audio-only information identified; all outcomes (spins, wins, feature triggers and results) are conveyed through on-screen text and animation. Sound/music are independently togglable via SOUND FX and AMBIENT MUSIC switches in the settings menu.

Palette overview in words: dim cool blue-green jungle background in the base game; sepia dark-brown film-strip cell borders framing every symbol; gold/tan title wordmark and gold royal-letter symbols (A/K/Q/J/10); orange-red flaming expanding WILD and gorilla eyes; warm orange-to-pink sunset ocean background with a white ship silhouette during Free Spins.

All primary controls (SPIN, bet +/-, AUTOPLAY, menu/sound/info) are large circular or pill-shaped touch targets. Autoplay offers a configurable spin count plus a 'Skip Screens' option, reducing manual interactions; no time-limited click windows observed, win/summary screens wait for 'PRESS ANYWHERE TO CONTINUE'.

Control positions are stable across the whole session: menu+sound stacked bottom-left, a separate 'i' info button beside them, CREDIT/BET labels left-of-center, bet -/SPIN/bet+ centered-right, AUTOPLAY beneath SPIN. The 7-page rules booklet is a strictly linear sequence with left-triangle/X/right-triangle navigation and an explicit 'Page N/7' readout on every page.
Reels 3 and 4 (the only reels that can host Wild) are marked by a purple frame AND a permanent 'WILD / WILD' text plate above them, not by color alone

Round-multiplier and free-spins medal tokens (x1/x2/x3/x5 or the medal ladder) show a printed number and a highlight ring plus a fixed left-to-right position, not color alone; the active Paytable/Rules menu tab also differs by icon and label, not just its purple fill
The four card-suit symbols (Spade, Heart, Club, Diamond) are differentiated by suit glyph shape, not color alone, though each also sits on a distinct tinted tile
No audio-only information; sound is a togglable accessory and all game state (wins, remaining free spins, multiplier tier, bet amount) is conveyed as on-screen text and numerals
Win, total-win and max-win callouts (e.g. 'WIN 2.58', 'TOTAL WIN 18.75', '5000X') are large, high-contrast numerals (pink/gold on a dark background), legible without fine color discrimination
Large circular tap targets for Spin/Autoplay/Turbo/+/-; on PC, the Space key can start a spin, be held to spin continuously, skip the spin animation, or activate the sole available on-screen button

A fixed 5-icon bottom menu (Sound/Paytable/Rules/History/Quit) appears on every info panel; Paytable (10 pages) and Rules (12 pages) are single scrolling documents reached by drag, with no next/prev buttons or page counter

BONUS FEATURE state is signalled by a full background palette shift from daytime blue sky to night-time navy sky, not just a text label; respin-lives hearts differ in fill (red=remaining) vs dim/outline (spent), not color alone

Multiplier and win values are shown as explicit numbers ('3X MULTIPLIER', dollar totals) rather than color alone; Buy Bonus decline/confirm buttons use a red X vs a green checkmark shape; info-booklet nav uses left-triangle/X/right-triangle shapes, not color coding

No audio-only information observed on any screen; all game state (bet, credit, win, respins-left via hearts, multiplier) is conveyed via on-screen text/icons, and SOUND/AMBIENT MUSIC toggles are clearly labelled as decorative audio controls
CREDIT is shown in blue/cyan text and BET in yellow text, each with its own text label; the WIN amount is displayed in large high-contrast cyan text on a dark background

Large round click targets with the SPIN button as the largest on the base-game screen; SPACE/ENTER are spin hotkeys usable without a mouse, holding SPACE engages turbo spin; Autoplay offers an adjustable spin-count slider (default 100) to reduce required interactions

Stable control layout across every screen (menu/sound/info grouped bottom-left, bet +/- flanking SPIN, Autoplay below SPIN); the 8-page info booklet is strictly linear (prev/close/next only) with an explicit 'Page N/8' readout on every page

Pickaxe tiers differ by icon silhouette plus a printed durability number, not color alone; block tiers use distinct pixel-art rock/ore/gem textures, not flat color alone; the BONUS scatter carries the printed word 'BONUS'. Residual risk: the 5-gem 'chance meter' on purchase cards relies on red-vs-gray fill with no numeric label, and the Extra Chance/turbo 'on' states lean on green fill (both also carry position/label-text cues).

Settings has separate Music and Sound toggles, implying audio feedback (spin, block-break, chest-open sounds) not mirrored by a distinct on-screen animation beyond pickaxes visibly falling and blocks visibly changing. Core game-state info (balance, bet, win amount, bonus purchase cost, bet history, provably-fair data) is otherwise fully presented as on-screen text.

Settings toggles (Music/Sound) show on/off state by the physical position of the round knob within the track (left=off, right=on), readable without color discrimination. The provider loading splash uses high-contrast white/yellow text and logo on a near-black background.

Primary interactions use large circular/square touch targets (SPIN, bet +/-, BUY BONUS). Autoplay is not available in this build (the control is present but confirmed DOM-disabled), so there is no automated-spin fallback beyond the turbo/quick-spin speed toggle, which only speeds up individual spins rather than removing the need to click repeatedly.

Control layout is stable and predictable: settings gear bottom-left, balance next to it, win/prompt text center, bet stepper and BUY BONUS/Extra Chance controls center-right, SPIN large and centered-right, disabled autoplay/turbo stacked to its right, hamburger menu top-right. The 'How to play?' content is one continuous scroll, not paginated; the separate 'Game rules' (bet limits) dialog is short and self-contained.

Block types are distinguished by colour AND distinct pixel-texture pattern (grass-cap Dirt, plain mottled grey Stone, red-speckled Ore, solid yellow Gold, cyan-streaked Diamonds, near-black Obsidian) -- identifiable by pattern alone. The bonus round's Nether-cave reskin changes only the palette, not the block shapes/patterns.
Pickaxe durability is shown as a printed white number badge, not colour; the BONUS scatter is identified by its unique eye/banner shape and the printed word 'BONUS', not colour alone.
Sound and Music are independent toggles in settings; win/loss state is always also shown as printed text ('WIN: $X' / 'WIN: $0'), not conveyed by audio alone.
Monetary values, bet limits, and feature counters (Total Win, Spins Left) are printed as large, high-contrast on-screen text rather than conveyed only through animation or colour.

Bet amount is adjustable via discrete -/+ step buttons rather than dragging; autoplay offers fixed count presets from 5 up to 1000 plus an infinity option, and a 'Space to spin & go' keyboard shortcut is available as an alternative to clicking SPIN.

Win and loss are not carried by colour alone: the banner text differs (WIN! versus OOPS....) and the figures differ (x1.07 with a dollar payout versus x0 with $ 0.00), although the multiplier is golden yellow on a win and coral red on a loss.

Stars and bombs differ by shape: a faceted golden five-point star with an amber glow versus a round purple cartoon bomb with yellow spots, cyan rim light and a twisted rope fuse. Closed cells are sky blue with a dark blue question mark.

The selected bomb preset is a filled blue button against dark buttons, and the current ladder step has a blue outline and a blue label. An invalid bet is outlined in coral red and also explained by a toast with a warning triangle icon and text.
Sound and Music toggles in the burger menu (both on by default). All results are also printed as text: win or loss banner, Cash out amount on the button, and the My bet history table.

Dark navy page background with white bold text; side panel and opened cells in dark slate grey-blue; the lime green Play / Cash out button and the sky blue closed cells stand out against it. The multiplier ladder strip along the bottom is cut off at the right edge and shows about 8 steps.
Single click per action, no hold or drag needed. MIN and MAX buttons, four quick-bet chips (2, 3, 8, 20) and five bomb buttons reduce typing.
Outcomes are text in the interface (banner, Cash out amount, history rows with date, bet, multiplier and win). Autoplay and auto cash out are absent, so every step is a manual click on a cell.

Gems and mines differ by shape, not only by colour: a faceted gem versus a round bomb with a lit fuse. The state of the round is carried by the word on the action button (BET / CANCEL / CASHOUT / START AUTOBET) as well as by its colour, so no state is signalled by colour alone.

A single Sound Effects switch in Settings; the game is fully playable muted. The win amount and the multiplier are printed on the result panel, and the running cashout value is printed on the action button itself.

White text on a very dark navy background; the key numbers (gems left, mine risk, opened count, current cashout) are repeated in a fixed strip under the controls, and a fullscreen switch is available in the top bar.

Tiles are large 84x84 targets in a regular 5x5 grid. Hotkeys remove precise pointing entirely: Space bets, cashes out and stops autoplay, R opens a random tile. Auto mode plays whole series of up to 100 rounds without any clicking.

The whole game is DOM rather than canvas: buttons carry names (Mute sound, Enter fullscreen, Settings, Auto, BET, min, max), and the balance, the bet, the multiplier ladder and the counters are readable as text.

Outcomes are distinguished by SHAPE, not only colour: a safe tile shows a cut diamond, an unsafe one a bomb with a spark. The primary button changes its WORD (Start Game / Cancel / Cash Out) rather than only its colour.
Sound is decorative (single volume slider in settings); no information is audio-only.

The whole interface is real DOM text (no canvas), so browser zoom and text scaling work. Key readouts - balance, bet, multiplier ladder, gems left, mine risk %, opened tiles - are numeric text, not gauges.
No timed reaction is required: the round waits for the player. Autoplay with preselected tiles removes repetitive clicking entirely.
Controls are DOM elements with visible text labels; the round state is announced by the button text. No audio cue is required to play: the outcome is visible.

The currently selectable row of tiles is a lighter yellow-green shade versus the darker saturated green of the rest of the field, but position reinforces it: the highlighted row always sits directly next to the already-resolved (safe) tiles, so progress can be tracked by which row is nearest the walked path rather than by hue alone.
A revealed safe tile changes from grass texture to bare dirt texture and gets a red flag on a white/cream post — the texture change, not the flag's red color, is what marks it as safe.

A revealed mine tile is a dark grey/near-black spherical bomb model with a light tan/beige twisted-rope fuse standing upright, a strongly distinct 3D shape versus the flat green grass tiles and the flag marker, so the mine/safe distinction does not rely on color at all.

The multiplier ladder tags are red pills with white text; the printed numeric value is the primary information carrier (readable independent of color), and their left-to-right ascending order along the platform edge is a second, non-color cue to which value belongs to which row depth.

Most affordances are non-color: royal letters A/K/Q/J are distinguished by their letter glyph even though each has a different color (A=teal/cyan, K=magenta/pink, Q=purple, J=green); miner/gold cart/pickaxe/BONUS are distinct icon art; toggle switches show on/off by handle position as well as track color (white=off, green=on); dialog confirm/cancel use checkmark/X glyphs as well as green/red. The Nugget level color-coding (bronze=pink rock, silver=white/grey rock, gold=yellow, diamond=not observed) relies partly on hue, but the level/points and payout amount are always also shown as text.

No audio-only information observed; SOUND FX and AMBIENT MUSIC toggles are purely atmospheric. All game state (win amounts, spins left, nugget levels/points, bet/credit) is conveyed through on-screen text and numbers.

Large round click targets, with the central SPIN button the largest. SPACE/ENTER also start/stop a spin (keyboard-operable). Autoplay with a configurable spin count (up to at least 100) reduces required manual actions.

Stable control layout across all screens: hamburger-menu and sound icons bottom-far-left, 'i' info button beside them, bet -/+ around the central SPIN button, AUTOPLAY pill below SPIN. The rules booklet is a strictly linear 7-page sequence (left/right triangle navigation, X to close), each page labeled 'Page n/7'.

Jackpot tiers are labeled by text word (MINI in green, MAJOR in cyan/blue, MEGA in golden-yellow) as well as color, so tier identity does not depend on color perception - though the labels are small, so a glance-only reader could momentarily conflate MINI/MAJOR without reading the word.

All ten paying symbols are distinct fruit/object shapes (bell, horseshoe, four different fruits, cherries) rather than color-coded tokens; the two top-tier symbols (Bell and Wild) are told apart by shape and by the presence/absence of the character portrait, not by hue.
Side-bet toggle switches print explicit 'OFF'/'ON' text and move the round handle to the opposite end of the track, not color alone.

The three game modes have distinguishable backgrounds by pattern and marquee text as well as hue: base game is a deep magenta/purple glow, Free Spins shifts to dark indigo/night-sky purple with white star sparkles, Disco Ball Respin shifts to warm amber/orange dot-matrix glow. Magenta/indigo/amber can look similar under some color-blindness types, so the on-screen mode name and background pattern are the reliable cue, not hue alone.

No information is conveyed by sound alone: Music and Sound FX are independently togglable in Settings; win amounts, spins-remaining counters, feature triggers and jackpot values are all shown as on-screen text/numbers.
Max-win badge and 'CLICK TO START' button use high-contrast yellow-on-dark 3-D lettering; the balance/bet readout is white/grey text on the dark stage, legible without color reliance.

Primary actions (Spin, Buy Bonus/Chance tickets, feature Buy buttons) are large single-click targets; Spacebar can substitute for the Spin click. Autoplay offers 8 preset round counts (10 to 1000) plus an infinite option, reducing the number of required clicks for extended play.

Bottom HUD control positions are stable across states: info(i) and settings(gear) far left, balance/bet readout center-left, autoplay(A) and Spin far right - a screen reader relying on position/labels can navigate consistently.

Verified in play: the jackpot rule text reads 'x20/x100/x1000 of the total bet', but with a side bet active the meters track only the BASE bet, not the inflated total bet - with both Chance x2.5 toggles ON the Total bet field read 0.32 FUN while Mini/Major/Mega stayed at 4.00/20.00/200.00 (x20/x100/x1000 of the 0.20 base). A user who applies the printed rule literally to the announced Total bet would overstate every jackpot value by 60%; the live meter numbers must be trusted over the rule wording whenever a side bet is on.

Two different payout bases coexist and are told apart only by the accompanying text label, not by any distinct sound or tactile cue: line wins are announced as 'Line N pays' and equal the paytable figure x the bet-per-line (total bet / 25), while jackpot wins are announced via the MINI/MAJOR/MEGA marquee labels and equal x20/x100/x1000 of the TOTAL bet. The number alone does not reveal which basis produced it - the label must be read together with the number.
Line diagrams in the paytable show payline paths only as green-highlighted cells against grey cells, with no numeric or textual encoding of the exact shape beyond the 'Line N' label.

Star (gold on blue) and Seven (red) are distinguished by shape (five-point star vs numeral '7') and badge shape, not color alone; Grape (purple) and Plum (blue-violet) differ by shape (cluster of berries vs two single ovoid fruits); Cherry and Watermelon share red tones but differ sharply in shape/size.
The win highlight is a gold outline/glow around winning symbol cells (border/shape-based), not a color-fill change of the cell background.
No information is conveyed by sound alone; Music and Sound FX are togglable independently; win/feature state (Respins counter, Win/Total win amounts, Last win) is always shown as on-screen text.

Checkbox state shown by a white checkmark glyph inside the box, not color alone; slider position (not color) conveys volume level; all bottom-bar controls are white glyphs on dark circles (shape-based icons: 'i', gear, 'A', double-arrow).

Two large round primary targets (Spin bottom-right, Info/Settings bottom-left); bet adjustment uses small up/down triangle arrows requiring finer motor control; Spacebar can substitute for clicking Spin; Autoplay with fixed round counts (10 up to 1000, or unlimited) reduces manual actions needed.

Control layout stable across all screens: info and settings buttons bottom-left, balance/bet fields center-left, status text center, autoplay and spin buttons bottom-right; the info/paytable panel is a single scrollable document with 3 sub-sections (Paytable / History-RTP [non-functional in this demo] / Rules) selectable via 3 icons at the panel's left edge.
Winning paylines are marked redundantly: a bright green numeric tag, a gold connecting line across the winning cells, and text naming the line ('Line N pays') — color is never the only cue for a win
Wild is distinguishable from every fruit/number symbol by shape (a full human figure spanning the reel) and by an animated golden glow around an expanded Wild reel, not by color alone

Each regular symbol has a distinct shape (star points, numeral 7, melon wedge, grape cluster, paired plums, round orange, tapered lemon, cherry pair) in addition to color, so shape alone distinguishes the full symbol set

All game-state information (bet, wins, feature counters, RTP, rules) is shown as on-screen text; Music and Sound FX are independently toggleable/mutable in Settings, and a master speaker icon also controls audio, so the game is fully playable with sound off

Christmas palette: dark magenta-to-purple background with white snowflakes; gold metallic reel frame overlaid with a red-and-white candy-cane stripe; deep maroon/burgundy bottom control bar; bright yellow wordmark with a red outline and gold cursive 'X-mas Edition' subtitle; green pine branch and red gift box with gold ribbon as corner decorations; Wild's Santa costume is red with white fur trim and gold accents
Checkbox states in the Settings and Autospin panels use a filled black checkmark glyph inside an outlined box (shape-based on/off state), not a color-only toggle

All actions are pointer/click based (bet ladder, spin, autospin, settings); one keyboard alternative is documented: Spacebar can replace clicking the Spin button (toggle in Settings, checked by default)

All paylines pay both left-to-right and right-to-left on consecutive reels ('All symbols pay both left to right and right to left on consecutive reels of an active payline'); on the captured win screen the winning grape combination lights up reels 3-4-5, not starting at reel 1 — without the both-ways rule, a description of 'reels 3, 4, 5 lit up' would sound like a malformed win

Recommend announcing, per spin result, the bet amount, each per-line win with its line number, and the round total as separate values; also an explicit announcement when Expanded Wild / Respin triggers, currently conveyed only via a large graphic banner reading '1 RESPIN'
Wild-Frame cells are marked with a gold BORDER around the cell in addition to any color shift, so the state reads without color perception.
Paying lines are always labelled with text ('Line N pays'), never color alone; free-spins progress shows both a heart-shaped progress bar and a numeric 'n/10' counter.

The 10-heart progress bar's fill color changes meaning by context (purple/violet during the base-game Wild-Frame cycle vs red/crimson during Free Spins) with no color-independent label on the bar itself; the 'Free spins: n/10' text elsewhere in the UI is what disambiguates it.
No information is conveyed by audio alone; all wins, feature triggers and state changes are shown as on-screen text/graphics, and Music/Sound FX are independently toggleable in Settings.
Extra multiplier and win amounts are always printed as large high-contrast numeric text (e.g. 'x4'/'x10' heart badge, 'Total win:' readout) rather than conveyed by color or icon alone.

Spacebar can be used to spin instead of clicking; Autoplay with configurable stop conditions (on any win, if bonus game is won, if single win exceeds, if balance changes by X) reduces required interactions; bet min/max can be reached by holding the stepper to saturation instead of precise clicking.

The seven paying mochi symbols are distinguished by color (pink, golden-yellow, blue, light purple, green, brown, beige) but also by shape cues: winged (pink), crown (golden), top hat and moustache (blue), pig snout and ears (purple), angry eyebrows and a flame tuft (green), bear ears (brown), sprout on head (beige).
SYSTEM SETTINGS toggle switches (BATTERY SAVER, AMBIENT MUSIC, SOUND FX) show on/off via both color (grey vs green) and handle position (left = off, right = on).
Buy Free Spins confirm/cancel buttons use green/red color but are also distinguished by glyph shape: a checkmark for confirm, an X for cancel.
Multiplier Spot tiles show the multiplier as printed gold text (x2, x4, up to x128) on a dark tile, readable independent of color perception.

No audio-only information was observed; SOUND FX and AMBIENT MUSIC toggles in SYSTEM SETTINGS confirm audio is decorative/supplementary. Game state (wins, spins left, multiplier values, feature completion) is conveyed through on-screen text and numbers on every captured screen.

Bottom-bar controls are large white glyphs/icons (menu, speaker, info, minus, plus, refresh-spin, stop) on dark circular buttons, distinguished by icon shape rather than by color; win amounts and status text (e.g. FREE SPINS COMPLETED) are large high-contrast white/gold text on a dark bottom bar.

All primary controls are large round or pill-shaped touch targets, with the central SPIN button the largest single control. SPACE and ENTER keys also start/stop the spin. Autoplay supports an adjustable spin count (observed up to 100 on the slider) and a SKIP SCREENS option to reduce interactions per round.

Bottom-bar control layout is stable across all base-game and popup screens (menu+sound bottom-left, info button beside them, CREDIT/BET left-of-center, bet minus/SPIN/bet plus at bottom-right with AUTOPLAY below SPIN). Settings toggle switches show state by both track color (grey=off, green=on) and knob position (left=off, right=on). Autoplay/bonus-buy checkboxes show a white checkmark glyph, not color alone. Bonus-buy confirm/cancel buttons use both color (red/green) and glyph (X/checkmark).
VOLATILITY level is conveyed by a count of 5 identical gold lightning-bolt icons plus the text label 'High', not by a color gradient.

The two tied-payout symbol pairs (Butterfly cyan vs Flower pink; Pinecone brown vs Leaf green) are distinguished by shape (insect wings vs petals; conifer cone vs single leaf with vein), not by color, benefiting colorblind players reading the paytable.

No audio-only information observed; SOUND FX and AMBIENT MUSIC are purely decorative toggles in Settings. All game state (win amounts, free spins remaining, BONUS ACTIVE, RTP/volatility/bet-limit text) is conveyed visually and in on-screen text.

Large circular click targets for SPIN, bet -/+, and menu/sound/info buttons. SPACE and ENTER also spin; holding SPACE engages Turbo Spin, reducing discrete clicks needed. Autoplay (slider-selected count, up to 100) further reduces required interactions.

Bottom-bar control positions are stable across all base-game/menu screens: hamburger-menu and speaker stacked at far bottom-left, a larger 'i' info button beside them, CREDIT/BET readouts centre-left, bet -/+ flanking the central SPIN button, AUTOPLAY directly beneath SPIN. The info booklet is a linear 6-page sequence navigated by left-triangle/X/right-triangle with an explicit 'Page n/6' readout - no hidden scroll content.

Each of the 9 banknotes is identified by its printed character name and multiplier number (x2 to x1000, printed in all four corners) in addition to its solid background color: Jack Trump=gold/yellow, Maggy Ways=pink/magenta, Frank Spin=salmon/coral red, Rich Highroller=green, Hamil Cash=cyan/turquoise, Ellen Golderson=orange/amber, Bill Cashington=dusty rose/pink, Jack Spinson=olive/sage green, Willa Luckynton=grey/silver.
The single active payline (Line 1) is marked by green fill AND its fixed middle-row position in the 3x3 lines diagram AND the text label 'Line 1' - readable without color perception.

No audio-only information is used; all game state (wins, bet, balance, gamble outcomes, autospin settings) is conveyed through on-screen text and numbers. Music and Sound FX are independently togglable and are decorative/ambient only.

The bet +/- arrows' enabled/disabled state at the min/max bet limits is conveyed only by brightness/contrast - bright white (enabled) vs dim grey (disabled) - with no secondary shape or text cue; flagged as a moderate risk for users with very low contrast sensitivity.

Bet is adjusted via small up/down triangle arrows next to the Total bet field; the primary large action targets are the round Spin/Autoplay/collect icons at bottom-right. Spacebar-to-spin is enabled by default as a keyboard alternative to clicking Spin.

Bottom-bar control positions are stable across base-game states: info(i) and settings(gear) at far left, balance/bet-adjust center-left, hint text center, autoplay(A) and spin at far right; during an active Gamble round the far-right icons swap to collect(cash-bag)+spin, and a Gamble-entry star/coin icon additionally appears next to spin after any base win.
Jackpot ticker tiers are color-coded (green MAJOR, red GRAND, blue MINOR) but each ribbon also carries its own text label, so color is not the sole differentiator.
System Settings toggle switches show on/off state by handle position (left=off, right=on) in addition to track color (grey/green).
Volatility is conveyed by a lightning-bolt count (3 of 5 filled gold, 2 grey/unfilled), not by a color name or word.
Money Respin lantern values are always printed as numerals on the lantern itself, not conveyed by lantern color alone.
High-value symbols carry distinct frame colors (turquoise oranges, blue firecrackers, purple drum, pink/magenta lion head) but are also distinguishable by their own icon shape, not color alone.

Jackpot tier badges (GRAND/MAJOR/MINOR) use distinct text labels and dollar values beyond color. Toggle states (ON/OFF) indicated by text labels and checkmarks, not color alone.

All game information is available visually. Win notifications use full-screen text overlays (7 Free Spins: CONGRATULATIONS banner; Money Spins: bottom-bar text). Feature selection via visual dialog cards. No audio-only information — all audio is atmospheric or UI enhancement only.

Red Lucky 7 is bold vivid red on a dark navy cell background — high contrast. Watermelon is green-and-red on dark background. MONEY symbols display a dollar value text on each cell face during Money Spins, aiding identification. COLLECT and SUPER COLLECT carry bold white text labels on shield shapes. Jackpot panel on left side uses colored pill badges with text amounts at all times.

All interactions are single click/tap. Keyboard shortcuts: SPACE/ENTER for spin. Autoplay supports up to 100 spins (slider control). SKIP SCREENS option auto-dismisses feature intro and end screens after a short delay, reducing required interactions. Pick a Boost requires one (Free Spins mode) or sequential (Money Spins mode) capsule clicks. Money Spins win notification auto-dismisses without requiring player confirmation, unlike 7 Free Spins which requires 'PRESS ANYWHERE TO CONTINUE' tap.

Canvas-based game — symbol names not announced by screen reader. Win amounts displayed as text in bottom bar (e.g., 'WIN $4.00'). Keyboard accessible: SPACE and ENTER keys start/stop spins. Feature completion shown as text overlay ('FREE SPINS COMPLETED', 'PRESS ANYWHERE TO CONTINUE').
WILD monkey's active multiplier is shown as printed text ('3x'/'9x') on an orange badge, not by color alone

Each of the 9 fixed paylines is color-coded (green/purple/pink/orange/blue/gold/red/magenta/dark-magenta) but also uniquely numbered 1-9; lines 8 and 9 use similar magenta shades, disambiguated by the printed number
Settings toggles (Battery Saver/Ambient Music/Sound FX) show on/off via handle left/right position, not track color alone (grey=off, green=on)

Ambient Music and Sound FX are independent toggles that can both be turned off; all game state (credit, bet, win amount, WINNER, multiplier badge) is conveyed via on-screen text/graphics, not sound alone

Info/rules booklet is a strictly linear 5-page sequence navigated with previous/close/next controls and an explicit 'Page N/5' counter on every page

Large round click targets with SPIN as the largest; SPACE/ENTER keys are keyboard alternatives to clicking SPIN; Autoplay with SKIP SCREENS reduces the number of clicks needed for extended play

Stable control layout across all screens: menu and sound icons far-left, info ('i') button next to them, bet +/- flank the central round SPIN button, AUTOPLAY below SPIN; the 4 jackpot ribbons keep the same top position and order (MINOR, GRAND, MAJOR, MINI) in every game state
Four low-pay symbols are told apart by suit shape (spade, heart, club, diamond) and the berries by shape; the three monkeys by face and frame colour (red, green, blue base).

Wild symbols carry the word WILD and a gold frame; Free Spin carries the words FREE Spin; wins are shown by glowing frame plus printed Win amount. Red-framed Gorilla versus green-framed monkey is the only colour-reliant pair, but faces differ.
No information is audio-only in the captured frames; sound can be toggled in the menu.
Panels use cyan or white text on dark charcoal with high contrast; wins are numbers in the Win banner and WIN field; multiplier is a large number; Spin and Turbo are icon-only.
Single big central Spin button; Space bar on PC; Auto Spin options up to 1000; Turbo toggle.

Toggle switches (Sound-Ambient, Sound-Effects, Quick Spin) show ON/OFF by handle position (left/right), not only by orange-vs-grey fill; plus/minus buttons are distinguished by glyph shape, not color; active paylines in the booklet are marked by filled-vs-empty cell contrast rather than hue.

Base game (bright blue-grey laboratory) and Free Games (purple-red dusk graveyard) are told apart by a full scene change, not color alone, and the free-spins counter always shows the remaining-spin count as text.
No information is conveyed by sound alone: ambient music and sound effects are togglable and decorative. All wins, spin counts, bet values and jackpot amounts are shown as on-screen text/numbers.
Key numeric values in the Help screen (bet limits, RTP percentages, coin denominations) are printed in a bold orange font against the white body text, an added contrast cue on top of plain text.

All primary controls are large circular buttons with SPIN the largest target. The space bar both starts a spin and can stop the reels early, giving a keyboard-only play path. Auto Play supports stop conditions (Free Games triggered, balance decreases by, single win exceeds) to reduce required manual actions.

Control bar order is stable left-to-right on every base-game frame: Info/paytable, BET, BET LEVEL +/-, BET MAX, SPIN, AUTO PLAY, COIN +/-, BALANCE. The paytable booklet and the Help screen are each a single scrollable document, closed with a top-right 'X', not multi-panel navigation.

All 9 monster symbols have distinct shapes (star-pointed, hairy-fuzzy, antennae-equipped, spiky-horned, round, etc.) enabling differentiation without relying on color; winning clusters highlighted by cyan glow border applied uniformly across all symbol colors

Reel multiplier activation signaled by gold badge frame change AND large numeric text overlay on grid — color change is supplementary to the number display; scatter bottle recognizable by unique rounded bottle silhouette and FREE SPINS text tag regardless of green color

Ambient music and sound effects independently toggleable in settings; all game state information (win amounts, multiplier values, free spins remaining, feature triggers) conveyed via on-screen text displays

Spacebar triggers spin; hold Space activates turbo spin; full autoplay with up to 100 configurable spins and SKIP SCREENS option; all primary controls (SPIN, AUTOPLAY, BET +/-) use large-target buttons
HTML5 canvas game with no accessible DOM text content; screen readers cannot report game state, symbol values, or win amounts — all information is visual only

Card-letter royal symbols (J green, Q yellow/orange gradient, K light blue, A pink/red) are identified by the printed letter, not color alone. Toggle switches in Settings show ON/OFF by both switch position and orange/gray color, so state is not color-only.

No information is conveyed by audio alone. Sound is decorative ambient music and effects, and both can be toggled off independently in Settings. Game state such as free games remaining, win amounts, feature triggers and jackpot values is always shown as on-screen text or numerals.

Base game background is a bright cyan-to-light-blue sky with green jungle foliage framing the screen; the Mount Mazuma character is tan/beige stone with amber-brown eyes and green leaf eyebrows. All primary controls are large rounded or diamond-shaped touch targets, with SPIN the largest target on screen. Control layout is stable across screens: the paytable icon is the leftmost control on the bottom bar, SPIN is the large central diamond, AUTO PLAY sits immediately to its right, BET and BET LEVEL are to the left of SPIN, and COIN and BALANCE are to the right. Toggle switches use knob left/right position plus green/grey colour; checkboxes use a check-mark glyph; the ways-to-win diagram uses check/cross shapes; multipliers, spins-left, RTP, bet limits and win amounts are always printed as text/numerals, not colour alone.

The six royal letters (A/K/Q/J/10/9) are distinguished primarily by character/shape, but also carry a colour-coded glow (magenta A, red K, orange Q, cyan J, blue 10, green 9) as a secondary cue only — do not rely on glow colour alone.

BUY FEATURE panel (gold/yellow, black text) and SPECIAL BETS panel (blue, magenta/pink text) are distinguished by position and label text, not colour alone; the two Buy Feature options differ by label and price, not colour.

No audio-only information observed; ambient music and sound FX are independently toggleable and decorative. All game state (wins, spins-left, multipliers, feature names, RTP/volatility/bet-limit text) is conveyed via on-screen text.
Preview screen shows the max-win claim and logo as large high-contrast text; the volatility indicator is reinforced with the word 'VOLATILITY' plus a numeric bolt count, not colour alone.

All primary controls are large round click targets; SPACE/ENTER also start/stop a spin and holding SPACE engages turbo spin. Autoplay with configurable spin count and Skip Screens reduces required manual actions.

Control positions are stable across screens: MENU/SOUND/INFO icons bottom-left, CREDIT/BET labels beside them, bet -/+ flank SPIN, AUTOPLAY below SPIN, branding fixed bottom-left; 7-page info booklet uses the same nav row with explicit 'Page N/7' readout.
Bottom control-bar buttons (turbo, minus, spin, plus, auto spin) are distinguished by icon shape and position on uniformly dark circles, not by color.
The three low-value coin symbols carry small spade, heart and diamond suit marks that double as a shape cue in addition to color, so they stay distinguishable without color vision.

Winning clusters are highlighted with a bright glow/sparkle outline around the cells rather than a color change to the symbols, and win amounts are also shown as plain text (e.g. 'BIG WIN', 'Win 1.50').

In the Bet Options dialog the selected Bet Size/Bet Level value is marked by size, brightness and central position, and is also shown as an explicit equation (e.g. '0.30 x 2 x 10 = 6.00'), not by color alone.
No information is conveyed by audio only; a dedicated Sound on/off toggle exists and all game state (win amount, bet, balance, multiplier) is shown as on-screen text/numerals.

Spin is the largest touch target on screen. Auto Spin offers fixed presets (10/30/50/80/1000 spins) that sharply cut the number of taps needed to play. On PC, Space starts/holds a spin, skips the spin animation, and activates the sole available button whenever only one button is on screen.

Base game control layout is fixed left to right: Turbo toggle, Minus, Spin (largest, centered), Plus, Auto Spin, with the balance/bet strip directly above. Paytable and Rules are strictly linear paginated booklets with a single back arrow and a persistent 5-icon bottom tab bar (Sound, Paytable, Rules, History, Quit) - no branching navigation.

Feature state is shown via text/numbers, not color alone: MEGAWAYS way-count, MULTIPLIER value, WIN amount and FREE SPINS LEFT are all printed as numbers; the paytable's valid-way vs invalid-way diagram uses shape (green check vs red X); Settings toggles use handle position (left=off, right=on) as well as track color; symbol category card colors (teal=tequila, magenta=taco, olive=cactus, maroon=skull, purple/brown=mandolin) are backed up by distinct artwork per symbol.

No audio-only information observed; Ambient Music and Sound FX are independently toggleable and purely atmospheric. All outcomes (wins, free spins awarded, multiplier changes, gamble results) are conveyed through on-screen text and numbers.

Win and free-spins-award amounts render as large high-contrast gold/orange digits on a dark wood background on the trigger and win screens; the splash screen's max-win text and volatility badge use bold high-contrast yellow/gold lettering with a dark outline rather than relying on subtle color.

Large circular click targets for spin/menu/sound/info. SPACE and ENTER keys start and stop spins (holding SPACE also engages Turbo Spin). Autoplay supports a configurable spin count (up to at least 100) plus a SKIP SCREENS option, reducing required interactions.

Stable control layout across all screens: menu/sound/info stacked bottom-left, bet minus/plus flanking the spin button bottom-right, autoplay below spin. The rules/paytable is a strict linear 8-page sequence navigated with previous/close/next controls and an explicit 'Page N/8' indicator on every page.

Win amounts, feature names (BONUS/SUPER BONUS) and free-spin counters are always printed as text/numbers, not conveyed by color alone; cell-multiplier values are numeric text (x2 to x1024) regardless of the tile's glow color.
The Cluster Pays paytable diagram distinguishes a valid cluster from an invalid one with a green check-mark versus a red X-mark (shape-differentiated, not color-only).
The Bonus Boost toggle relies partly on blue=off switch position, but is also disambiguated by an 'X' icon and by left/right position, not color alone.
No audio-only information found; feature name, spins remaining, win amounts and multipliers are all conveyed as on-screen text. Music and Sound FX are separately toggleable and purely decorative.

Large circular spin button; spacebar-to-spin is available and toggleable in Settings; autoplay presets from 10 up to unlimited reduce required clicks; Buy Features lets a player skip manual spin-hunting for bonus rounds at a fixed cost.

Bottom bar control positions are stable across base game and feature rounds: info and settings buttons far left, bet stepper center-left, autoplay and spin buttons far right; feature rounds add Win/Total win/Free spins readouts in the same bar as plain text and numbers.
Chip denominations (1/5/10/25/100) always carry a large printed number on the chip face; color is never the only way to read a chip's value.

The three betting ovals (left/center/right) are visually identical in color and shape and are told apart only by screen position and by the '<amount> FUN' text label above a placed bet — no color dependency.

Round outcome is duplicated by a text pill near the hand ('Win: X FUN' / 'Push: X FUN') and, on an outright win, a large bottom-bar text banner; a loss is shown by the chip disappearing (a position/text cue), not by a color cue.
A busted hand (dealer or player) shows a red badge that also carries the word 'Bust' printed on it — text-duplicated, not color-only.
A soft hand containing an Ace shows both possible totals as text separated by a slash (e.g. '4/14') until resolved — a numeric cue, not a color cue.

One confirmed color-only exception: inside the Settings menu, the History tab's icon/label turns red when clicked with no accompanying text/content change (the panel content silently stays on Rules) — flagged as a genuine accessibility weak point in that single control, and separately as a build defect (see coverage gap).

The Settings menu's Sound & Music tab exposes independent sliders for Music and Sound Effects volume, and every round outcome (win/push/loss, payout amounts, dealer bust) is shown as on-screen text — no information is audio-only.

HIT/STAND/DOUBLE/SPLIT are each shown only when legal for the active hand (not always-shown-but-greyed-out), each with its own icon and text label. The rules booklet (reached via the hamburger Settings menu, Rules tab) is a single linear document with clearly separated, consistently ordered sections — Objective, Deck/Card values, How To Bet, Betting Limits, Player Options (Hit/Stand/Double/Split), Dealer Rules, Game Outcomes/Payoff table — that could be announced as landmarks.

Free-spins vs base-game state is shown by both a background palette shift and explicit counter/caption text. The spin/stop button changes both color (green/red) and shape (triangle/square). Toggle switches show both fill color and knob position.

No audio-only information observed. Settings exposes separate Ambient and Effects sound toggles, implying music/SFX are decorative. All win amounts, feature triggers and jackpot-race state are conveyed via on-screen text and numbers.

The 25 payline-number tags beside the reels use many decorative colors, but the printed NUMBER identifies each line, not the tag color; line paths themselves are diagrammed with orange-highlighted cells on a dark grid in the paytable booklet.
Large circular targets for spin, info and autoplay. Autoplay with configurable stop conditions reduces the number of repeated clicks needed. No keyboard shortcuts were confirmed either way.

Stable bottom-bar control order across all states: info, bet, bet-level, bet-max, spin, autoplay, coin, balance. The Pay Table and Help content are plain scrollable text with no pagination controls to operate.

Gamble round's suit/colour choice is never colour-only: BLACK/RED buttons carry text labels, and the four suit tiles use distinct pictograms (spade/club/diamond/heart) in addition to black/red colouring, so the player can act on shape and text alone. No information observed to be conveyed by audio only; Music and Sound FX are separately toggleable, and every audible cue noted in the rules has an on-screen text/animation confirmation (win amounts, 'Line N pays', free-spins counter, gamble result reveal).

Every symbol is distinguishable by shape, not color alone: the four card symbols (A/K/Q/J) are different letterforms; the four high symbols are different object silhouettes (doll figure, mortar-and-pestle, round clawed shield, drum-with-skull); Wild is the only horned, open-fanged mask; Scatter is the only animal-head icon; Hot Strike is the only symbol rendered as flame-lettered text rather than a pictorial icon

Super Bet's ON/OFF state is conveyed by brightness/saturation of the same green-family hue (dull teal vs bright green) rather than a hue change -- the state should be announced explicitly rather than inferred from color

No mechanic in this game is communicated by sound alone -- every trigger (Wild Transform, Free Games, Hot Strike, Super Bet, Jackpot Race) has a paired visual cue: banner text, a glowing symbol, or a colored badge state change
The in-game Help screen renders plain white text on black with orange highlighted numbers/keywords, giving high native contrast

All actions are single-click/tap on fixed-position diamond buttons on a static bottom bar (no drag, no timed reflex input, no multi-touch gestures); the Space bar is also bound to spin/stop, giving a keyboard-only alternative

Every numeric readout the player needs (BET, WIN, BALANCE, COIN, prize tickers) is canvas-drawn text, not real DOM text, and requires a synthetic description layer anchored to the fixed bottom control-bar positions

Each of the 6 regular symbols pairs a distinct icon/letter with a distinct tile color (Lamp=purple, Ring=teal/green, Amulet=blue, A/K/J=dusty rose/maroon tile with red/green/blue letters) — identity never depends on color alone.
Jackpot bar's three plaques (MAJOR green, GRAND red/crimson, MINI teal) are also distinguished by name label and by plaque size/shape — GRAND is visibly larger and centered.
WILD (genie artwork, 'Wild' script) and its jackpot-badged variant (smoking-lamp artwork, 'Jackpot' script) are distinguished by artwork and text label, not by color.

Settings toggle switches use knob position (left=off/right=on) plus track color (grey/green); autoplay checkboxes use a white checkmark glyph plus green fill — state readable without relying on color.

All game state (wins, respin trigger, jackpot amounts, autoplay count) is shown as on-screen text/numbers; no information is conveyed by sound alone. Sound and vibration toggles are independent and vibration is off by default.

Body text and win readouts are high-contrast white/gold on dark backgrounds throughout. Weakest spot: the preview screen's volatility indicator uses filled-vs-unfilled gold/grey lightning bolts with no accompanying numeric or word rating.
Large circular touch targets for spin, bet +/-, and the four bottom-bar icons. Autoplay (up to 100 spins with a 'SKIP SCREENS' option) reduces the number of required interactions for extended play.

Rules/paytable is a single continuous vertical scroll panel, not a paged booklet with page-N-of-M indicators — a screen reader would need to expose scroll position/percentage rather than a page count.
The three carts and three spirits are told apart by color and also by the small icon at the foot of each cart (flame, water drop, leaf) and by position: Red left, Blue center, Green right.
Element symbols differ by shape (flame, water drop, leaf), not only color. Letters A, K, Q are orange-tan, blue and green and map to the Red, Blue and Green carts, so color and letter agree.
Wild is a golden crest with the word WILD on a red ribbon; Free Spins is the only pink scroll with a text caption. Both are legible without color.
Sound can be switched on or off in the menu. No gameplay information is known to be audible only; not verified with sound.

Cart values (x1, x3), the floating win multiplier, the ways plate and balances are printed digits, not bar fills. Panels are charcoal grey with gold headings and gold-yellow payout numbers, symbol counts in white-grey.
Large tap targets (spin ring about 200 px wide at 760 px frame). Space starts a spin, holding Space repeats, tapping during a spin stops the reels. Auto Spin offers 10, 30, 50, 80 or 1000 spins.
The play field is a canvas; only the Paytable and Rules panels are exposed as DOM text. Win amounts, ways and cart values exist only as drawn text.
Four creatures have different silhouettes (dragon head, winged bird, striped cat, plated reptile), so colour is not needed to tell them apart.

Five element discs differ by glyph shape as well as hue: golden-yellow 金, green 木, azure-blue wavy strokes, orange-red 火, brown-orange 土. Orange-red, brown and golden-yellow are close for red-green colour blindness, but the glyphs differ.
Wild and Scatter carry the printed words WILD and SCATTER, so they never depend on colour.
A win is shown by brightening and glow on winning tiles with all others dimmed, a central amount with the text n WAYS WON, and a WIN field in the bottom bar.
The selected autoplay value is a lighter turquoise-tinted pill with turquoise text; no shape change, so it relies on colour and brightness.
Free spins change the scene from jade green to warm gold with a pink reel panel; this is also named by the large text Remaining Free Spin: N.

Every event has a visual form: win overlay with ways text, full-screen 10 FREE SPINS and Free spins won!, remaining counter, TOTAL WIN with COLLECT button. A Sound toggle is in the player menu; audio cues were not captured.
Winning symbols glow and the rest dim; win amounts are large gold digits; bottom-bar figures are bright turquoise on dark teal. Panel text is white and grey on charcoal.

Large central spin button (about 180 px); tap game area to stop reels. PC: Space starts a spin, hold repeats, press during spin skips animation. Turbo and Auto Spin (10, 30, 50, 80, 1000) reduce tapping; Stop shows remaining count. Bet wheels need scrolling; Max Bet and Confirm are single taps.

Canvas build; Paytable, Rules and Bet Options are overlay panels with real text. Win amounts and the free spin counter are canvas text. The ribbon marquee rotates automatically and truncates at its edges.

The four Christmas-cracker low symbols are told apart by pattern and card color rather than hue alone. The active MULTIPLIER cell is marked by its centre position plus a brighter ring, not a specific color -- the same x1/x2/x4/x6/x8/x10 values cycle through every position. Winning tiles are marked by a white/gold diamond-pattern glow (brightness and pattern), not a color swap. Toggle switches use left/right position in addition to an orange fill.

No information is conveyed by audio alone. 'Sound - Ambient' and 'Sound - Effects' are independently mutable toggles that do not affect outcomes. Win amounts, spin state and multiplier values are all shown as on-screen text and numerals.

Large circular touch targets for SPIN, AUTO PLAY and BET MAX; stepper +/- buttons for BET LEVEL and COIN avoid the need for precise dragging. Autoplay offers 10 to 500 spins with an explicit stop-on-Free-Games toggle, reducing the number of clicks needed for extended play.

Bottom control bar keeps a stable order across every screen: (i) info, BET, BET LEVEL -/+, BET MAX, SPIN, AUTO PLAY, COIN -/+, BALANCE. The Help screen is real linear HTML text across 11 pages (not canvas graphics), comparatively more screen-reader-friendly than the canvas-rendered reels and paytable booklet.

The six cash-symbol value tiers are distinguished by outline shape as well as color - scalloped round coin for the two lowest tiers (Blue, Green), hexagon for the two mid tiers (Pink, Purple), octagon/rounded-square for the two highest tiers (Orange, Red) - and every tile also prints its value as a bold white number.

The four jackpot tiers (Mega/Major/Minor/Mini) are labelled by name text in addition to plaque color, and always sit in the same fixed vertical stacking order with the highest value at the top, so tier identity does not depend on color perception.

The Free Spins level meter shows a removed cash tier with a crossed-out (X) overlay and a filled/unfilled marker state rather than color alone, and the numeric 'Free Spins: N/M' counter gives the same progress independently of the meter graphic.
Mute state on the Settings panel (All Sounds/Sound Effects/Music) is shown by an icon shape change - a cross through the speaker icon - rather than by color alone.

Independent mute toggles are provided for All Sounds, Sound Effects and Music, so audio can be fully silenced; all gameplay information (wins, spin counter, level progress) is also shown as on-screen numeric text.
Royal card symbols are color-coded (A red, K pink/magenta, Q blue, J green) but each also shows its own printed letter, so color is not the only identifying cue.

WILD and SCATTER symbols carry their name as baked-in text; the Mystery Modifier's three outcome badges (green W / blue up-arrow / red X) are each paired with a full descriptive sentence in the rules pages.

Ante Bet and Settings toggle switches show handle position (left=off, right=on) in addition to track color (grey vs green); paytable/rules navigation uses triangle/cross-shaped green arrows, not color alone.
SOUND FX and AMBIENT MUSIC are purely decorative toggles; no game information (win triggers, feature state, amounts) is conveyed by audio alone — all state is duplicated as on-screen text.
Win amounts, free-spins-remaining and credit/bet figures are always shown as large plain numeric text in the bottom bar, duplicated alongside any color or icon cues.

Bottom bar uses large round click targets, with the central SPIN button as the largest element. SPACE/ENTER keys also spin, holding SPACE engages Turbo Spin, and Autoplay (configurable spin count plus Skip Screens) reduces required interactions.

Control layout is stable across all screens: hamburger-menu and sound icons stacked far-left, 'i' info button to their right, bet -/+ around the central SPIN button, AUTOPLAY just below SPIN. The info booklet is a fixed linear 8-page sequence (paytable, then rules subtopics) navigated with left/right arrows and closed with an X.
Winning symbols are shown by brightness: they stay bright with a golden sparkle while all other symbols are dimmed, and the plaque prints WIN with the amount. Hue alone is never the signal.
Royals A (coral red), K (hot pink), Q (purple), J (light sky blue), 10 (mint green) and 9 (dusty brown-rose) are distinguished by the printed letter or number as well as by color.
Fruits that differ mostly by hue (red strawberry, pink-cream peach, yellow-green apple) also differ by shape: leafy top with seeds, round with a crease, short stem.
Remaining bonus spins are shown by three daruma dolls on the table (lit red doll = spin left, dark grey doll = used) and also by the printed caption Bonus Spin with a numeral.

Increasing Prize Multiplier tiles have an orange-red sunburst and a black raccoon silhouette; ordinary Prize Multiplier tiles are pale cream with a white-orange sunburst. Shape and silhouette separate them, not only color.

Every state change has a visual cue: WIN plaque text, multiplier numeral, the Bonus Feature won plaque with pink glow, the Bonus Spin numeral and the Total Win screen. No sound-only cue was verified; audio was not captured.

Two fields of 6x3 stacked in a portrait column; the top field is above the center bar and the bottom field below it. Prize multiplier tiles carry large gold-orange numerals, and the win multiplier is a large gold-orange numeral on an orange-glow garden path below the lower field.

Panels (Paytable, Rules, Bet Options, Auto Spin) are dark charcoal-blue with white and light-grey text, terracotta orange headings and light tan or gold payout numbers. The base game background is light cream and tan, with the reel panels semi-transparent cream.

In the Bonus Feature a large gold counter with a dark outline shows the running total of multipliers while tiles empty, and the final Total Win is a huge gold numeral with a red outline on a golden screen.
Space key starts a spin, holding Space repeats spins, Space skips the reel animation, and when one button is available Space activates it. Touch: tap Spin or the game area to stop the reels.

Auto Spin offers 10, 30, 50, 80 or 1000 spins and shows a Stop button with spins remaining; a Turbo button shortens spins. Control buttons are large round buttons about 100 px across in the 760 px wide frame. Bet controls are locked during a spin.

The Paytable and Rules panels are real HTML text and can be read by a screen reader. Balance, bet, win, multiplier, the Bonus Spin counter and the 1458 WAYS label are drawn on the canvas and may not be exposed.

Screen layout, important for non-visual use: there are TWO independent fields of 6 reels by 3 rows, one above the other, separated by a dark wooden center bar with a gold diamond ornament. Each field has 729 ways, 1,458 in total. A win needs matching symbols in succession from reel 1 inside ONE field; the fields are counted separately.
A Wild landing in one field is duplicated into the other field on the opposite side of the center bar, so the state of one field can change the other. Wild appears on reels 2 to 6 only.
Ninja symbols are blue and samurai symbols are red or orange, but each also differs by subject: masked face, helmeted face, star, sword. Wild and scatters carry the printed words WILD and SCATTER.

Multiplier tokens are green x2, blue x3 and red x5 and also print their number. Turbo state is shown by a diagonal strike-through and the word OFF, not by colour alone. Wins are numeric and bet lines are numbered at the board edges.
Low symbols are brush-stroke letters on wooden plank tiles with silver-grey frames: A grey-blue, K pink-red, J golden-orange, Q lavender-purple; the letter shape identifies each.
Sound can be switched off in the menu; features and wins are announced by banners (NINJA FEATURE!, SAMURAI FEATURE!, BIG WIN, MEGA WIN, TOTAL WIN) and numbers.

Gold frames surround every high symbol and the title lettering; reels sit in a dark brown frame with a gold border. Bet and settings panels are dark charcoal with an orange-gold selected value and a bright orange Confirm button.

In free spins the whole scene takes a darker navy tint and the Free Spins Remaining label is gold brush lettering with a large number. Winning lines are drawn in cyan and non-winning tiles are dimmed.

Single large round spin button; on PC the Space key starts a spin, holding it continues spins and pressing during a spin skips the animation. Auto Spin offers 10, 30, 50, 80 or 1000 spins; Turbo is available.
Rules and paytable are real DOM text. Every pay symbol has a distinct subject. Menu items (Quit, Sound, Paytable, Rules, History, Close) each have an icon and a text label.

Most affordances are non-color: toggle switches use handle position, checkboxes use a checkmark glyph, paytable/rules nav controls use triangle/cross shapes, FREE SPINS-remaining and WIN amounts are numeric text, and the WILD-pattern token track uses a ring highlight plus 'LEVEL UP' text rather than color alone. The archway torch flame's blue (base game) vs orange/red (free spins) color shift is decorative only - the active mode is also conveyed by the 'FREE SPINS LEFT' counter and a changed bottom-right control icon. The five rune-stone symbols (red, green/emerald, blue, purple, olive) are distinguished primarily by color but each also carries a distinct carved rune glyph shape as a non-color cue.

No audio-only information: SOUND FX and AMBIENT MUSIC are separately toggleable and purely decorative/reinforcing. All game state (win amounts, free spins remaining, level-up events, pattern selection, max-win cap) is conveyed through on-screen text and imagery.

Key information uses large, high-contrast text: the max-win banner and logo are large gold-on-dark text on the preview screen, CREDIT/BET labels are gold text on a dark bottom bar, and win/level-up/free-spins-remaining readouts are large bold numerals on dark backgrounds throughout.

Spin is the largest click target on screen; SPACE and ENTER keys also start/stop spins (keyboard-operable, no mouse required for core play). Autoplay with a configurable spin count and a SKIP SCREENS option reduce the number of actions needed to play and to get through feature intro/end screens.

Control layout is stable and consistent across all screens: hamburger menu + sound stacked bottom-left, 'i' info button beside them, bet -/+ flank the large central spin button, autoplay near the spin button. The info booklet is a strictly linear 8-page sequence navigated with </> and closed via a center X, in the same position on every page.

Active line-count is a printed number, not a colour code. Wild and Scatter tiles carry their own name-tag text baked into the artwork. The winning payline is marked by a gold outline AND its own numeric win overlay, not colour alone. Free Games vs Super Free Games are distinguished by an entirely different background illustration and by different trigger-banner text ('Feature Triggered' vs 'Bonus Feature'), not just a colour shift. Toggle switches (Settings, Auto Play stop conditions) show handle position in addition to their on/off colour. The Minor and Grand jackpot values are both labelled with words, so their gold/white-on-dark-plaque colour is not the only distinguishing cue.

No information is conveyed by audio alone; feature triggers, wins, jackpot tickers and element collection are all shown as on-screen text or graphics. Sound is controlled by two independent toggles in Settings (Sound - Ambient, Sound - Effects) plus a master mute icon in the service strip.

Base game background is a dark blue/violet/teal cosmic wormhole scene with a black-disc-and-halo black hole and pink meteor streaks. The reel frame is carved gold-yellow with jade-green serpent-vine ornaments at the top corners and coral-pink tentacle scrollwork down the sides; reel cells are deep violet/near-black tiles with thin gold borders. Free Games switch the background to a warm dusk sky over a Chinese hillside village with teal-blue pagoda roofs and a dragon-guardian face at the lower right; Super Free Games switch it again to a more saturated pink/blue/purple cosmic vortex. The bottom UI bar is a pink/magenta serpent-skin ribbon with gold-rimmed buttons and a large red circular Spin button; the two jackpot plaques are dark teal/navy with gold/white text.

The circular Spin button is the largest and most central target on screen. The space bar both starts and stops a spin, reducing the need for precise pointer clicks. Auto Play offers configurable stop conditions (feature triggered, balance-decrease threshold, single-win threshold) that reduce the number of manual interactions needed for extended play.
