Payline number badges around the reel frame are NOT in sequential top-to-bottom order (left edge reads 5,2,1,3,4; right edge reads 4,2,1,3,5) -- risk of confusion for users relying on positional expectation rather than reading each numeral
6-page in-game info booklet is a strictly linear sequence with explicit 'Page N/6' indicator and left-triangle/X-close/right-triangle navigation, friendly for sequential traversal

Control layout stable across all screens: hamburger menu and sound icon far-left, 'i' info button next to them, credit/bet center-left, SPIN centered, AUTOPLAY below SPIN, 'PRAGMATIC PLAY' branding fixed bottom-left

Card suit symbols (Spade, Heart, Club, Diamond) are distinguished by shape alone: Spade has upward-lobe with triangular stem, Heart has two upper lobes and V-bottom, Club has trefoil (three round lobes), Diamond is a rhombus. Shape fully disambiguates all four suits for deuteranopes and protanopes without color.
WILD state is communicated by text labels ('WILD' on each symbol cell, banner 'IS WILD DURING RESPINS') — not by color alone. BAR symbol identified by 'BAR' text lettering, not color.

Volatility meter shows 5 of 5 flame icons — count communicates the level without requiring color differentiation. Autoplay checkbox uses a visible checkmark shape in addition to green color. Toggle switches use left/right position in addition to color.
Ambient Music, Sound FX independently toggled off in System Settings. All gameplay information available visually: feature banners, WILD text overlays on symbols, win amounts in bottom bar.

Persistent left-side paytable panel always visible during gameplay listing all 9 pay entries (WILD x3 = 200x down to Diamond = 0.8x) as text with amounts. Full paytable accessible via info button. Win amounts shown as text in bottom bar ('WIN $XX.XX', 'LINE N PAYS $XX.XX').

Symbol colors: Joker — blue collar, red-blue jester hat, gold bells; Seven — royal blue numeral on magenta-pink tile; Bell — bright gold-amber metallic; BAR — tan-gold plaque with dark brown text; Spade — purple-violet gem; Heart — red-ruby gem; Club — emerald green gem; Diamond — sky blue-sapphire gem. All on gold-bordered tiles with sparkle glints.

Autoplay up to 100 spins with SKIP SCREENS option. Keyboard shortcuts: SPACE and ENTER start/stop spin. Respin Until You Win runs fully automatically — no player action required during respins. Turbo Spin and Quick Spin options available.

All symbols have distinct shapes describable by screen reader: Joker face, numeral 7, bell object, 'BAR' text, and four uniquely shaped suit symbols. Feature state communicated by banner text at top of reel area. WIN and LINE N PAYS are text elements in bottom bar.

Each outcome tile's multiplier badge colour is not reliably matched to its own option name: the RED option's badge is red/maroon, the BLACK option's badge is gold/amber, but the GREEN option's badge renders BLUE/cyan instead of green. This is mitigated because every tile also carries a printed text label (RED/GREEN/BLACK plus a garment word) directly beneath its badge, so outcome identity never actually depends on colour alone.

The footer history strip (past-round multipliers at the bottom of the base game) encodes win versus loss purely by hue: white/grey text for a round that was not won, magenta/pink text for a round that won. No accompanying icon or word ('WIN'/'LOSS') was found next to those figures on any captured frame, so users who cannot distinguish white from pink may not be able to read session history from that strip alone.

No audio-only information was identified anywhere in the captured frames: the 'Sound' toggle in Settings is an explicitly decorative audio on/off switch, and all game state (bet amount, countdown, multipliers, win/loss, balance) is conveyed as on-screen text and numbers.

Disabled control state is shown mainly by a dimmer mid-grey text colour rather than a strong visual change: the MAX button on the bet-size picker renders visibly dimmer/greyed once the 850 FUN ceiling is reached, versus the still-white MIN button. The numeric value itself (which stops changing at 850/0.1) is the more reliable, colour-independent confirmation of the bet ceiling/floor.

All primary controls (BET SIZE pill, +/- steppers, HIGH RISK toggle, the three outcome tiles) are large rounded touch targets sized for a mobile card layout. MIN/MAX quick-jump buttons reach the bet floor (0.1 FUN) or ceiling (850 FUN) in a single tap instead of repeated stepping, and AUTO MODE removes the need to tap a tile every round.

Control positions are stable across all game states: hamburger/close button top-right, profile + AUTO MODE pill + balance in the second row, BET SIZE / stepper / countdown / HIGH RISK controls in one horizontal row, three outcome tiles beneath it, and Total Wins / Big Wins counters fixed at the very bottom. The 'How to Play' content is a single linear scroll (back-arrow plus X to exit) rather than a tab set, so it can be read top-to-bottom without branching navigation.
The three scatter pots are dual-coded: blue/red/green pot color plus a distinct emblem shape (bat/dragon/tiger), so identity does not depend on color perception.
Free-spins reel multipliers (e.g. X2/X3/X5) and MONEY dollar values are always printed as legible numerals, not conveyed by hue alone.
Settings toggles (Battery Saver / Ambient Music / Sound FX / Intro Screen) are dual-coded: green=on / grey=off color plus knob position (left/right).
Royal card symbols are colored (A red, K blue, Q magenta/purple, J green) but differentiated primarily by the letter itself, color is only a secondary cue.

No audio-only information observed; SOUND FX and AMBIENT MUSIC are purely decorative toggles. All game state (spins left, win amounts, modifier activation, feature trigger) is conveyed through on-screen text and numerals.
Royal-card symbols (A/K/Q/J) rely on the printed letter plus a secondary color; there is no additional non-letter shape cue for users who cannot read the small glyph.
Large circular touch targets throughout (SPIN, MENU, SOUND, INFO, AUTOPLAY); SPACE and ENTER keys also start/stop a spin, reducing reliance on precise mouse targeting.
The paytable/rules booklet is a strictly linear 8-page sequence navigated with previous / close / next controls; a 'Page N/8' counter is always shown, giving an unambiguous progress readout.

The three scatter symbols are primarily colour-coded (blue/red/green) to their matching chests and Plinko modifiers, the game's main colour-dependent system. Each is also distinguished by a completely different creature illustration (three-headed wolf/Cerberus vs multi-headed dragon/Hydra vs boar's head) and by printed text naming the chest ('BLUE CHEST'/'RED CHEST'/'GREEN CHEST') and modifier ('EXTRA BALLS'/'MULTIPLIER BALLS'/'PRIZE BOOST'), so colour-blind players can still identify them without relying on colour.
The '243 ways to win' example diagram uses a green check mark for a valid pattern and a red X for an invalid one; this pairing is reinforced by shape (check vs X), not colour alone.

No audio-only information observed; all game state (win amounts, balls remaining, bet, credit, armed modifiers, rules text) is conveyed as on-screen text or iconography. Ambient music and sound FX are explicitly togglable and purely decorative.

The three treasure chests above the reels and the three scatter medallion icons on the Buy Bonus plaque/Plinko HUD are visually similar in shape/silhouette; the distinguishing creature artwork inside each medallion is small and requires close or zoomed viewing to tell them apart.

Large circular click targets throughout (SPIN, menu, sound, info, bet +/-). SPACE and ENTER keys start/stop a spin, giving a keyboard-only path. AUTOPLAY reduces the number of required interactions. During Plinko rounds the SPIN button becomes a stop/skip icon (red-outlined square) to speed through ball-drop animations.

Fixed control layout: menu/sound icons at the far left of the bottom bar, a separate info ('i') icon beside them, CREDIT/BET labels centre-left, bet +/- flanking the central SPIN button. The 8-page rules booklet is a strictly linear sequence with an explicit 'Page N/8' counter and a dedicated close (X) control, making page position reliably announceable.

Blue Ranger and Green Ranger symbols are identical in silhouette and differ only by hue - a genuine colour-blind weak point, distinguishable only via a small reel-badge ring colour and paytable position.
The four low-tier symbols (heart, diamond, spade, club) are the classic card suits; colour is redundant because each has a distinct, recognisable shape.
The four mid-tier weapon/tool icons (dagger, axe, shuriken, robot head) each have a distinct silhouette, so colour is not required to tell them apart.
The top-bar Kaiju panel (Mega Reels / Power Collector / Kaiju Cash) is coded by monster silhouette, text label and icon glyph in addition to colour, so it stays readable without colour.
The jackpot ladder (MEGA/MAJOR/MINOR/MINI) is identified primarily by the printed tier name and by plaque size/position (largest on top), not by colour alone.

CRITICAL GAP: Gold Tiger (warm gold-amber), Purple Tiger (deep purple-violet), and Green Tiger (bright lime-green) are distinguished solely by color — identical silhouettes with no text label, shape difference, or positional cue. Deuteranopia/protanopia users risk confusing Gold Tiger and Green Tiger. Tritanopia users may struggle with Purple Tiger. No secondary non-color identifier exists for the three tiger symbols.

BAR family symbols carry visible text labels (one/two/three rows of 'BAR'; 'ANY BAR') — fully distinguishable without color. Red 888 is identified by the repeated numeral 8 shape. Gold Paw is identified by its circular medallion form. Win highlight uses a lime-green glow on winning symbols; win amount is also displayed as text ('WIN $X.XX') in the bottom bar providing a non-color win signal.

All game-critical information is visual: PAYS column permanently visible, win amount shown as 'WIN $X.XX' text in bottom bar, RTP stated in info panel text. Sound is purely atmospheric. AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX can be independently toggled off in System Settings. No game information is conveyed solely through audio.

Permanent PAYS column on the left side of the canvas displays all 9 symbol payouts at all times without requiring any panel interaction. Text in the PAYS column is relatively small and may require screen magnification. RTP (97.52%) is stated in text on info panel page 1/4.

Full keyboard support: SPACE or ENTER starts and stops the spin; hold SPACE activates TURBO SPIN. Bet adjustment via on-screen (+)/(−) buttons and also via TOTAL BET control inside the System Settings overlay. Autoplay supports up to 100 auto-spins; TURBO SPIN and QUICK SPIN options reduce per-spin interaction time.

All 9 payout values are visible in the permanent on-canvas PAYS column without opening menus. The 4-page info panel contains all game rules in text form. Win amount is shown as text in the bottom bar. CREDIT and BET are labeled text fields. Bottom bar hint 'HOLD SPACE FOR TURBO SPIN' describes keyboard controls.

The three tiki-mask symbols (red/green/blue) share the same mask template and face color matches card-border color, but each also carries a distinct crest shape (three-feather / solid fern-frond / spiky) and distinct teeth color (gold / green / grey-white). These non-hue cues are subtler than the dominant face-color difference, so red-green colorblind players may need to rely on crest shape and teeth color rather than glance-level recognition.
Free-spins locked vs unlocked grid cells are distinguished by both color (dark maroon vs light tan) and a distinct engraved tiki-pattern texture, not color alone.
Settings toggle switches show on/off state by both handle position (left=off, right=on) and track color (grey=off, green=on).
Buy Free Spins confirmation dialog distinguishes cancel from confirm by both color (red vs green) and glyph shape (X vs checkmark).

No audio-only information was observed; all game state (win amounts, free spins remaining, total ways, bonus active, credit/bet) is conveyed as on-screen text. Sound/Ambient Music toggles are purely decorative.
Win amounts, free-spins-remaining count and total-ways count are shown as large high-contrast gold text on dark wood plaques, legible without color discrimination.

All primary controls are large circular click targets; SPACE/ENTER give full keyboard control of spin start/stop (holding SPACE engages turbo spin); autoplay supports a configurable spin count (observed default 100), reducing required repeated clicks.

Win and credit counters animate upward mid-count before settling on the final value; only the stabilized end-value represents the true amount, transient mid-animation reads should not be treated as final.
A/K/Q royals share identical payouts (8/4/2) and are distinguished by letterform, not only color (A red, K green, Q blue).

The three Treasure Egg colors are also distinguished by a differing gold overlay pattern -- heart-and-scroll filigree on the red egg vs diamond-lattice on the green and blue eggs -- not by hue alone; each color's transform-to-Wild round threshold is also spelled out in printed numbers in the Paytable/Rules.

The active cell on the multiplier ladder (x2-x15) is marked with a brighter gold overlay and larger size, not color alone; the end-of-spin 'TOTAL WIN' banner differs from the per-round 'WIN' banner by its label text and red plaque shape, not color alone.

No audio-only information was found: all state (win amounts, round/multiplier, feature triggers) is conveyed through on-screen text and numerals; Sound is a togglable on/off control with no other noted function.

Payout numbers and rule text are printed as plain white/yellow text on a dark panel; the ways-counting diagram uses a check mark versus an X shape rather than color alone; the splash title is large, high-contrast gold lettering on a red background.
The central Spin button is the largest touch target on screen; the Space bar performs spin/stop/turbo-skip on PC; Auto Spin (5 presets) and Turbo Spin reduce the number of required interactions.

Control positions are stable across every gameplay frame (Turbo far left, minus/Spin/plus centered, Auto to the right, menu hamburger at the far right edge); the status bar (balance/bet/win) is a fixed three-field row, each pairing an icon with a text value.
Reindeer (antlers, tan fur) and Sabertooth Cat (golden mane, open roar) both use deep purple hex frames. Distinguishable by portrait illustration only; shape of antlers vs. mane is the discriminator.

Baby Dinosaur (orange-red scales, spiky crest) and White Wolf (white fur, blue eyes) share blue-family hex frames. Wolf frame is icy blue; dino frame is darker slate blue-gray. Portrait is the primary discriminator.
The 10 royal tile uses a deep violet-purple hex frame in the same color family as Reindeer and Sabertooth Cat frames. Distinguished because it shows the numeral '10' rather than an animal portrait.
Winning symbols gain a bright white/silver halo glow around their hex borders. Win amount appears as large orange-gold text at bottom center ('WIN $X.XX'). Win state is not conveyed by color alone.
Ante Bet stone shows 'OFF' or 'ON' text label at all times alongside a golden arrow icon. State is readable without color discrimination.

All payouts, rules, and feature descriptions available as readable text in the 6-page info panel (opened via 'i' button). Win amounts display visually at bottom center. Ambient music and sound effects are independently disableable via separate toggle switches in system settings.

SPACE key (hold for turbo) and ENTER key control spin start/stop. Autoplay with configurable spin count (slider) and Skip Screens option reduces required interactions. Spin, Autoplay, and Start Autoplay buttons are large targets.

Grid recommended to be read column by column left to right, top to bottom within each column; column 1 is leftmost where WILD cannot appear. WILD symbol displays 'WILD' in yellow text on its hex border; BONUS displays 'BONUS' in stone-carved letters — both labels are on the symbol face. Large win state also shows 'WINNER' subtext below win amount.
Picked-but-undrawn numbers are shown with a gold/amber border outline rather than a fill-color change, so a pick stays identifiable without color vision.

The open Rules section is marked with a solid white fill versus outline-only for the rest, and the selected Autoplay round-count preset likewise uses solid fill versus outline -- neither relies on hue alone.

Ball/match type (regular match=orange, bought-extra match=green, free-bonus match=purple) is conveyed mainly by hue, with the printed ball number as the only other cue; the match type itself is not additionally labelled in on-screen text.
No information is conveyed by sound alone; Sound and Music are independent toggleable sliders in Settings, and every round outcome (matches, multiplier, win amount) is shown as on-screen text.
The round-result win popup shows the multiplier and win amount in large bold white text on a dark card, high-contrast against the near-black game background.
All primary actions (Play, Cash Out, Buy Extra, Autoplay presets) are single large buttons; a shuffle/quick-pick button auto-selects numbers in one tap instead of up to 10 individual taps.

Monetary values (bet, payout, balance, min/max bet, Max Profit) and round-outcome text are printed numerals/labels suitable for text-to-speech; the Rules booklet is one continuous scrollable document reached via six labelled section jump-links rather than a true multi-panel accordion.

Gems and the mine differ by SHAPE as well as colour: gems are an upward-pointing faceted crystal silhouette (blue/green/gold), the mine is a round sphere with a lit fuse spark. Tile borders also change colour (light blue on a gem tile, red on a mine tile).

The Turbo toggle communicates on/off by knob position (left/right) as well as by the green glow, and the multiplier ladder marks the current rung by both a purple highlight and its position next to the action button.
Grid-size and active-state buttons are told apart by fill brightness, not hue, so the selected grid size and mines count remain readable without colour.
All round outcomes (win amount, multiplier, loss) are conveyed fully in on-screen text and pop-ups; sound can be muted via the top-bar speaker icon or the Settings sound slider.

Core actions (Start Game/Cancel/Place bet, tile clicks, Cash Out) are single discrete clicks with no drag or timed/hold gesture. Turbo Mode reduces the number of required clicks by revealing a pre-selected pattern in one action, at the cost of higher risk per click.
All key numbers (balance, bet, multiplier, win amount, RTP, limits) are printed as plain on-screen text rather than canvas-only or audio-only, which is compatible with OCR/text-scraping tooling.
A hit (exploded) mine and a merely-revealed unopened mine are told apart mainly by artwork (fireball burst vs intact sphere) - no text label such as 'Hit' vs 'Unopened' is printed on the tile itself.

Every numeric game-state value that matters (multiplier cells, Balance, Disk cost, Rows, bet amount, Max Profit, RTP) is printed as plain text, not conveyed by colour alone. The one place colour carries information with a shorter text backup is the risk gauge (three flat colour bands with no per-band numeric label), but the risk LEVEL itself is also spelled out in text ('Risk: High') right next to the gauge.

Sound and Music are independent, separately mutable sliders in Settings; every state change observed (bet deducted, disks in flight, payout received) is also reflected in the visible Balance/board state, so no information is audio-only.

All adjustable numeric controls (Disk cost, Rows, Disks count) use paired round -/+ buttons, plus, for Disk cost only, one-tap 'min'/'max' shortcuts; the primary action is a single large 'Drop N Disks' button. No drag or gesture input is required - dropping disks, opening panels and adjusting settings are all discrete clicks.

Control layout is stable and always in the same left-to-right order (back/exit top-left, wordmark next to it, Balance + sound + settings top-right, Disk cost / Rows / Disks-count+Drop along the bottom). The Drop button's own sub-label always states the exact bet amount that will be charged, so the consequence of pressing it is legible without reading the Disk cost and Disks-count fields separately. There is no distinct win-celebration overlay or counter animation - the outcome must be inferred from the Balance figure changing between frames.

Jackpot bar: all 5 tiers carry text name (MINI/MINOR/MAJOR/MEGA/GRAND) plus distinct color plus dollar value — triple redundancy, safe for all color-blindness types. Settings toggles: OFF=gray pip-left, ON=green pip-right — dual cue (color and position). Win symbols have orange glow plus text WIN and LINE N PAYS announcement.

Each symbol has a unique shape: Eye (iris in teardrop frame), Scarab (beetle silhouette), Cobra (rearing snake with hood), Lotus (plant with gem), Scepters (crossed staffs X-shape), Ankh (cross with loop), WILD (pharaoh mask face), MONEY (round coin). Shape differentiation works without color.

No audio-critical information identified. Win amounts, payline results, jackpot tier highlights, RTP, bet limits, and all RESPIN FEATURE rules are conveyed entirely through on-screen text and visual indicators. No sound-only notifications documented.

Separate minus and plus buttons for bet adjustment (no fine-motor slider required for bet changes). Autoplay supports up to 100 spins reducing repeated button presses. SKIP SCREENS checkbox in autoplay bypasses win animation screens. Turbo and Quick spin modes available.

Win amounts displayed as numeric text: WIN $4.00, LINE 5 PAYS $4.00. Jackpot bar shows text tier names and dollar values at current bet. All settings have explicit text labels and sub-descriptions. PLACE YOUR BETS prompt and autoplay spin count are on-screen text.

RTP (96.51%), bet limits (MINIMUM BET $0.10, MAXIMUM BET $240.00), and full RESPIN FEATURE mechanics (trigger conditions, 16 MONEY values, tower growth thresholds, FULL SCREEN BONUS) are published as text in the paytable/rules panel.

All five low-pay symbols use distinct shapes: Pink Heart (heart), Purple Hex Gem (hexagon), Red Diamond (rhombus), Purple Triangle (triangle), Green Orb (sphere) — shape alone differentiates them; color is supplementary. Red Diamond (crimson red) vs Green Orb (green) are shape-distinct (rhombus vs sphere), safe for red-green colorblind. WILD identified by ornate gold frame, pink ribbon bows at sides, and gold W emblem — not by pink color alone.

SOUND FX and AMBIENT MUSIC independently toggleable via Settings. BATTERY SAVER mode reduces animation speed — useful for players sensitive to motion or animation intensity. All win and feature outcomes confirmed by on-screen text, not sound alone.

Win feedback uses multiple simultaneous cues: animated pink/gold border around winning cluster cells plus WIN $X.XX and WINNER text in gold on bottom bar — no color-only signaling. Free Spins result confirmed by full-screen text overlay (CONGRATULATIONS YOU HAVE WON $X.XX IN N FREE SPINS). Active WILD multiplier shown as bold cyan/turquoise text on the orb in Free Spins — high contrast against pink background.

Autoplay available with 8 preset spin counts (10/25/50/75/100/250/500/1000 spins) plus loss/win stop conditions. SPACE and ENTER keyboard shortcuts for spin; hold SPACE for turbo spin. BUY FREE SPINS button persistently visible in base game left panel — instant access without waiting for natural SCATTER trigger. Bet adjustable via minus/plus stepper buttons in Settings (no text entry required).

Each of the 3 rings is distinguished by both color (pink/magenta fire, lime-green leaf, cyan water) AND a distinct icon shape (flame / four-leaf-clover / water-drop) at a fixed 12-o'clock badge position, so a colorblind player can identify a ring by icon shape and fixed position, not color alone; the center-hub outcome icons (element icon on hit, grey cloud on miss, purple skull on bust) are likewise each a distinct shape, not only a distinct tint.

Sound and Music are independently toggleable in the settings/burger menu, and no gameplay-critical information appears to be conveyed by audio alone - outcomes are always shown visually via the center-hub icon and printed values.

All numeric checkpoint labels and monetary values (BALANCE, WIN, the CASHOUT/PART CASHOUT button faces) are rendered in a bold, high-contrast white/light-grey sans-serif font against the dark charcoal-grey background throughout the UI.

Bet adjustment uses discrete +/- stepper buttons rather than a required drag/slider (the autoplay spin-count control offers a slider only as an alternative to its preset buttons), and a keyboard shortcut ('Space to spin & go', toggleable in settings) is available as an alternative to mouse-clicking PLAY.

The three lanes (red/green/blue ring glow) are each also a visually distinct character portrait (red = bandana inmate, green = bald saluting inmate, blue = plaid-shirt inmate) and each has its own printed first-step multiplier (3.9X/2.5X/1.55X), so identity does not rely on color alone. Risk remains: no on-screen text label names a lane by color, and distinguishing the red vs green glow could still be difficult under protanopia/deuteranopia at a glance - an adaptation should announce the portrait/character, not the color.

The SOAP (no-win) and HANDCUFFS (loss) round outcomes are distinct icon artwork (a tan bar-of-soap icon vs a named, crossed-out handcuffs icon in the bonus dialog), not conveyed by a color shade alone.
CASHOUT's active state (solid yellow fill, black dollar amount) versus its idle/inactive state (flat dark, no value shown) is conveyed by both fill color and the presence/absence of a printed amount.

The bet stepper's up/down caret buttons stop responding at the printed min ($0.12) and max ($200), but the disabled arrow is not clearly visually dimmed versus the active arrow - the disabled state is confirmed only behaviorally (value stops changing), which is a gap for low-vision users relying on a visible disabled affordance.

A settings toggle ('Space to spin & go', captured ON) binds the spacebar to trigger PLAY. Autoplay offers preset spin counts (5/10/15/20/25/50/75/100) plus a fine-tune slider and optional stop conditions ('stop if cash decreases by', 'stop if total coef increases by'), letting a motor-impaired player pre-configure a session without per-spin input.

The three rings are told apart primarily by ICON (gingerbread man / Christmas tree / snowman) and by angular position (outer/middle/inner), not by colour alone -- idle rings all share the same neutral slate-blue tone. Only an actively-filling ring takes on a distinct hue (fire=dark red, leaf=green, water=cyan); a colour-blind user can still track the engaged ring via its badge icon lighting up and via the numeric multiplier printed directly on the fill arc.

PART CASHOUT and CASHOUT buttons are distinguished by legible text labels first, and only secondarily by an active-state highlight colour (CASHOUT turns solid yellow/gold when active) -- the text label alone is enough to tell them apart without relying on colour.

Toggle switches in the settings menu (Sound / Music / Space-to-spin) encode state both by position (left=off, right=on) and by colour (grey track=off, green track=on) -- redundant encoding that helps colour-blind users.

The WIN field shows only the LAST completed round's payout, not a live running total during an active round -- it stays at the previous round's value (or 0) while CASHOUT climbs. A low-vision or cognitively-impaired user watching WIN during an active round would see a stale or zero figure while money is actually accumulating in the CASHOUT button text instead.

All wheel ladder numbers and the two carry-over values (+7X on the water ring, +20.5X on the leaf ring) are printed as legible text directly on the ring rather than conveyed only by colour or position -- a screen-magnifier user can zoom in and still read every value.
Multiplier token colour rings (green x2-x20, blue x21-x100, violet x101-x500) are always paired with a printed 'xN' number on the token itself

Free Spins feature state is signalled by a full background/theme swap (day desert to night starfield) AND a logo-mascot swap (pharaoh to alien head) AND explicit text ('BONUS ACTIVE', 'Free spins: N/15'), not colour alone

no information is conveyed by sound alone; all key state (bet, balance, win amount, free-spins count, accumulated multiplier, bonus price) is shown as on-screen text/numbers; Music and Sound FX are independently toggleable, on by default
win amount and bet multiplier on the win screen are shown as very large, high-contrast outlined text/numbers

bet size is chosen via small up/down stepper arrows that open a scrollable list rather than a drag control, needing several small clicks to reach a distant value (0.20 to 50.00 span); spacebar can substitute for clicking Spin, reducing precision requirements

the playfield is a non-rectangular stepped pyramid, not a normal reel grid: 8 columns of heights [2,4,5,4,4,5,4,2], rows top-to-bottom [2,4,6,6,6,6], 30 active cells total; in the two bottom rows the two centre columns are blocked by a decorative door instead of symbol tiles — this shape is structural (payouts depend on the count of identical symbols across the whole irregular field), not decorative

the Buy Bonus dialog's CANCEL and BUY buttons are both the same green colour and shape, distinguished only by their text label, not by position or colour — a screen-reader-only user must rely on reading the label

Reel symbols are distinguished by shape, not color alone: BAR is white block letters on a plain black cell (no fruit art); Lucky 7 is an orange-red numeral; Gold Star is a yellow star on a red disc; Plum is a dark blue/purple oval; Orange is an orange round fruit; Lemon is a yellow oval fruit; Cherry is a pair of red cherries with a green leaf; X is a black letter on a grey cell with no glow.

Toggle switches in Settings show on/off state by BOTH handle left/right position AND green fill color; Autoplay checkboxes show checked state via an explicit white checkmark glyph, not color alone; disabled bet +/- buttons at the min/max limits are shown by greyed-out, lower-contrast icon fill rather than hue alone.

The active payline on a win is marked by a colored line overlay PLUS a printed line-number tag at both ends of the screen PLUS a flame animation over the winning symbols. Green is reused for several distinct controls (nav arrows, the close X in the info booklet, the 'on' toggle state, BET MAX / START AUTOPLAY buttons), but each is also distinguished by shape, position, or accompanying text.

No audio-only information is used: SOUND FX and AMBIENT MUSIC toggles are purely decorative and do not affect game outcomes (rules page 4/5). All game state — balance, bet, win amounts, payline results, bet-limit ceilings/floors — is conveyed visually and in text.

High-contrast text throughout: yellow CREDIT/BET/WIN values on a near-black background, white body text on dark semi-transparent info panels with cyan/light-blue headings. Controls are large circular icons, with a large central SPIN button, aiding low-vision targeting.

Large circular click targets throughout, with SPIN the largest. SPACE and ENTER keys start/stop a spin (holding SPACE also engages Turbo Spin), reducing reliance on precise pointer clicks. Autoplay with an adjustable spin count (up to at least 100) reduces the number of repeated manual actions needed.

Control layout is stable across all screens: menu and sound buttons stacked bottom-left, a separate 'i' info button beside them, CREDIT/BET readouts center-left, large circular SPIN button center-right flanked by bet -/+ buttons, AUTOPLAY directly below SPIN. The 5-page info booklet is a strict linear sequence navigated with left/right arrow buttons and closed by a dedicated X, suitable for sequential traversal.
the five payline side-badges pair a fixed color with a printed number 1-5 (yellow=4, red=2, blue=1, green=3, magenta/pink=5), so lines remain identifiable without color perception

the VOLATILITY bolt-icon row shows 4 of 5 bolts filled (visually suggesting a higher rating), but the adjacent body text explicitly states 'Medium volatility'; the text label should be treated as authoritative, not the bolt count

settings and autoplay toggle switches pair a green fill with a distinct left(off)/right(on) handle position, and checkbox options show an explicit white checkmark glyph, so on/off state is readable without color discrimination

no game information is conveyed by audio alone; ambient music and sound effects are separately toggleable and purely decorative, while all state (credit, bet, win, respins-remaining heart counter, feature running total) is conveyed visually and in text
CREDIT, BET, WIN and money-symbol values are consistently rendered in yellow/gold on dark panels for high contrast, independent of the surrounding art

SPACE and ENTER keys start/stop a spin without needing to click; holding SPACE performs a turbo spin; spin, menu, info and bet +/- controls are large circular click targets; Autoplay (default 100 spins) with a Skip Screens option reduces required interactions

control positions are stable across base-game screens (menu/info bottom-left, credit/bet left-center, bet +/- flanking spin bottom-right, autoplay beneath spin); the rules booklet is a strictly linear 6-page sequence navigated by left/right triangle icons and closed with a central X, with an explicit 'Page n/6' readout on every page
Symbols are told apart by shape and content (face, coffin, goblet, cross, letters); tile background colors green, blue and magenta are only a secondary cue.
Royals A K Q J 10 are all dark grey letters and differ by letter shape; red, green, blue and purple glows are decoration only.
Winning lines are drawn in gold with line numbers at the left edge; winning symbols get gold borders.
Selected auto spin chip uses a red fill and red text versus grey, relying partly on color.
Feature starts and ends are announced with on-screen banners (EXPANDING SYMBOLS FEATURE, REMAINING FREE SPIN, LAST FREE SPIN, TOTAL WIN); sound can be toggled in the menu.
Expanding symbol is shown enlarged above the reels, a banner names it, tiles get gold fiery frames and non-winning symbols dim.
Space key spins, hold Space repeats, Space skips animation; turbo button shortens spins; auto spin 10 to 1000.
Game is canvas based; Rules and Paytable panels are real DOM text. Win amounts and remaining free spins are large printed numbers.

Wolf-faction symbols use teal/cyan ornamental frames; vampire-faction symbols use red/crimson frames. Color differentiates factions, but symbol subject (wolf animal motif vs vampire human portrait) independently identifies faction without color.
Select Free Spins screen uses explicit text labels (WOLVES / VAMPIRES), numeric spin counts (14 / 8), and lightning-bolt count badges (3/5 vs 5/5) — no color-only dependency for mode selection.
BET and CREDIT values shown as large yellow numeric text on dark charcoal background — high contrast. Win amounts displayed as large gold text overlay centered on screen.

Autoplay supports up to 1000 spins with Turbo Spin and Quick Spin options. No time-pressured mechanics in base game. Select Free Spins modal requires a player choice; no auto-selection timeout was observed.

All 8 pay symbols differ by shape and iconography, not color alone. Card symbols (A/K/Q/J) have distinct letterforms. SCATTER is a rectangular golden ticket labeled VIP SCATTER. WILD is a circular moon orb with bat and WILD text. Tumble multiplier values displayed as text (x1, x2, x1024) in addition to colored bubbles.

Card royals use different colors — A is magenta-purple, K is red-orange, Q is lime green, J is cyan-blue — but each also has a unique letter, so color is not the sole differentiator. Dracula and Cat Vampire Girl are entirely different character types (human vs cat). Vinyl disc vs cocktail glass are visually distinct objects.

Win amounts and feature outcomes shown as text. Free Spins completion screen is fully visual with text. AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX toggleable independently in Settings. No audio-only game information detected.

Win amounts displayed as dollar text on screen. Congratulations overlay uses large golden text on dark background. Multiplier bar shows numeric values (e.g. x1024) in large text at center of wooden wheel display.

Keyboard shortcuts: SPACE and ENTER start and stop spin. Autoplay supports up to 100 autospins. Quick Spin and Turbo Spin modes reduce required interaction frequency. SKIP SCREENS toggle auto-dismisses feature intro and end screens.
Canvas-based game — all content rendered in a single canvas element. No DOM text or ARIA labels available for screen readers.

Low-value gems are distinguished by suit shape as well as color: blue spade, pink/magenta club, red heart, green diamond. WILD portrait sits in a glowing turquoise-blue frame; SCATTER is a pink/purple gemstone dollar sign on a gold plaque. Paytable nav uses shape (left triangle / cross / right triangle) not just the green color. Settings/autoplay toggle switches show state via handle position (left=off, right=on) in addition to green when on.

No audio-only information observed; AMBIENT MUSIC and SOUND FX are purely decorative toggles. All game state (win amounts, active line number, multiplier value, credit/bet, autoplay count) is conveyed via on-screen text/graphics, not sound alone.

Large round click targets, the central SPIN button is the largest control. SPACE and ENTER keys also start/stop the spin. Autoplay (adjustable spin count plus Skip Screens) reduces the number of required clicks for extended play.

Stable control positions across all base-game screens: menu+sound stacked far-left, info ('i') button just to their right, bet +/- flanking the central SPIN button, AUTOPLAY directly below SPIN. Info booklet is a strictly linear 6-page sequence with a 'Page n/6' indicator always in the same bottom-right position.
Royal letters are color-coded (red A, green K, purple/magenta Q, blue J) but each is also a distinct alphabet letter shape, so identification does not depend on color perception.

Active feature state (Free Spins vs base game) is signalled by both a background tint shift (navy blue base game vs dark brownish-red/maroon Free Spins) and an explicit 'FREE SPINS LEFT n' text counter, not color alone.
Settings toggle switches (Battery Saver/Ambient Music/Sound FX/Intro Screen) show state by handle position (left=off, right=on) in addition to track color (grey=off, green=on).
High-value symbols are distinguished by distinct imagery (portrait, car, roulette wheel, dice, card fan), not by color coding.

No audio-only information; Ambient Music and Sound FX are purely decorative toggles. All game state (wins, spins remaining, multipliers, feature triggers) is conveyed through on-screen text and numerals.
CREDIT, BET and WIN labels are large gold/yellow text on a dark background, high contrast; promo captions on the splash screen are large high-contrast text (gold/white/purple on dark magenta).
Large round click targets; SPACE and ENTER also work as spin/stop hotkeys. Autoplay (slider up to 100 spins) and a Skip Screens option reduce the number of required manual clicks.

Bottom-bar control positions are stable across all screens (menu/sound far left, info icon next, bet -/+ flanking spin, autoplay below spin). The 7-page rules booklet is a linear sequence with left/right triangle navigation and an explicit 'Page N/7' indicator on every page.

Jackpot tiers are distinguished by both colour (blue/green/magenta/red poker chips) and by their printed tier name (MINI/MINOR/MEGA/GRAND) plus vertical position on the ladder, so they stay legible without colour vision. Locked versus unlocked Enhancer Reels are shown by icon shape (padlock and chain versus an empty or tagged cell), not colour. The active info-panel icon is shown by brightness and position, not hue. Two residual colour-only cues: the VOLATILITY step icon (orange fill versus outline, no printed step number) and the gold-versus-red body colour split on Instant Prize coin icons, though the printed cash numeral on each coin stays legible regardless of colour vision.

No information is conveyed by audio alone. Jackpot ladder values, multiplier tags, the Bonus Game spin-remaining indicator, and win totals are all shown as on-screen text or graphics. The three sound toggles (All Sounds, Sound Effects, Music) control ambience only and do not gate any gameplay information.

Win amounts are shown as large, high-contrast gold-on-dark 3-D lettering. Balance and Total Bet are white bold text on a black translucent strip. RTP and the malfunction clause are plain white text on a dark background in the Know the Game panel. The active bottom-navigation icon is solid white versus dim grey outlines for the other three, a brightness cue usable without fine colour discrimination.

The Spin button is a large circular target dominating the right edge of the screen. The space bar both starts a spin and skips animations (Quick Play), reducing the number of precise clicks needed. Bet changes are made by scrolling a single list (0.10 to 100.00 fun) rather than repeated plus/minus taps.

Control layout is stable across screens: speaker and hamburger-menu icons top-right; Autoplay, Bet Select and Spin stacked on the right edge; Balance bottom-left, Total Bet bottom-right. The info booklet (Paytable/Rules/Settings/Know the Game) is reached through one consistent 4-icon bottom bar. This documents visual layout consistency only; no ARIA labelling or literal screen-reader software support was observed or tested.

Coin overlay badges: money awards are round badges with the value printed before the 'x' (e.g. '5x'); multiplier badges are angular red gem-shaped badges with the 'x' printed before the value (e.g. 'x5') -- distinguished by shape and text order, not color alone.
The five royal symbols (A, K, Q, J, 10) differ in body color (purple/red/green/blue/orange) but are identified primarily by their distinct letter/number glyph shape, not color alone.
The Ante Bet toggle shows its state via a background color change plus explicit 'ON'+checkmark vs 'OFF'+arrow-icon text, not color alone.
Autoplay checkboxes (Turbo Spin / Quick Spin / Skip Screens) show a white checkmark glyph inside the box in addition to the green fill, not color alone.
Free Spins remaining is shown as explicit numeral text ('<N> FREE SPINS LEFT'), not a color-coded bar or dial.
Win amounts are always paired with numeric text (e.g. 'WIN 100X', 'WIN $319.50'); no information is conveyed by banner color alone.
Volatility is conveyed via the text label 'MEDIUM VOLATILITY' plus a small waveform icon, not by a color-filled bar/segment count.

Line-number badges flanking the reels are told apart by their printed digit, not by color. Toggle switches in Settings carry handle position as well as color (grey=off, orange=on). Bet, win, balance and jackpot amounts are always shown as high-contrast numerals rather than color-coded. Wild and Scatter are identified by distinct artwork and printed labels in the Pay Table, not by frame color; the only pure-color cue is the green rope-wreath frame on the two highest-paying regular symbols (longship, shieldmaiden) versus the plain frame on the rest, and identity there is still carried mainly by the artwork inside.

No information is conveyed by sound alone; all game state (bet, win, balance, jackpot ticker amounts, autoplay stop conditions) is shown as on-screen text. Sound is limited to ambient music and effects, both independently toggleable in Settings (Sound - Ambient, Sound - Effects), plus a Quick Spin toggle and a footer mute icon.

Win and Big Win text is large gold/yellow lettering over a bright orange sunburst, high contrast against the darker reel background. The Pay Table booklet and Help screen use white/light-grey text on a near-black background, also high contrast. The two vertical columns of small colored line-number badges flanking the reels are printed in a small font that may be hard to read without zooming; all 25 paylines are permanently active regardless of whether these badges are legible.

The SPIN button is the largest circular target on screen, centered in the control bar. The space bar can both start and stop a spin, reducing the need for precise pointer clicks. Coin size and bet level are only adjustable via repeated plus/minus clicks (no direct numeric entry), partly offset by the BET MAX shortcut and by Auto Play preset spin counts (10, 20, 30, 50, 100, 500) that reduce the total number of required interactions.

Bottom control bar keeps a stable left-to-right order: info (opens Pay Table), bet display, bet-level stepper, bet max, spin (largest, centered), auto play, coin stepper, balance, with a separate darker service strip below it for balance/bet/win/session controls. The Pay Table booklet and the Help screen are both single continuous scrolling documents with no tabs or page numbers, reached from the info button and from the gear-icon Game Menu respectively.

Most affordances use icon shape, text labels or thumb/element position rather than colour alone: toggle position, payline dot position, Heart-disc vs Spade-disc shape, and the selected-bet cell's distinct size/centring. The primary 'go' yellow is reused for SPIN, confirm-checkmarks and the selected bet/preset, but each also carries a distinct shape or position, so colour is never the sole cue.
Payline diagrams in the rules booklet use lit-white vs dim-red dots on a fixed grid of positions -- shape/position-based and safe for all colour-vision types, not relying on hue discrimination.

No audio-only information was identified; Sound and Music are separate, clearly labelled on/off toggles in Settings. All game state (win amounts, bet, balance, gamble history/attempts-left, RTP/bet limits) is conveyed as on-screen text/numbers.

Large round targets throughout, SPIN is the largest and most central. No keyboard-spin hint was observed on this build. This specific demo build drops roughly 30-50% of clicks on the SPIN button without starting a spin (an observed build quirk, not the intended design) -- relevant to motor-impaired users who may need repeat inputs.

Stable control layout: five right-hand-column round buttons in a fixed vertical order (speed, autoplay, SPIN, bet, menu) during base play; the same column collapses to fewer context-specific icons inside sub-panels (settings/autoplay/bet-ladder/booklet). Balance/Win/Bet readout is always at the same three bottom positions (left/centre/right).
Jackpot ladder tiers (MEGA/MAJOR/MINOR/MINI) are distinguished by colour (red/magenta/green/cyan) plus printed tier name and currency amount, so colour is never the only cue.
Hold & Win lives are shown as hearts that are bright pink/red when available and grey/desaturated when spent, plus a fixed count and position, so remaining lives can be read without relying on hue.
Bonus Scatter (BONUS star) and Jackpot Scatter (JACKPOT hex plaque) both carry their function as on-symbol text rather than relying on gold-vs-magenta hue alone.

The RTP disclosure, malfunction clause and full mechanic rules are presented purely as on-screen text with no audio equivalent, so deaf or hard-of-hearing players are not disadvantaged for these facts.

Cherries (pink/magenta) and Apricot (orange) share a similarly rounded fruit silhouette and the same pay tier, so a low-vision player relying on rough shape alone could confuse the two; hue and the paired-cherries shape are the disambiguators.

Autoplay batches up to 1000 spins and a scrollable bet-value list reduce the number of discrete clicks needed for extended play, though the bet list still needs scroll/drag gestures with no numeric keypad entry, and no turbo-spin or skip-screens toggle exists to speed pacing.
All bet/win/jackpot/Instant Prize amounts are pure-canvas numerals with no ARIA labels or audio narration; a screen-reader or blind user has no alternative channel to read these values.

During Respins, the GOLD vs GREEN scatter distinction (gold = sum of triggering scatters, green = running cumulative sum) is colour-dependent with no shape/text difference beyond the on-screen 'PAYS $X.XX' / 'NEXT PAYS $X.XX' labels, which should be used as the reliable cue instead of coin colour.

Nav icons use triangle/X shapes, settings toggles use left/right switch position in addition to grey/green fill, and the four jackpot boxes are labelled with printed names (GRAND/MAJOR/MINOR/MINI) rather than relying on border colour alone.

No audio-only information observed; ambient music and sound FX are purely decorative and independently toggleable in System Settings. All game state (win amounts, remaining spins/respins, jackpot values, feature selection) is shown as on-screen text and numerals.

Primary targets (Spin, info, menu) are large circular buttons; SPACE/ENTER also start/stop a spin without clicking. Autoplay with a configurable spin count reduces the number of required interactions for extended play.

Stable control layout: hamburger-menu + sound icons stacked far-left, larger info button to their right, bet +/- flanking the central Spin control, Autoplay below/right of Spin. The rules/paytable booklet is a strictly linear 8-page sequence with left/right triangle navigation and a centre close X on every page.
Pick a Potion: both potion bottles are rendered identically green before selection - no colour or shape cue distinguishes the MYSTERY CURSES outcome from the FORTUNE HEX outcome ahead of the pick.

Free Spins variant is identified by banner text ('SUPER/MEGA/plain VOODOO FREE SPINS') and a pinned card icon in addition to the reel-frame glow colour (cyan for Super, gold/amber for Mega, warm orange/red for plain Voodoo).
Rules/paytable booklet navigation icons are all green but differentiated by shape: left-pointing triangle (previous), 'X' (close), right-pointing triangle (next).
Settings menu toggles (Battery Saver, Ambient Music, Sound FX, Intro Screen) show on/off state via slider handle position (left=off, right=on) in addition to green-vs-grey track colour.

Sound FX and Ambient Music are purely decorative toggles; all game state (wins, free spins left, guarantee status, feature names) is conveyed through on-screen text and numerals, with no audio-only information.

Win screens show the amount as large high-contrast yellow/gold numerals outlined in red on a brown parchment background, plus a full sentence 'YOU HAVE WON $X IN N FREE SPINS', legible without colour discrimination.

SPACE and ENTER keys start and stop the spin; holding SPACE engages Turbo Spin, reducing discrete clicks needed. Autoplay (configurable spin count, with Turbo/Quick Spin/Skip Screens options) further reduces required interactions for extended play.
Rules/paytable booklet is a strictly linear 7-page sequence navigated with previous/next arrows and closed with an X, with a persistent 'Page n/7' readout.

The three rings pair their colour (blue/green/red) with a distinct icon shape (wave/leaf/flame) and a printed multiplier number on the ring itself, so ring identity never relies on colour alone; the paytable rows repeat the same colour+shape+text pairing.

No audio-only information was observed; a Sound slider and a separate Music slider are decorative and independently adjustable. All state changes (balance, Payout, Part Payout figures, ring fill, bonus results) are conveyed as on-screen text and graphics.

A light/dark Theme toggle (sun/moon switch, top-left) inverts the whole UI to a black background while keeping the same glossy icon assets, useful for users sensitive to bright screens. Residual risk: the Cash Out / Part Payout buttons' temporarily-unavailable state (during an active spin, autoplay or bonus) is shown only by a subtle drop in contrast/greying of the button face, with no icon change or explicit disabled label.

Two spin methods exist: a single click, or press-and-hold for continuous auto-spinning (hold is OPTIONAL here, unlike sibling game Rings of Olympus where holding is mandatory), reducing the discrete clicks needed for repeated play. A separate one-click AUTO toggle also exists for fully hands-off continuous play.

The playfield is canvas-based; control layout is fixed and stable (balance top-left, theme toggle below it, help/sound/menu icons top-right, wheel gauge centred, bet +/- and spin/cash-out/part-payout cluster on the right). The rules booklet is a single long scrollable document with 6 quick-jump section buttons plus additional un-buttoned sub-sections reached only by scrolling.

Engine, Wings and Hull ring segments are colour-coded blue, green and red, but each ring is also uniquely marked by a printed number (1/2/3), a distinct icon shape (turbine, biplane-wing, aeroplane-nose) and its own multiplier ladder, so colour is never the only identifying cue.

The two negative-outcome result symbols use different pictograms rather than colour coding (Empty Box is a brown box, Broken Gear is a grey gear-cog with an exclamation mark), and locked Hangar items are marked with a padlock and a question-mark glyph, not colour.

No information is conveyed through audio alone; Sound and Music are separate toggle sliders in Settings, and every outcome (win, loss, ring progress, bonus result) is shown as on-screen text and numerals.

The multiplier dial is one continuous unified ring track rather than three visually separated rings, with all three rings' labels interleaved along the same strip; a low-vision player may find it hard to tell which lit arc segment belongs to which ring by position alone, since ring identity is only confirmed by matching the printed multiplier value to that ring's ladder.

Hold-to-spin plays continuous rounds only while the SPIN button is held down; there is no separate autoplay screen with a fixed number of rounds, so sustained pressure for a variable duration replaces repeated single taps, which may be harder for some motor-impaired players.

Balance, Total Bet, Bet Amount, Payout and Part Payout are printed as plain text near their controls, and the four round action buttons (BUY BONUS, SPIN, CASH OUT, Part Payout) sit in a fixed cluster, which is favourable for screen-reader exposure if these are exposed as accessible labels.

The three rings are told apart by RADIUS and by their own multiplier ladders as well as by colour (red, green, blue), and the element symbols differ in shape - a flame, a leaf rosette, a curling wave. No information is colour-only.
Separate mute controls for effects and for sound sit in the top right corner; the outcome of a spin is visible without audio.

Balance and the rules booklet are DOM text and scale with browser zoom, but the ring multipliers and the Payout / Part Payout readouts are drawn on the canvas at a small size and do not scale with the browser.
No timed reaction is required: the round resolves on its own and the decision to cash out is taken between rounds, with no countdown. Hold to Spin replaces repeated clicking.

The playfield is canvas: ring progress, the payout figures and the landed symbol are not exposed to a screen reader. The cash-out button additionally prints a broken label ('CASH OUT NULLX') in the DOM instead of the current multiplier.

Ring colour (red/green/blue) is never the only cue: every filled segment also carries a printed multiplier number, and Jack/Potion/Ghost are additionally distinguished by shape (pumpkin/bottle/ghost icon on each badge).
Hold-to-spin state is shown by icon shape (crossed-out vs solid lightning bolt), not by a colour change, so it stays legible for all colour-vision types.

No audio-only information was observed: all round outcomes (wins, ring progress, payouts) are conveyed through on-screen numerals and the Balance figure; Sound and Music are separate toggleable sliders in Settings.

Balance, Bet Amount, Payout, Part Payout and every ring's multiplier value are printed as bold white/light-grey numerals on a near-black background, giving high contrast regardless of the ring's colour.

Only two actions drive play: press (or press-and-hold) the round Spin button, and press Cash Out or Part Payout; Bet +/- are large round targets either side of the readout; no drag gestures or precision targets appear anywhere in the captured flow.

Layout is stable and non-shifting across every screen (fixed header icon row, fixed Cash Out/Spin/History cluster); the Rules booklet is one continuous scrollable document with fixed section jump-links rather than a paginated carousel, so it can be read linearly top to bottom.

The three rings are told apart by fixed radial position (outer/middle/inner) and by their own printed multiplier ladders in addition to colour (red, green, blue); the five symbols differ by drawn pose/effect - flame licks, jagged bolts, a water swirl, a plain figure with no aura, and a hand holding a card - not by badge colour alone. Grey player and Yellow Card are deliberately low-saturation so they read by shape without colour.
All feedback (round result, bonus wording, RTP, limits) is delivered as on-screen text; sound and music are independently toggleable sliders in Settings, and no information is audio-only.

All interactions are single clicks (Spin, Cash Out, Part Payout, Auto/Stop, bet +/-); no drag, timed hold, or multi-touch gesture is required to play a full round, despite the printed rules text describing a press-and-hold 'Hold to Spin' behaviour that this build does not require.

Every numeric outcome - Balance, Payout, Bet Amount, Part Payout amount, and each ring's multiplier - is printed as plain on-screen text, so a screen-reader overlay could announce round state without relying on the canvas art.

The three rings are identified redundantly by fixed radial position (outer/middle/inner), the printed caption at the centre medallion (Six!/Four!/Run!/Dot!/Out!) and the printed multiplier numbers on each ring — not by ring colour (red/green/blue) alone.

No information is conveyed by sound alone — round outcomes (wins, Free Cashout banners, ring fills, Dot!/Out! results) are always shown as on-screen text and graphics; Sound and Music are independently mutable in Settings.

Filled ring segments show as a brighter lit arc with a glowing dot marker against the printed multiplier labels; unfilled segments stay a dull, unlit version of the same ring colour, so fill state is also readable from the marker's position along the printed multiplier scale.

Cash Out and Part Payout buttons switch between dim grey (unavailable) and bright white (available) text/label brightness rather than a colour change, so availability is readable without colour discrimination.

Hold-to-Spin lets a player keep the round running by holding the Spin button instead of repeated clicks; Autoplay starts continuous rounds from a single click and needs only one Stop click to end it, reducing repetitive clicking for extended play.

The three rings (Lion=red-orange, Snake=green, Rhino=blue) are never distinguished by color alone: ring position is fixed (Lion always outer, Snake always middle, Rhino always inner), each ring's tier values are printed as static text around its own circumference, a permanent legend of three animal-head icons sits above the center circle, and the center circle itself shows an animal-head icon (not a color swatch) matching the last-landed symbol.
No sound-dependent gameplay information was identified; Sound and Music are togglable sliders in Settings, and all game state feedback is conveyed visually via the wheel graphic and text counters.

Bet Amount, Payout and Part Payout values are rendered in a relatively small font at 1280x800, off to the side of the large central wheel graphic, while the main Balance figure (top-left) is comparatively larger and bolder.

The sole spin control is a press-and-hold gesture ('Hold to Spin') rather than a single tap/click-and-release per round; no alternative single-press-per-spin control was found in this build, which may be harder for users with limited ability to sustain a button press.

Balance, Bet Amount, Payout and Part Payout are all rendered as on-screen text next to a clear label, not encoded only in fill length. However, the ring fill amount itself (how many of N sectors are lit) is conveyed only graphically, with no text equivalent (e.g. no 'Lion 6/7' label anywhere).

Bet/bet-level/coin/balance/win values and the paytable are always shown as legible text and numerals, not conveyed by colour alone; the mixed low-symbol payout row is labelled with the printed word ANY rather than relying on colour recognition. Settings toggles show state by knob position (left=off, right=on) in addition to colour fill. Residual risk: the three low-value knot symbols differ from each other only by cord colour (gold/red/green); their printed payout amount and paytable position, not the colour, are the reliable way to tell them apart.

No information observed is conveyed by sound alone; bet, balance, win amount, jackpot ticker values and bet limits are always shown as on-screen text. Settings expose separate Sound - Ambient and Sound - Effects toggles (both on by default) plus a master volume control described on the Help screen; round outcomes never depend on hearing anything.

The reel window is a curved, glossy red 3D cylindrical drum rather than flat square cells, with symbols floating on the continuous curved surface instead of being separated by grid lines — a physical-slot-machine look that may be harder to parse than a flat grid. The Help overlay uses white body text on a near-black background (high contrast); a winning line's own payout is printed as a large gold numeral directly over the highlighted line, in addition to the smaller total in the service strip.

All interactive controls are large circular or pill-shaped targets. The space bar both starts and stops a spin, reducing the need for precise pointer clicks. BET MAX and AUTO PLAY, with a configurable spin count and optional stop conditions, reduce the number of manual actions needed to reach a desired bet or play many rounds unattended.

Bottom control bar order is stable left to right: info (i), BET, BET LEVEL stepper, BET MAX, SPIN (large centre button), AUTO PLAY, COIN stepper, BALANCE; a second footer strip below shows game name/settings gear, balance, bet/win, clock, turbo, fullscreen, sound and the HABANERO wordmark. The Help overlay is a single linear scrolling document with labelled section headers (Game Interface, Auto Play, Game Menu, Disconnection Policy, Jackpots, Return To Player); the paytable/rules booklet is a fixed 6-page sequence navigable with only previous/home/next controls.

Lucky Seven (red numeral 7) vs Watermelon (red flesh, green rind): distinguished by shape — numeral vs fruit slice. Lemon (bright yellow, oval) vs 7 (red numeral): shape differentiates fully. Card symbols K (bright green letter), Q (purple/magenta letter), A (orange-red letter): letter label provides full differentiation independent of color.

Winning symbol highlight uses both luminance brightness increase and color — luminance-based contrast is accessible across most colorblind types. Settings toggles: ON state is green, OFF is grey; positional redundancy (pill position left=off, right=on) partially mitigates color dependency.

Scatter symbol carries 'SCATTER' text label — fully accessible by text alone. Golden Frog identified by distinctive frog shape, not color alone. Volatility indicator is count-based (5 filled lightning bolts) — accessible by counting.

Game fully playable without sound. All win events have visual text confirmation: WIN $X.XX banner, NICE! overlay with dollar amount, LINE X PAYS $X.XX sub-text. Audio provides atmosphere only — no audio-exclusive game information.

Golden Frog: gleaming gold body, large round eyes, seated on gold coins — distinct silhouette. Scatter: bright cyan/ice-blue diamond gem with 'SCATTER' text. Lucky Seven: bold crimson-red numeral with white outline. Watermelon: red flesh, black seeds, dark green rind. Lemon: bright yellow oval with green stem leaf.

SPIN button is large circular target (~80px). Autoplay available up to 100 spins with SKIP SCREENS option. Bet adjustment requires repeated +/- button taps; no direct numpad input observed. Paytable navigation requires drag-scroll gesture per rules text.

SCATTER carries text label directly on symbol. Card symbols K, Q, A identified by single letter. Numeral 7 readable as character. Golden Frog, Lemon, Watermelon have no text labels — require alt-text implementation. Game state banners are text-based: 'PLACE YOUR BETS!', 'WIN $X.XX', 'GAME PAYS $X.XX', 'LINE X PAYS $X.XX', 'NICE! $X.XX'. Balance/bet displayed as 'CREDIT $X BET $X' text.

Wild is identified by character art (lab coat, goggles, green beaker), not by a color-coded frame; Scatter is the only round glowing-orb icon among otherwise rectangular icons; base game and free games are told apart by a background shape/gradient change (purple lab vs pink/teal bubble scene), not color alone
Control icons (spin/stop/skip/replay) are distinguished by glyph shape on solid colored circles, not hue alone
The in-game Help screen renders plain white text on black with orange highlighted numbers, always embedded in a full sentence rather than conveyed by color alone
Space bar starts a spin and can also stop the reels mid-spin, in addition to the on-screen SPIN button
The three bonus moons are blue, red and yellow, but the Bonus Feature intro prints a text label beside each: +1 to all prizes, absorb all prizes, doubles 3 prizes.
Moon charge is shown by a row of five dots under each moon (filled versus dark) as well as by colour.
Multipliers and prizes are printed as numbers (x20, 3x, 64x), not only by colour.
Royal letters A, K, Q, J are dusty red-orange, pink-purple, muted green and muted blue-teal, and also differ in letter shape.
Wild and Scatter carry the words WILD and SCATTER on the artwork; Wild is orange lettering on grey-brown werewolf, Scatter is pink lettering on a dark-brown werewolf before an orange moon.
